articles.title: Muse Charm: Meta surpreende e lança "Tamagotchi de IA" • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Muse Charm: Meta surpreende e lança “Tamagotchi de IA”
Chaveiro tem tela com avatar personalizável e sensor de impressão digital.
A Meta aproveitou o aparente sucesso do seu novo agente de IA e apresentou o Muse Charm, um pequeno dispositivo em formato de chaveiro com inteligência artificial. Ele serve para conversar com o agente pessoal Muse sem usar o celular e lembra os famosos Tamagotchis.
O dispositivo foi revelado por Mark Zuckerberg no encerramento da apresentação Meta Connect 2026, nesta quarta-feira (23/09). A Meta ainda não informou o preço do produto nem detalhou em quais países ele será vendido.
  Ver no Threads
A ideia do Muse Charm é ser um acionador físico, compacto e portátil do agente de IA da Meta. O usuário poderá tocar no sensor de impressão digital na lateral do aparelho e já começar a falar com o Muse.
Isso sem precisar desbloquear o smartphone ou abrir um app de apoio — ao menos é o que afirmou Zuckerberg, durante a demonstração. O Muse Charm também é uma alternativa para quem não estiver usando os óculos inteligentes da Meta.
Sem os óculos, esse será “o jeito mais rápido de falar com o Muse e mostrar o que está acontece ao seu redor”. Zuckerberg não entrou em detalhes sobre essa última parte, mas as imagens aproximadas mostram o que parece ser uma câmera na parte superior do dispositivo.
O pequeno display mostra o avatar Jolly, que interage com o usuário. A experiência combina voz em tempo real e animações na tela, aproximando o produto da lógica dos antigos Tamagotchi, inclusive na personalização do avatar.
Apesar de já ter sido apresentado publicamente, o Muse Charm ainda não está pronto para chegar às lojas. Segundo Zuckerberg, a equipe precisa finalizar a disposição dos componentes internos antes do início da produção. A previsão da Meta é colocar o aparelho no mercado em dezembro, a tempo das compras de fim de ano.
O anúncio do “chaveiro” inteligente faz parte de uma expansão maior do agente de IA dentro do ecossistema da Meta. No Connect, a empresa também apresentou o Muse Realtime Avatar, que dá ao agente uma representação visual para conversas em tempo real, e confirmou a chegada do agente aos óculos inteligentes da companhia.
Nos óculos, o Muse poderá ser acionado por voz e usar a câmera para entender aquilo que o usuário está olhando. A Meta citou tarefas como identificar produtos, ajudar em exercícios, registrar refeições e marcar compromissos.

articles.title: Bentley's first EV is a 375-mile luxury SUV that hits 60 mph in 2.8 seconds
articles.text:
First look: Following months of fervent speculation and multiple official previews, Bentley has finally revealed the Torcal, its first fully electric vehicle. It is the fourth model line in Bentley's current portfolio, joining the Flying Spur luxury sedan, Continental GT/GTC coupe and convertible, and Bentayga SUV.
Like other modern Bentleys, the Torcal is also named after a natural wonder. Bentley says the name comes from El Torcal de Antequera, a natural reserve in the Sierra del Torcal mountains of Andalusia, Spain, known for its striking limestone rock formations, high cliffs, and deep caves.
Designed and engineered at Bentley's headquarters in Crewe in northwest England, the Torcal SUV is based on the Porsche Cayenne Electric's 800-volt PPE platform. However, while the Cayenne EV delivers around 1,156 hp and 1,106 lb-ft of torque in its flagship Turbo variant, the Torcal focuses more on luxury and offers relatively restrained performance.
The Torcal is available in two trims: a base Core model and a sportier S variant. Both feature a 113.2 kWh battery that Bentley claims delivers an estimated range of up to 375 miles on the WLTP cycle, or around 320 miles under EPA testing. The battery supports up to 400 kW of DC fast charging, which can charge it from 10% to 80% in just 16 minutes or add 100 miles of range in just seven minutes.
In terms of performance, both the Core and S trims feature the same dual-motor permanent-magnet synchronous powertrain with an all-wheel-drive layout. In the flagship Torcal S, the setup delivers up to 888 PS (876 hp) of power and 1,350 Nm (996 lb-ft) of torque, while the Core variant delivers 821 PS (810 hp) and 1,194 Nm (852 lb-ft) of torque.
Bentley claims 0-60 mph acceleration times of 3.3 seconds for the Torcal Core and 2.8 seconds for the Torcal S. The former can reach a top speed of 155 mph, while the latter can reach up to 162 mph. It is worth noting that the Torcal S was tested with Launch Control enabled, while the Core does not offer the feature.
The Torcal Core starts at £165,000 in the UK and $230,000 in the US, while the Torcal S starts at a cool £200,000/$270,000. Bentley will start accepting pre-orders next month, but production is not scheduled to begin until Q2 2027. Alongside the US and UK, the Torcal has been confirmed to launch in Germany, Switzerland, Canada, China, India, and other major markets.

articles.title: GTA 6 : Rockstar lance le coffret collector ultime à 400 euros (sans le jeu à l'intérieur)
articles.text:
Le produit avait d’abord fuité ce jeudi matin. Des fans avaient repéré dans les données du Rockstar Store une liste de 55 produits dérivés, avec cette « Vice City Collection » perdue entre des t-shirts et un tas de goodies, comme l’a rapporté Insider Gaming.
La fiche indiquait un colis lourd, limité à un exemplaire par personne, de quoi faire espérer une vraie édition du jeu. Rockstar l’a officialisé dans la journée et le moins que l’on puisse dire c’est que le contenu est assez décevant.
Que contient le coffret à 400 € ?
Sur le papier, c’est l’édition collector que les fans réclament depuis l’ouverture des précommandes, fin juin. Seulement voilà, la boîte baptisée « Grand Theft Auto VI : The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection » ne contient ni disque ni code de téléchargement. Pour jouer, il faudra payer le jeu en plus, à 79,99 € en édition standard. Le coffret coûte donc à lui seul cinq fois le prix du jeu qu’il accompagne.
Tout tourne autour de Macca the Gator, un alligator mascotte d’une émission de télé fictive de Leonida, l’État inspiré de la Floride où se déroule GTA 6. D’après la fiche du Rockstar Store, la boîte mesure 48 x 33 x 30 cm et n’a pas droit à la livraison gratuite.
On y trouve :
- une figurine de Macca the Gator d’environ 15 cm, avec un compartiment caché ;
- des lunettes de soleil Oakley Frogskins ;
- une casquette New Era ;
- un sac bandoulière Leonida Keys ;
- un miroir magnétique ;
- une cuillère à cocktail ;
- un porte-clés en forme de lame de rasoir ;
- un verre à shot ;
- des pin’s dans une boîte en métal ;
- des autocollants ;
- et un poster recto verso.
Pour le jeu lui-même, rien ne change. Rockstar ne vend toujours que deux éditions, la standard à 79,99 € et l’Ultimate à 99,99 €, cette dernière uniquement en numérique. Une version en boîte, qui on le rappelle, ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement, un choix que Strauss Zelnick, CEO de Take-Two, maison mère de Rockstar, a défendu en août.
Le collector de GTA V coûtait 130 €, jeu compris
En 2013, on pouvait acheter l’Édition Collector de GTA V pour 129,99 €. Elle comprenait déjà une casquette New Era, un sac de sécurité avec sa clé, un boîtier métallique, une carte de Los Santos et plusieurs bonus en jeu. Et surtout, l’exemplaire de GTA V était dans la boîte. Une précision qui semblait assez superflue à l’époque.
Pourtant, le procédé n’est pas nouveau chez Rockstar. En 2018, le studio vendait déjà une « Collector’s Box » pour Red Dead Redemption 2 : une boîte métallique à cadenas, une pièce et quelques babioles, sans le jeu, pour environ 100 €. Huit ans plus tard, le prix a été multiplié par quatre.
Ce nouveau coffret s’ajoute à la liste de produits dérivés : les manettes DualSense aux couleurs de GTA 6 à 84,99 € pièce ou encore l’album officiel en CD et en vinyle dans une période marketing déjà bien entamée par le studio.

articles.title: Leading semiconductor analyst says AMD should be investigated for 'treason' over availability of restricted chips in China, AMD blames diversion of export-controlled RFSoC — $36,000 radar silicon allegedly quoted at $1,000 for crowdfunding project
articles.text:
Leading semiconductor analyst says AMD should be investigated for 'treason' over availability of restricted chips in China, AMD blames diversion of export-controlled RFSoC — $36,000 radar silicon allegedly quoted at $1,000 for crowdfunding project
Export-restricted hardware with 40 – 52 weeks lead times readily available in China (almost).
Dylan Patel, the head of SemiAnalysis, a top semiconductor analysis company, has discovered that China-based Puzhi Electronic Technology is crowdfunding development of a system that is based on AMD's Zync UltraScale+ XCZU47DR RFSoC, which is a U.S. export-controlled dual-use component. Dylan Patel called on the government to investigate AMD for treason, whereas, in a statement to Tom's Hardware, AMD denied selling or shipping the chips directly into the restricted region and said it investigates suspected cases of illegal diversion.
"AMD found a business opportunity in dumping U.S. military chips for 1/4 of the cost in China," Patel wrote in an X post. "U.S. list price is $36K for this chip, with $4K – 5K to U.S. companies at volume, but it is getting quoted $1K in China to crowdfunding campaigns. AMD needs to be investigated for treason. It is not just export violations, but it is literally selling military end use components to an adversary for less than your home country."
AMD denies any wrongdoing and says it investigates suspected diversion cases to determine whether any violation of law occurred, although it did not explicitly confirm that it had opened an investigation into this particular case.
"AMD is committed to full compliance with all U.S. and global export regulations and has a clear policy requiring our distributors, resellers, and customers to do the same," a spokesperson for AMD told Tom's Hardware. "Any shipment into restricted regions is a direct violation of our policy. This recent instance is unrelated to any direct AMD sales or shipments. We investigate all suspected diversion cases and if we find any violation of law, we will report it to relevant authorities and cease all business with the company."
AMD told Patel the same, according to another X post he made as a follow-up on the matter.
AMD's Zynq UltraScale+ XCZU47DR RFSoCs pack four general-purpose Arm cores, two Cortex-R5F real-time cores, an FPGA with 930,000 gates, DSP engines with 4,272 DSP slices, as well as eight 14-bit analog-to-digital converters (ADC) capable of up to 5 GSPS and eight 14-bit digital-to-analog converters (DAC) operating at up to 9.85 GSPS to receive, process, and generate RF signals in real time without relying on separate data converters. Devices based on Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoCs are used for software-defined radios, radar and phased-array systems, wireless and satellite communications, electronic test equipment, and other applications that require high-bandwidth, low-latency signal processing. Puzhi Electric officially positions its upcoming systems based on the Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoCs for 'professional engineers' and 'advanced researchers in universities,' though such systems can be used for completely different applications.
AMD's Zynq UltraScale+ XC-series RFSoCs are designed for commercial and industrial applications, but AMD also offers separate XQ-series defense-grade RFSoCs for aerospace and defense applications, although there the XCZU47DR does not have a direct XQZU47DR counterpart. Yet, the closely related ZU48DR is available in both XC and XQ versions. The latter adds defense-oriented qualification, ruggedization, and support rather than fundamentally different processing capabilities.
Therefore, while the XCZU47DR is technically aimed at civil, commercial, and industrial applications, the chip is a dual-use component featuring a 3A001.a.14 ECCN classification under the U.S. Commerce Control List (CCL) and therefore its exporting, re-exporting, or transferring normally requires a BIS export license to non-allied destinations (e.g., China) on anti-terrorist and national security concerns. This means that any shipment to China requires a license, but in practical reality, that license will almost certainly be denied. However, there is a license exception that allows shipping such items to commercial companies from the Group B countries, which means legitimate exports to dozens of states from where such goods could get to China illegally.
This might explain how Puzhi obtained its XCZU47DR devices, but it does not explain the enormous apparent difference between the prices available to Chinese and American buyers. The $1,000 figure, however, is Patel's reported price for the chip rather than a publicly advertised retail offer.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Xilinx, which AMD later acquired, introduced its 3rd Generation Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC family, including the XCZU47DR, in February 2019, and the devices reached production status in 2020, meaning that they have been on the market for almost six years now. Xilinx and then AMD have sold the unit to tens, if not hundreds, of companies in different countries, so determining the origin of the units that Puzhi has might be difficult.
It should be noted that lead times for XCZU47DR at various resellers like Avnet and DigiKey are 40 to 52 weeks, which indicates that the components are in high demand in the U.S. and Europe. Meanwhile, Puzhi claims it can ship its system based on the RFSoC on November 6, 2026.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Governance gaps that can undermine your AI ROI
articles.text:
Governance gaps that can undermine your AI ROI
Why AI spending outpaces measurable business value
Artificial intelligence has become a significant area of investment for UK businesses. More than £6 billion of new AI-related investment was announced during London Tech Week in June, while the UK remains home to the largest AI sector in Europe and the third largest globally.
From customer service and knowledge management to software development and internal operations, organizations are looking for places where AI tools can improve productivity, decision-making and business performance.
Principal Industry Advisor at ShareGate and Microsoft MVP.
But as investment accelerates, another gap is becoming harder to ignore: organizations are often scaling AI faster than their ability to measure, govern and explain its value. That matters when CIOs and CFOs are increasingly being asked not simply whether AI is being adopted, but what the organization is getting in return.
As businesses move from individual copilots towards agents embedded across workflows, the economics become more complicated. A user making a single prompt is relatively easy to understand. An agent may make multiple model calls, retrieve information, invoke tools and take actions to complete one task.
Depending on the platform and pricing model, that can introduce additional consumption, infrastructure and oversight costs. CIOs therefore need to understand not only where AI has been deployed, but what it is doing, what it costs and whether the outcome justifies that cost.
The not-so-hidden cost of AI
AI investment is increasingly being scrutinized in the same way as any other major technology investment. The difficulty is that measuring its return can be unusually complex.
Usage may be distributed across departments, applications, models and workflows, while the benefits can range from time saved to improved quality, reduced risk or increased revenue. Without agreeing what success means first, organizations can end up measuring activity rather than value.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
That becomes difficult when organizations expand AI without first defining where it sits in the workflow, who owns the outcome, what success looks like and how costs will be measured. Spending can become fragmented across licenses, models, infrastructure, platforms and consumption-based services, with no single view of whether those investments are delivering value.
The scale of the challenge is becoming visible. Research commissioned by Emergn estimates that large UK businesses lose £67 billion annually across transformation and AI initiatives that fail to deliver. Separately, a Censuswide survey of 500 senior UK decision-makers found that just 31% of businesses already using AI reported a positive return on their investment.
Governance is part of that measurement challenge. A 2026 ShareGate survey of 851 IT leaders across seven countries found that cost visibility was the most commonly cited barrier to measuring AI ROI, identified by 51% of respondents, followed closely by governance complexity at 47%. The challenge isn't simply knowing what AI costs. It's connecting that cost to the use case it supports, the information AI interacts with and the outcome it creates.
Much of the AI debate to date has focused on model selection, skills and productivity. But as adoption spreads, another gap is becoming visible: confidence in governance does not always match what happens in practice.
The same study found that 93% of IT leaders believed their Microsoft 365 governance was ready to support AI responsibly, yet 29% reported that AI tools had surfaced sensitive internal data that should not have been accessible. Another 8% weren't sure whether it had happened at all.
Those gaps carry costs as well as risk. Duplicated tools, additional validation, rework, security investigations and time spent establishing whether an output can be trusted all create a hidden tax on AI adoption. For CIOs trying to demonstrate value, reducing that friction starts with making AI usage more visible, accountable and measurable.
How organizations can regain control
Good governance doesn’t begin and end at procurement. Knowing how many licenses have been purchased and where they have been assigned is useful, but regaining control requires a broader view: visibility into how AI is being used and what it costs, clear ownership of the outcomes, and a well-governed information environment for AI to work from.
Clear ownership matters just as much. As AI becomes embedded in business processes, responsibility can easily become fragmented across IT, security, business teams and individual employees. That makes some basic questions surprisingly difficult to answer: Who owns the outcome? Who monitors the cost? Who decides whether a use case should scale, change or stop?
Cost governance is only part of the picture. Organizations also need to improve the information environment in which AI operates. That means reducing redundant and outdated content, managing access appropriately and helping employees and AI systems find authoritative sources.
Cleaner, better-governed information does not guarantee a correct AI response, but it can reduce ambiguity and make reliable grounding easier. That can mean less time spent searching, validating and reworking outputs.
Employees have a role here as well. Clearly distinguishing drafts from approved material, keeping trackers and priorities current, recording decisions and maintaining authoritative sources all make organizational context easier for people and AI to interpret. Where organizations use AI meeting assistants or similar tools to capture context, those tools should be subject to the same privacy, retention and access controls as the information they create.
The question for leaders, then, is no longer simply whether AI is worth the investment. It is whether they have enough visibility and control to understand where AI is creating value, where it is creating cost and what they should do differently as a result. AI investment is likely to continue, but under different expectations.
Deployment alone is not evidence of value, and governance is becoming more than a risk-management exercise; it is increasingly part of the business case. Leaders need to understand what AI costs, who is accountable for its outcomes, whether the information supporting it can be trusted and what measurable benefit it creates.
The organizations best positioned to scale will not necessarily be those deploying the most AI, but those that can explain what it is doing, understand what it costs and make informed decisions about where it belongs.

articles.title: How Meta says it's addressing privacy concerns amid new smart glasses lineup
articles.text:
It’s no secret that Meta has privacy issues.
After all, there’s been a lot of apprehension surrounding the company’s ever-growing lineup of smart glasses. In particular, these products have sometimes been called “pervert glasses” due to being used to harass people and, according to a recent lawsuit, even allegedly capture and share intimate images without consent.
Naturally, this was a big topic of discussion during a media roundtable at Meta’s Menlo Park, California, headquarters. Speaking with Ming Hua, VP of wearable devices, MobileSyrup and several other international outlets had some questions about Meta’s continued approach to addressing privacy concerns with its products.
“Privacy is always front and centre when we design [wearables],” said Hua. “Actually, from the first generation, we’ve had a privacy LED, where it’s signalling to people when you are capturing. So that continues to be very core.”
However, we’ve seen instances where people have covered up the LED to remove that layer of transparency, and a quick Google search will show countless products that are specifically designed to do just that. To address this, Hua points out, Meta recently closed a loophole that allowed cameras to cover the light after recording had begun without issue.
“We’ll continue to make sure that the algorithm is very robust, and also really bring awareness about how things work,” she added, referring to a recent marketing campaign that promotes the glasses’ privacy features.
She also cited a new feature that was announced at Connect 2026: private processing. This technology, which is already used to encrypt WhatsApp chats, will allow glasses to keep data used by AI features secure and inaccessible even from Meta. During the Connect 2026 keynote, CEO Mark Zuckerberg confirmed that private processing will be rolled out “soon” to features like Live Translations before expanding to “more and more” features.
When asked about how the discussion surrounding “pervert glasses” influences Meta’s approach to privacy, Hua stressed that moderation in addition to all of the aforementioned initiatives, content moderation is a big focus for Meta.
“We’re also taking actions to take down the content that’s not good,” she said. “[We] take down the accounts if they continuously violate the platform policy, and also [are] blocking the search terms. We also are taking down content that teach people how to tamper with glasses.”
Time will tell what else Meta may do to improve privacy. In the meantime, it should be noted that the company just unveiled a new pair of audio-only glasses that remove the camera entirely.

articles.title: After IonQ Buyout, SkyWater Reiterates Role as Quantum Foundry - EE Times
articles.text:
After quantum computing company IonQ acquired SkyWater in July this year, the subsidiary said it is pledging to treat its quantum chip customers equally, including parent IonQ.
“IonQ is treated as a customer of the foundry, just like anyone else,” SkyWater’s new SVP of quantum technologies Mihir Bhaskar told EE Times. “For all quantum customers SkyWater serves, their data and information remain strictly with the dedicated SkyWater team manufacturing their devices.”
Bhaskar, a quantum technologist for 15 years, founded Lightsynq, specializing in photonic interconnects and quantum memory, in 2024. IonQ acquired the company in 2025.
“Since joining IonQ, I’ve helped lead technology strategy, including assisting with the acquisition of SkyWater,” Bhaskar said. “With SkyWater now in place, the most exciting role for me is leading the SkyWater Quantum Solutions business unit to support all our quantum customers.”
SkyWater has nine “major” quantum customers, according to Bhaskar. Startup competitor Anderon has parent IBM as its primary customer and is looking for more.
“Priority number one for any business—especially in the foundry space—is protecting customer intellectual property,” Bhaskar said. “If your customers don’t trust you, you can’t do business. It is critical in the foundry business because customers bring highly sensitive IP and designs, trusting us to manufacture them.”
SkyWater has been making quantum chips for about 10 years. Its customers include IonQ, PsiQuantum, Qolab, and QuamCore.
Qolab and QuamCore are building what Bhaskar described as “potentially disruptive” superconducting technologies that may eliminate the well-known “chandelier” design from quantum computers.
“A major challenge in scaling superconducting qubit systems used by players like IBM, Google, and Rigetti is wiring and controlling larger numbers of qubits without creating a massive, tangled mess of cables,” Bhaskar said. “SkyWater is building a platform with Quadcore to solve these high-density integration and routing challenges.”
Modalities
The “modalities”, or techniques, that quantum chip companies use to make qubits include trapped ions, quantum dots, silicon vacancies in diamond, photonics, and superconducting.
Bhaskar said every one of those modalities ultimately relies on either superconducting or photonic methods to move quantum information.
“We support all major modalities,” Bhaskar said. “That might sound impossible for a single foundry, but fundamentally, there are only two ways to transport quantum information across a chip or system.”
SkyWater offers its SC250 (superconducting) and SP90 (photonics) platforms together with its technology-as-a-service model that provides early-stage process customization to prove manufacturability.
“While we offer baseline process design kit platforms [PDKs], our core business model accommodates custom process development within a volume manufacturing environment,” Bhaskar said. “We develop new processes outside standard PDKs to make breakthrough innovations manufacturable for the first time.”
Anderon
IBM established Anderon with the help of the U.S. government in May this year as the “world’s first” pure-play quantum chip foundry. The U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Anderon $1 billion under the CHIPS Act early in September to scale production. IBM is Anderon’s main customer.
Specific to the U.S., additional domestic capacity can help address supply chain constraints, provide manufacturing redundancy, and give quantum companies more options as they move from research prototypes toward production, Heather West, IDC’s quantum research lead, told EE Times.
Anderon offers customers wafers supporting superconducting qubit arrays, quantum input/output signaling, and readout signal chain components, new CEO Mukesh Khare told EE Times. The company plans to expand to other quantum modalities, such as spin qubits, he said.
“Fantastic step”
U.S. government investment in domestic quantum semiconductor manufacturing is a “fantastic step” for the entire ecosystem, Bhaskar said.
“Competitors like Anderon are building new 300-mm facilities for future capability,” Bhaskar noted.
SkyWater supplies its quantum customers from two 200-mm facilities in Minnesota and Florida as well as a 300-mm advanced packaging facility in Florida for chiplet integration and new materials.
“SkyWater is already shipping quantum wafers today and has been doing so for the last decade,” Bhaskar noted. “Our active capacity has powered the last several generations of quantum innovation and will continue to power the next. While others are working toward becoming a quantum foundry in the future, SkyWater is already the operational quantum foundry today.”

articles.title: ESA et Mistral unissent leurs forces pour accélérer l’IA en Europe
articles.text:
L'Agence spatiale européenne et Mistral ont signé une lettre d'intention pour explorer ensemble de nouveaux usages de l'intelligence artificielle dans l'ingénierie spatiale et l'observation de la Terre. Les deux parties veulent aussi encadrer le déploiement de ces technologies sur une infrastructure européenne.
Josef Aschbacher, directeur général de l'ESA, et Arthur Mensch, PDG de Mistral, ont signé cet accord qui prolonge une collaboration déjà en place entre les deux organisations. Soulignons qu'une lettre d'intention n'engage à rien de concret, mais elle pose un cadre de travail avant d'éventuels projets.
Trois chantiers pour faire entrer l'IA de Mistral dans l'ingénierie spatiale
L'accord couvre trois domaines. Le premier réunit l'observation de la Terre et l'ingénierie. Il s'agit de croiser les données recueillies par les satellites (climat, reliefs, activité humaine) avec les modèles de Mistral. Le deuxième vise à développer des capacités d'IA propres au secteur spatial. Le troisième porte sur la formation et le partage de compétences entre les équipes des deux organisations. Pour Josef Aschbacher, l'IA devient une capacité déterminante pour l'avenir du spatial, un domaine où l'ESA mène déjà des projets opérationnels et de recherche.
Dans les grandes lignes, l'IA doit surtout faciliter l'accès à des connaissances techniques, automatiser des tâches répétitives et appuyer des décisions d'ingénierie, sans se substituer aux humains qui les prennent. Ce travail s'appuie sur deux outils déjà en service. Orbit est un assistant IA sécurisé qui aide au quotidien les équipes d'ingénierie de l'ESA. EVE (Earth Virtual Expert), conçu par le Φ-lab de l'agence avec des partenaires européens, sert à interroger et interpréter les données d'observation de la Terre.
L'ESA et Mistral veulent aussi étudier comment déployer ces outils sur une infrastructure européenne, avec des garanties de sécurité, de résilience, de traçabilité et d'auditabilité, et une protection des données sensibles. Concrètement, la traçabilité permet de déterminer comment une IA est arrivée à un résultat, et l'auditabilité, de faire vérifier son fonctionnement par un tiers. Pour l'ESA, il s'agit surtout de garder la main sur l'infrastructure et les données, plutôt que de dépendre de fournisseurs extra-européens.
Arthur Mensch dit vouloir transformer les données de l'ESA en services utiles pour l'industrie spatiale, avec la technologie de Mistral, présentée par l'entreprise comme pouvant s'adapter à différents besoins. Mistral a multiplié ce genre d'accords ces derniers mois avec des acteurs français et européens. Nous rapportions fin mai un partenariat similaire avec Airbus, portant notamment sur l'aviation commerciale, la défense et l'espace. Avec l'ESA, la coopération reste pour l'instant au stade de l'exploration, aucun calendrier ni budget n'a été communiqué.

articles.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro und 18 Pro Max: iPhone-Konkurrent kommt mit Blickschutz und Qualcomms neuen Superchips
articles.text:
Xiaomi 18 Pro und 18 Pro Max: iPhone-Konkurrent kommt mit Blickschutz und Qualcomms neuen Superchips
Xiaomi erweitert seine Smartphone-Reihe: Die Modelle 18 Pro und 18 Pro Max sind da. Beide Geräte gehören zu den ersten angekündigten Geräten mit Qualcomms neuen High-End-Prozessoren Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 und Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Im Xiaomi 18 Pro steckt der Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, im größeren 18 Pro Max der Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Xiaomi kombiniert die Chips mit älterem LPDDR5X-Arbeitsspeicher und UFS-4.1-Flashspeicher. Die Prozessoren würden zwar auch die neueren Standards LPDDR6 und UFS 5.0 unterstützen – davon macht Xiaomi aber keinen Gebrauch.
Zwei Kameras mit 200 Megapixeln
Bei den Kameras ähneln sich beide Modelle stark. Laut Xiaomi kommt ein Leica-Summilux-System mit drei Kameras auf der Rückseite zum Einsatz. Die Hauptkamera löst mit 200 Megapixeln auf, nutzt einen Light-Fusion-960L-Sensor, eine Blende von f/1,67 und einen optischen Bildstabilisator. Die äquivalente Brennweite liegt bei 23 Millimetern. Dazu kommt ein Teleobjektiv, das ebenfalls 200 Megapixel liefert. Es arbeitet mit Blende f/2,4, optischer Bildstabilisierung und einem Samsung-HP5-Sensor, die äquivalente Brennweite beträgt 75 Millimeter. Makroaufnahmen sollen laut Hersteller ab zwölf Zentimetern Abstand möglich sein.
Die Ultraweitwinkelkamera kommt auf 50 Megapixel, ein Sichtfeld von 102 Grad und eine Brennweite von 17 Millimetern. Für Selfies gibt es eine 50-Megapixel-Kamera mit Blende f/2,2 und 90 Grad Sichtfeld. Beim 18 Pro Max unterstützt die Hauptkamera zusätzlich die LOFIC-HDR-Technik, die Aufnahmen mit sehr hellen und sehr dunklen Bereichen verbessern soll.
Display mit Blickschutz
Das Xiaomi 18 Pro hat ein 6,4 Zoll großes LTPO-Display mit 2436 × 1120 Pixeln. Beim 18 Pro Max misst der Bildschirm 6,9 Zoll und löst mit 2624 × 1208 Pixeln auf. Beide Panels passen ihre Bildwiederholrate dynamisch zwischen 1 und 120 Hertz an – das spart Strom. Die Spitzenhelligkeit gibt Xiaomi mit 4000 cd/m² an. Dazu nennt der Hersteller den großen Farbraum BT.2020 und DC-Dimming, eine augenschonende Helligkeitsregelung.
Wie das Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra bieten die neuen Xiaomis ein sogenanntes Privacy Display. Ist die Funktion aktiv, lässt sich der Bildschirm von der Seite kaum noch einsehen. Xiaomi erreicht das wie Samsung über eine veränderte Pixelmatrix. Nutzerinnen und Nutzer können den Blickschutz auch nur für einzelne Apps oder für Benachrichtigungen einschalten statt für den ganzen Bildschirm. Deutlich unterscheiden sich die Akkus: Das Xiaomi 18 Pro bekommt einen Silizium-Kohlenstoff-Akku mit typisch 7000 mAh, das 18 Pro Max sogar 8500 mAh. Diese Technik erlaubt mehr Kapazität bei gleichem Volumen. Beide Geräte laden per Kabel mit bis zu 100 Watt und drahtlos mit bis zu 50 Watt. Auf der Rückseite bei den Kameras gibt es einen kleinen Extrabildschirm, der bei Selfies hilft, aber auch mit KI-Bildern verschönert werden kann.
Preise und Verfügbarkeit
Für Deutschland nennt Xiaomi bislang weder Termin noch Preise. In China sind die Smartphones seit dem 23. September erhältlich: Das 18 Pro kostet dort ab 5999 Yuan, umgerechnet rund 780 Euro, das 18 Pro Max ab 6999 Yuan, also etwa 910 Euro – jeweils mit 12 GByte RAM und 256 GByte Speicher. Der globale Start soll noch in diesem Jahr folgen.

articles.title: Trop c'est trop ? Disney+ fait une nouvelle fois grimper ses prix aux États-Unis
articles.text:
Trop c'est trop ? Disney+ fait une nouvelle fois grimper ses prix aux États-Unis
La plateforme de streaming Disney+ continue une tradition annuelle bien désagréable pour ses abonnés en annonçant une nouvelle augmentation de ses tarifs outre-Atlantique.
Pour la quatrième fois en quatre ans, le service de streaming Disney+ a annoncé une augmentation de ses tarifs aux États-Unis. En 2025, le prix des abonnements avait connu une hausse outre-Atlantique quelques semaines avant sa réplique sur les offres de la plateforme en France, ce qui n'annonce donc rien de bon, cette fois encore, pour le porte-monnaie des abonnés français.
Disney+ : des tarifs d'abonnement toujours plus chers
Aux États-Unis, depuis le mercredi 23 septembre 2026, l'abonnement Premium à Disney+ passe de 18,99 $ à 21,49 $/mois, soit une hausse de 13 %. La formule Standard avec pub augmente quant à elle de 50 cents et passe de 11,99 $ à 12,49 $/mois.
À noter qu'aux États-Unis, Disney+ ne propose pas de formule Standard sans pub, comme c'est le cas en France.
L'an dernier, Disney+ a augmenté de 1 € les tarifs des abonnements Standard avec et sans pub en France, et de 2 € pour la formule Premium. Reste donc à savoir à combien s'élèvera cette nouvelle augmentation pour les abonnés français quand elle arrivera inévitablement dans l'Hexagone.
Comme toujours, le service de SVoD présente cette hausse tarifaire comme une nécessité pour continuer d’“investir dans les histoires que vous aimez” et proposer aux abonnés davantage de contenus de qualité.
Mais entre des fonctionnalités qui disparaissent, une publicité de plus en plus envahissante et, comme on le constate chaque mois, une quantité (et qualité) de nouveautés ajoutées au catalogue de Disney+ qui n'est pas toujours du même acabit que celle de la concurrence chez Netflix ou Prime Video, combien de temps la plateforme pourra-t-elle justifier ces augmentations avant que les abonnés ne finissent par décider que trop, c'est trop ?

articles.title: SpaceX has stopped taking Falcon 9 bookings past 2028, betting everything on Starship
articles.text:
Looking ahead: SpaceX appears to be preparing for a future without Falcon 9, even though the rocket remains one of the most important launch systems in service. The company is reportedly no longer accepting Falcon 9 launch reservations beyond 2028. That suggests a plan to shift customers to Starship, the much larger rocket SpaceX is developing for high-volume satellite launches, deep-space missions, and NASA's lunar program.
Meanwhile, Falcon 9 is still doing much of the work in the commercial launch market. In 2025, it launched 165 times, successfully delivered every payload to orbit, and had one unsuccessful booster recovery. The rocket accounted for nearly half of all launches worldwide.
Falcon 9 changed the economics of launch through reusable boosters and a rapid launch cadence. It also made rideshare missions more common, allowing several satellite companies to place spacecraft on the same launch. That has been especially important for startups and smaller operators that cannot afford a dedicated mission.
If SpaceX stops offering Falcon 9 after 2028, those customers will need other options. Other launch providers could pick up some of the demand, but none currently launches at Falcon 9's pace. The industry has already raised concerns about a shortage of rockets and launch capacity as demand for satellite deployments grows.
Musk has said SpaceX will shift its engineering and manufacturing resources away from Falcon and toward Starship once the newer vehicle is flying often enough to justify the move. He said the company would make the shift only after Starship can fly dependably several times a week. The goal would then be to increase Starship's flight rate to several launches a day, eventually allowing SpaceX to phase down Falcon operations.
 – Elon Musk (@elonmusk) August 22, 2026
That leaves an obvious question: Can Starship meet that standard by 2028?
The company is treating Starship as the vehicle that can eventually replace Falcon 9 and handle missions that Falcon cannot. Starship is designed to carry much larger payloads and eventually fly missions to the Moon and beyond. But the system has not yet reached orbit. Its newest prototype began flying this year, and its first orbital attempt is scheduled for Sept. 28.
Falcon 9 also performs missions that Starship cannot simply take over. It currently carries cargo and astronauts to the International Space Station for NASA. Starship's upper stage is too large to dock with the station, so retiring Falcon 9 could create a problem if the ISS operates beyond 2028. The station may receive an extension through 2032.
That could leave NASA relying more heavily on Russia's Soyuz spacecraft or Boeing's Starliner, if Starliner resolves the issues that have limited its use. Neither would be a direct replacement for Falcon 9's current role.
NASA's Artemis program may help explain why 2028 has become such an important date for SpaceX. The agency's plan calls for astronauts to launch aboard Orion on the Space Launch System. A separate Starship vehicle would be refueled in orbit through 15 launches, travel to lunar orbit, and take two astronauts to the Moon's surface.
That lunar landing is scheduled for 2028. SpaceX needs Starship to be ready if it is to meet that commitment. NASA has also reopened the lunar-lander competition, with Blue Origin as the only other candidate mentioned in the provided material.
SpaceX could change course and continue Falcon 9 flights longer than planned. For now, though, its booking policy suggests that the company is betting Starship will be ready to take over within two years.

articles.title: Galaxy S25 FE usa câmeras do S26 FE e tem 43% de desconto no Magalu • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy S25 FE usa câmeras do S26 FE e tem 43% de desconto no Magalu
Galaxy S25 FE (256 GB) conta com mesmo kit de câmeras do novo S26 FE; celular premium da Samsung sai 43% mais barato do que o preço original no Pix com cupom
O Galaxy S25 FE de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 3.299 no Pix com cupom LU300 no Magazine Luiza. O celular acessível da Samsung quase igual ao novo S26 FE, com destaque para as câmeras, recebe desconto de 43% sobre o preço original de R$ 5.799.
O Galaxy S25 FE é quase idêntico ao novo S26 FE, com apenas o processador sendo diferente entre eles: o modelo de 2025 possui um chip Exynos 2400 de 4 nanômetros, enquanto o mais recente traz um Exynos 2500 de 3 nm. Ambos possuem 8 GB de RAM e 256 GB de espaço interno.
As câmeras possuem a mesma configuração: sensor wide de 50 MP com OIS, ultrawide de 12 MP e telefoto de 8 MP com zoom óptico de 3x para aproximações; o kit filma em 8K. Já a frontal de 12 MP grava em 4K a 60 fps. Porém, o sucessor traz novos recursos como o My FanCam e Super Steady.
Sua tela LTPO AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,7″ possui taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de 1.900 nits, sendo capaz de reproduzir imagens com cores excelentes e alta fluidez nas transições em apps e games, além de contar com visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar.
O corpo de alumínio do S25 FE é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Gorilla Glass Victus+, resistente contra pancadas e arranhões. A certificação IP68 adiciona proteção extra em cenários como ambientes com muita poeira e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.900 mAh resiste até 28 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 45 W via USB-C e de 15 W sem fio garante energia suficiente para um dia inteiro, ideal para usuários com agendas corridas.
O Galaxy S25 FE de 256 GB (R$ 3.299 no Pix com cupom LU300) roda Android 16 e deve receber sete atualizações do sistema operacional. O celular da Samsung conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: This brutal Guy Ritchie quiz is so hard that I bet you can't score more than 70% — even MobLand and The Gentlemen fans will struggle
articles.text:
MobLand and The Gentlemen fans, listen up — test your knowledge with this brutal Guy Ritchie quiz I bet you won't get more than 70% on
It's as rough as a Ritchie shootout
Since 1998, we've been enjoying the feature films and TV shows of one Guy Ritchie. A man who arguably defined the British gangster sub-genre, cult hits like Snatch and Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels have stood the test of time.
Fast-forward to 2026, and streaming hits like Netflix's The Gentlemen and Paramount+'s MobLand are all anybody wants to talk about... and rightly so. And that's all without scratching the surface of the projects Ritchie has worked on in between.
But can you fill in the gaps? I've created the ultimate quiz for any and all Guy Ritchie fans, focusing on his feature-length movies and TV shows over the last three decades.
I didn't say it was going to be easy, though... so do your worst.
Of course, all of this is up to the time of writing — we already know that we've got plenty more Ritchie projects to look forward to.
Young Sherlock season 2, The Gentlemen season 3 and MobLand season 3 have all either been greenlit or are in development. There's a few more titles to add to this list... but that would be giving away the quiz questions.
Much like Ritchie-style gangster, I'm just not that nice.

articles.title: GMKtec Evo-X3 review: Strix Halo in a brand new suit
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
With its 128GB of fast DDR5-8000 RAM and AMD’s potent Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor there is a lot to like. The sleek and strong metallic Evo-X3 redesign is also welcome. However, the new price of this AI workstation is difficult to swallow.
Pros
- +Uses AMD’s powerful Ryzen AI Max+ 395
- +128GB of LPDDR5X-8000 memory on board
- +Can use up to 96GB as VRAM
- +USB4 and OCuLink ports are available
- +Excellent metal build quality
- +Quiet under load
Cons
- -Quite large and heavy for a mini PC
- -Sizable and heavy power brick
- -Just one USB4 port
- -Not enough video outputs
- -Price doubled since the previous gen Evo-X2 launched
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
GMKtec already has an AMD Strix Halo mini PC in its stables, in the form of the Evo-X2. Now, just six months later, we have another AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 processor-packing mini PC from GMKtec in the labs. The obvious difference is that the Evo-X3 has a brand new chassis and cooling design, it also comes with 128GB of LPDDR5X-8000 as standard. Those are welcome changes. Half a year later, though, the price has basically doubled as seemingly every electronics product with RAM and NAND chips inside has been affected by the ongoing component shortage.
The result is a desirable computer that will offer strong appeal to enthusiasts who want machines with a large pool of fast, unified RAM, in a competently revamped case. But you will have to have quite a compelling reason to part with the $3,799.99 our 128GB/2TB configuration costs in mid-2026.
Design of the GMKtec Evo-X3 AI Mini PC
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
GMKtec has thoroughly revamped its Evo-X family with the new X3. Gone is the short-but-stout design, where we saw a plastic inner case sandwiched by some brushed aluminum. Now GMKtec has gone almost entirely metal, with the exception of a textured and vented soft-touch green plastic cap. This towering new design, which is over 14-inches tall with the base attached, features a metal CNC chassis. That body feels very strong, the panels seem thick, and the base is made from a matching material. Where the mini PC meets the desk, there’s a pair of broad padded rubberized feet that you stick on after unpacking and fixing the metal base on the device.
While still in mini PC territory, the Evo-T3 is pushing it a bit at roughly 2.7 liters. Its flat base is about 4-inches wide, which helps it stay very stable on the desk. There are no side feet, which makes running it on its side inadvisible. Users will also have to hide away the large power brick if they are after the cleanest minimal workspace.
GMKtec Evo-X3 specifications
| Processor | AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16C/32T), up to 5.1 GHz , 85W | Row 0 - Cell 2 | 
| Graphics | AMD Radeon 8060S integrated GPU (40 RDNA 3.5 compute units, up to 2.9 GHz) | Row 1 - Cell 2 | 
| RAM | 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 RAM (soldered) | Row 2 - Cell 2 | 
| Storage | Dual M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD slots (2TB / 4TB options) | Row 3 - Cell 2 | 
| Physical Ports | Front: 2x USB‑A 3.2 Gen 1, 3.5 mm audio. Rear: 1x USB‑A 3.2 Gen 2, 1x USB4 Type‑C (PD 3.0 / DP-alt), 1x HDMI 2.1 , 1x OCuLink PCIe Gen 4 x4, 1x RJ‑45 2.5G LAN, DC‑IN barrel jack | Row 4 - Cell 2 | 
| Wireless | Wi‑Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 | Row 5 - Cell 2 | 
| Dimensions | Approx. 14.0 x 7.5 x 1.6-inches (≈ 2.7 L chassis) | Row 6 - Cell 2 | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Pro, Linux compatible | Row 7 - Cell 2 | 
| Price (as configured) | $3,799.99 (128GB RAM + 2TB SSD) Use code GMKX3DP3 to get 5% off the prices listed on Amazon | Row 8 - Cell 2 | 
Ports and Upgradeability
GMKtec keeps the front of its mini PC simple with just three ports and the power button. In the top third of the tower’s facade, there’s a central green power button with a white LED ring lit when it is powered up. The middle third of the front is left plain, but the lower third has one USB 3.2 Gen 1, one USB 2.0, and a 3.5mm audio combo jack. I wish there was a Type-C port on the front, preferably USB4 or better.
Around the back it has a good variety of ports, but I wouldn’t describe them as numerous. You will find a USB‑A 3.2 Gen 2 port, a USB4 Type‑C (PD 3.0 / DP-alt) port, an HDMI 2.1 port, an OCuLink PCIe Gen 4 ×4 port, an RJ‑45 2.5G LAN port, and a DC‑IN barrel jack. Ideally, I’d like to have a full size DP port, as well as a second USB4 port, plus more USB-A ports. If I were to use this as a daily driver I think I’d need to connect a fast USB docking solution for the oodles of peripherals I like to have ready and connected.
Wireless connectivity seems adequate enough, with an M.2 2230 card inside providing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4. I had no problems with either during the test period.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Access to the components inside the GMKtec Evo-X3 is straightforward, but takes time as there are eight Torx-6 screws securing the side panel in place. Once they were all unscrewed I needed to use a guitar pick and a bit of gravity to tilt the heavy panel off. Removing of the panel allowed access to the two M.2 PCIe 4.0 x4 slots, one of which was already populated with a Crucial P310 2TB M.2 NVMe SSD fitted with a slim heatsink. In the opposite corner of the chassis I saw an M.2 2230 socketed MediaTek wireless card. There are no other internal user upgrade or repair options as the 128GB of LPDDR5X-8000 RAM is soldered to the motherboard.
Test System Setup

| Geekom A9 Max 2026 | 10,230 | 414 | 262 | 26 | 19 | 29 | 24 | 17 | 14 | 2,960 | 12,500 | 43,990 | 
| Arctic Senza AI 370 | 17,750 | 627 | 613 | 54 | 47 | 56 | 46 | 32 | 27 | 2,830 | 15,110 | 39,760 |

| GMKtec Evo-X3 | 50,008 | 2,132 | 2,046 | 138 | 128 | 126 | 95 | 95 | 78 | 2,884 | 19,081 | 100,579 | 
Productivity Performance on the GMKtec Evo-X3
GMKtec describes the Evo-X3 as a machine that targets AI workloads, but first we ran through our standard mini PC benchmark comparison suite, which targets more general computing usage.
A brief glimpse at the tech specs of the X3 reveals that it has lots of modern fast CPU cores, supported by one of the best iGPUs, and plenty of RAM and storage. It should make light work of our productivity benchmarks, and indeed its 16C/32 core AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 CPU left its mini PC rivals eating dust, most strikingly in multi-threaded tests.
View Original
View Original

As we expected, the single core tests show the GMKtec Evo-X3 is a competent performer in the context of the competition in our charts. It isn’t the only Zen 5 machine in this race, so it doesn’t get a chance to dazzle yet.
Moving onto the multi-core tests is where the Ryzen AI Max+ 395’s 32 threads show their potential for real-world data crunching performance. For example, in Y-cruncher it completed its Pi compute in around 60 seconds. That’s twice as fast as its nearest competitor in our mini PC charts, the Beelink SER10 Max.
Rendering in Cinebench is also strong. In Cinebench 2026, the X3 scored roughly 7,300 points in multi-core. That’s over 40% faster than its nearest competitor, the Arctic Senza AI 370. Video transcoding performance is also in a new class, with the Evo-X3 crushing the competition, achieving around 24 frames per second.
For some added AI benchmarking stats, we did a few tests in Geekbench AI and LM Studio Bionic to weigh the GMKtec Evo-X3 against the Evo-T2. These are both machines with large unified memory pools by default and which the makers claim to be local LLM champs.
Using Geekbench AI with the ONNX framework and DirectML backend the Evo-X3 achieved a half precision score of ~37,100. On the Evo-T2 using the same options, a score of ~23,060 was achieved.
However, machines like the GMKtec Evo-X3 and T2 might be picked up by consumers to work with local LLMs considerably larger than most consumer GPUs can load. With this in mind, I ran LM Studio Bionic chat sessions powered by the new Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M model on both machines. To use this 27 billion parameter model as intended, a machine needs around 20GB of ‘VRAM’ of shared memory to avoid undesirable side effects like out-of-memory errors and slowdowns.
I prompted the same tasks on both machines then analyzed the logs and found prompt processing was pretty similar between the platforms, ranging either side of 200 tok/s. However, the AMD Strix Halo Evo-X3 far outpaced the Panther Lake Evo-T2 by generating responses at up to 28 tok/s, compared with around 8 tok/s at best, respectively. It would be possible to tune these LLM speeds for each machine, but I didn’t tweak settings for the comparison tests. With 128GB of unified memory in the Evo-X3, allowing up to 96GB to be dedicated to the GPU, even larger models can be utilized for the most capable local AI chatbots, agents, generation workloads.
During our demanding tests, the GMKtec Evo-X3 stayed admirably cool and quiet. All our tests were done with the default 85W balanced profile, as the system shipped. Owners can also choose to run this system in Silent Mode (54W) or push it to Performance Mode (peak 140W).
Gaming and Graphics on the GMKtec Evo-X3
The GMKtec Evo-X3 is pretty good at gaming, thanks to its powerful CPU and iGPU with lots of fast memory onboard. Remember, the Ryzen AI Max 395+ has 16 Zen 5 CPU cores with 32 threads, and its Radeon RX 8060S iGPU features 40 CUs and 2,560 shader cores – more CUs than a vanilla PlayStation 5. The capacious LPDDR5X-8000 memory pool has a 256-bit interface.
Before moving onto our standard synthetic and AAA PC gaming tests, I decided to run around in Star Wars Outlaws. I chose the High preset, at 1440p, and kind of enjoyed this game, experiencing a performance level of mostly between 60 and 90 frames per second. The graphics weren't anything special, but I noticed the game was using about 9GB of VRAM which could have meant dips and stutters on systems packing 8GB GPUs and using the same graphics settings. While the CPU usage was mostly under 20%, the iGPU was nearer to 90%.
Next up, our benchmarks include a trio of 3DMark synthetics and two iconic PC gaming standards. In the 3DMark Solar Bay test, which seems most appropriate to the mini PCs we have tested in 2026, the Evo-X3 left the competitors in the dust with over 50,000 points. It was almost twice as fast as the Panther Lake B390 iGPU, and about three times as fast as the Radeon 890M machines that came with fast dual-channel RAM (like the aforementioned Arctic and Beelink mini PCs).
In 3DMark Steel Nomad we got a respectable score of 2,132, and the frame rate reached 21 FPS. It was a similar story in 3DMark Speed Way, where the Evo-X3 managed a score of 2,046. For some context this Speed Way result still lags behind my Asus Zephyrus G16 laptop with RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, which scored up to 2,425.
Moving on to real AAA games, let’s check the data provided by the multi-scene benchmarks built into Shadow of the Tomb Raider and Cyberpunk 2077. The former scales well with processor resources and can still often look and run great on humble iGPUs. As for Cyberpunk 2077, it can really push even the strongest modern GPUs, so here we've used two settings to show how the GMKtec Evo-X3 can perform. I thought both these titles looked better than Star Wars Outlaws, too.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The Shadow of the Tomb Raider High 1080p test resulted in an impeccably smooth 138 FPS on average, with the low of 126 FPS, on the Evo-X3. That’s a great score for a mini PC without a discrete graphics card. I was inspired to re-test at 1440p High, and the X3 still achieved an average 96 FPS / low 86 FPS.
In Cyberpunk 2077 the Evo-X3 managed to achieve 96 FPS using the 1080p High preset, with 1% lows at 78 FPS. This is certainly another candidate for moving up to 1440p and/or higher quality presets. CD Projekt Red also provides lots of upscaling tech (DLSS, FSR, XeSS) settings to adjust in this futuristic RPG, to try and get your sweet spot performance / resolution / quality setting dialed in.
Power, Heat, and Noise when using the GMKtec Evo-X3
When I left the GMKtec Evo-X3 to idle, my power meter measured wattages around 16W from the wall for the whole system. When the PC was pushed with simultaneous CPU and GPU benchmarks running, power draw seemed to peak at a little under 150W. GMKtec shipped this device with ‘Balanced Mode’ set in the BIOS, allowing the processor to consume up to 85W. The supplied 230W power brick had plenty in reserve, and it might need it in ‘Performance Mode’ where GMKtec says that the processor alone will demand up to 120W with peak power spikes to 140W.
System tools showed that during light activities like browsing the web, and typing reports like this one, the CPU temperature stuck around 42 degrees Celsius (in a 22 C room). Playing games for 30 or 40 minutes, the reported CPU temperature seemed to stay between 75 C and 82 C most of the time. The peak CPU temperature I saw was 85 C.
GMKtec’s powerful mini PC was a quiet operator at idle and under load. My measurements from about half a foot in front of the device show noise levels under 30 dBA at idle, which is very quiet and under the measurement threshold of my meter. Stressing the system with multiple CPU and GPU loads I managed to get nearly 37 dBA out of the system. This seemed an exceptional result during my testing, as most of the time the max noise level during benchmarks was nearer 33 dBA.
Software and Warranty on the GMKtec Evo-X3
The GMKtec Evo-X3 ships with Windows 11 Pro installed. Unlike its Evo-T2 brother, I found no pre-installed AI apps and tools on the X3. However, I note that the product page mentions GMKtec Claw and Wrangler as features. I installed LM Studio Bionic and Comfy UI for some AI testing, though.
GMKtec sells the Evo-X3 with a one-year warranty.
GMKtec Evo-X3 configurations
GMKtec sells only two Evo-X3 configurations in the U.S. Both machines feature the same processor and generous amounts of RAM. The only configuration choice is between a 2TB SSD (our model) and a 4TB SSD equipped model.
At the time of writing our 2TB configuration is listed at $3,799 but the product page says the price is normally $4,100. The 4TB model is currently $3,999, discounted from $4,349. We don’t know when the prices might get adjusted. Pricing for computers and devices with lots of RAM and storage is volatile right now.
Bottom Line
I was impressed by many aspects of the GMKtec Evo-X3 mini PC. Computing on a machine with so much RAM felt quite liberating. Especially when so much of it can be allocated to the system's iGPU. Moreover, the CPU and iGPU components of the SoC are plenty powerful for the compact form factor. I was also impressed by the X3's sleek design, solid build quality, and quiet operation.
No machine is perfect, though. For example, despite having a variety of ports available including USB4 and OCuLink, I felt there were not enough ports in total. To use this as my daily driver I’d feel pinched by the Evo-X3’s design offering just a single USB4 port, and one HDMI out.
The price is high, even considering the spec, but that's unfortunately common during this component shortage.
GMKtec sells its new Evo-X3 direct at the offer price of $3,799, as mentioned and linked above. At the time of writing we note that our GMKtec Evo-X3 128GB/2TB configuration is also available from Amazon U.S. at the same price, if you prefer.
If you like what you’ve seen of the Evo-X3, the nearest competitors that we have experience of are the Evo-X2, also from GMKtec, and AMD’s first-party, turn-key Strix Halo mini-PC. However, we know there are several next-gen Ryzen AI Max 495+ machines coming to retail soon. Depending on market pricing, configurations, design, and port selections of these refreshed ‘Gorgon Halo’ models, they might be worth waiting for. We saw Minisforum, Lenovo, GMKtec, Chuwi, and AceMagic with AI Max 495+ designs at IFA 2026 earlier this month.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Promising Canadian gothic narrative roguelite Curse of Resthaven launches Oct. 29
articles.text:
Curse of Resthaven, a new gothic narrative rogue from Toronto’s Hilltop Studios, will launch on October 29 on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, PC and Mac.
In a marked departure from Hilltop’s acclaimed debut game, the colourful deduction puzzle-adventure Lil’ Guardsman, Curse tasks players with leading a colony that’s being threatened by supernatural forces. As Governor Ambrose, you’ll have to navigate a time loop that includes resource management, deck-building based expeditions, and interrogations with the people of Resthaven, all of whom are fully voiced by Canadian actors. The game also features a striking graphic novel-inspired art style.
Lil’ Guardsman was one of 2024’s biggest gaming delights, so I can’t wait to see what Hilltop has cooked up with its sophomore title. To help tide us over, Hilltop has also announced an expanded version of the game’s Steam demo will launch on Oct. 8, allowing you to sample the opening hours of the experience. The perfect Halloween title!
