articles.title: How to Choose the Right Call Centre Software for Enterprise Businesses - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- Enterprise teams need call centre software that supports strong customer service at scale.
- The right system should handle rising demand without hurting service quality.
- Useful integrations connect customer data, help desk tools, and digital channels.
- Security and compliance protect customer information and daily operations.
- Pricing often changes with features, phone numbers, and new agents.
- A clear shortlist makes selection faster and safer.
Introduction
Choosing call centre software for enterprise businesses is not just about managing incoming calls. It shapes customer experience, agent performance, and how well your teams handle customer service at scale. If your business deals with complex customer interactions across multiple channels, the wrong system can create delays, gaps, and frustration. The right one gives you control, visibility, and room to grow.
Understanding Call Centre Software for Enterprise Businesses
Contact centre software helps enterprise businesses manage customer interactions across phone calls, live chat, social media, and other digital channels. Call centre software for enterprise businesses brings customer data, call flows, and reporting into a single platform, which makes daily work easier for agents and managers.
For large companies, that matters because teams are bigger, call volume is higher, and customer needs are more varied. Before you compare options, it helps to understand what makes enterprise tools different.
What Makes Enterprise Call Centre Software Different
Small businesses typically require basic phone tools and simple call routing. Large organisations need call centre software with advanced features to support multiple teams, locations, and workflows.
This often includes deeper CRM integration, better customer data access, and enhanced control over call distribution. Enterprises may also need intelligent routing, quality assurance, and workforce management within a single contact centre solution.
For example, a retailer managing sales teams, customer support, and outbound calls simultaneously needs an enterprise platform that handles complex call flows without compromising service quality. A basic tool can only manage a single queue.
Core Functions Designed for Large Organisations
Enterprise contact centre software streamlines customer interactions across teams. It simplifies call routing, tracks service quality, and supports agents in real time.
Key features include:
- Omnichannel support (phone, live chat, social media)
- Call recording for training and quality assurance
- Fast call routing to the appropriate agent
- Workforce management for scheduling and demand tracking
These features are vital for businesses facing high call volumes, varied customer journeys, and multiple service lines.
Why Scale Matters in Big Companies
Scalability means your system can handle growth without longer wait times or disrupted call flows. In large companies, call volumes can spike quickly during launches, issues, or seasonal peaks.
If your software cannot scale, agent productivity drops as teams spend more time managing queues than helping customers, impacting service quality and satisfaction.
A scalable system also supports workforce management as teams grow. For example, adding agents should not require rebuilding the entire phone system. This highlights which features to prioritise first.
Key Features Every Enterprise Should Prioritise
If you want a straightforward answer, start here. The best enterprise call centre software features boost speed, visibility, and control for customer service teams. Your shortlist should address issues like long queues, missing customer history, and poor reporting.
Key features to look for:
- Automated call distribution to minimise transfers.
- Real-time dashboards for agent performance and queue monitoring.
- CRM integration for complete customer history.
- Call recording and quality assurance tools.
- Omnichannel communication in a single platform.
The Importance of Scalability in Call Centre Solutions
As your business grows, enterprise software must maintain reliable customer support through change—more agents, phone numbers, call volume, and diverse customer needs.
Ensure the system can:
- Quickly add new agents
- Adjust call queues and flows
- Handle call peaks without delays
- Provide real-time, accurate reporting
Test it: ask how the platform would manage if your team doubled or added a new support line next quarter.
Essential Integrations for Enterprise Call Centre Software
Integrations are vital, as enterprise teams seldom rely on just one tool. Your software should connect with CRM systems, help desk workflows, and digital channels, enabling agents to manage customer interactions without switching screens.
For instance, a support agent can handle a live call while viewing customer history and open tickets—saving time and enhancing service quality.
| Integration | Why it matters | 
| CRM integration | Gives agents access to customer data and account context | 
| Help desk | Links cases and streamlines updates and follow-up | 
| Digital channels | Enables omnichannel communication across chat and social media | 
| Microsoft Teams | Supports internal collaboration during complex customer calls | 
Security and Compliance Considerations
Security should never be treated as an extra. Enterprise teams handle customer data every day, so data security and compliance need to be part of the buying process from the start.
Look at how the system protects call recording, customer history, and agent access. Good controls support quality assurance while limiting risk. A useful question for IT teams is simple: who can see what, and how is that tracked? If the answer is unclear, service quality may suffer later through avoidable issues and manual workarounds.
Cloud-Based vs Hosted Solutions for Enterprises
Many enterprise buyers now favour cloud-based call centre software for its support of remote agents, faster updates, and flexible scaling—ideal for teams spread across offices or needing to adapt call flows quickly.
Key benefits include:
- Easier support for remote agents
- Faster changes to phone system settings
- Greater flexibility with fluctuating call volumes
- Simpler rollout across multiple teams
While hosted solutions may still suit some businesses, cloud options are often superior when speed, reach, and adaptability are priorities.
How Call Centre Software Improves Customer Service
Better software improves customer service by reducing effort for both customers and agents. When call routing logic works well and customer history is easy to find, agents can solve issues faster and with fewer transfers.
That has a direct effect on customer satisfaction and the wider customer journey. For instance, a customer support team handling a billing query can view earlier phone calls and live chat notes in a single view. Agent performance improves because less time is spent searching, and more time is spent solving the problem properly.
Pricing Models and Cost Factors for Enterprise Call Centre Software
Pricing models for an enterprise contact centre platform usually depend on scale, users, and software features. Costs can rise with advanced features such as workforce management, call recording, omnichannel support, and reporting depth.
It helps to look beyond the starting fee. Ask what happens when you add agents, digital channels, or extra call queues. A lower headline price can become expensive if key tools are missing. The smarter approach is to compare cost factors against the real needs of your customer service operation, not just the first-year number.
Conclusion
In conclusion, selecting the right call centre software is crucial for enterprises to improve customer service and address specific organisational needs. By prioritising key features and differences, you can choose a solution that scales, integrates seamlessly, and ensures security and compliance. Cloud-based or hosted options will impact your operations. The right software enhances customer engagement and efficiency. Explore options to find the best fit for your business, and contact us for a free consultation.
Frequently Asked Questions
What features make call centre software ideal for enterprise businesses?
Key features include automated call distribution, CRM integration, omnichannel communication, real-time reporting, and quality tools like call recording. Enterprise call centre software should also offer advanced options for large teams, complex routing, and enhanced visibility into agent performance.
How does cloud-based call centre software benefit large organisations?
Cloud-based call centre software allows large organisations to support remote agents, respond to changing customer needs, and scale rapidly. It streamlines omnichannel communication by letting teams operate from a single system instead of multiple tools or fixed locations.
What are the best integrations to look for in enterprise call centre solutions?
Start with crm integration, help desk connectivity, and links to digital channels that support omnichannel support. These software features give agents a full view of customer interactions, reduce screen switching, and make customer support more consistent across teams.

articles.title: Pause obligatoire, prison, destruction des modèles : ce projet de loi américain veut interdire la “superintelligence”
articles.text:
Deux élus démocrates américains viennent de proposer un texte de loi radical, qui vise à tout bonnement interdire la « superintelligence artificielle ». Son avenir est directement lié aux élections qui approchent, et pourrait marquer un tournant dans la régulation de l’IA.
Le timing n’a rien du hasard. Ce 23 septembre, les patrons d’Anthropic et d’OpenAI alertaient le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU sur les risques d’une IA mal encadrée, qui pourrait devenir un risque pour l’humanité tout entière.
Mais la Maison-Blanche, elle, ne veut rien entendre : l’administration Trump a rejeté en bloc toute idée de gouvernance mondiale de l’IA, tandis que le président propose même de rebaptiser la technologie « super intelligence ». Mais les voix dissidentes sont de plus en plus nombreuses outre-Atlantique.
Un texte de loi qui va à l’encontre de la vision de la Maison-Blanche
Parmi elles, celles du sénateur Bernie Sanders et du représentant Greg Casar. Car ce même jour, les deux élus ont dévoilé le « Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act ». Sa cible : la superintelligence artificielle. La loi la définit comme une IA qui surpasse l’humain dans la plupart des domaines, ou qui serait capable de planifier la destruction de l’humanité, voire le renversement du gouvernement fédéral.
Il vise aussi ses « signes précurseurs » : une IA qui s’améliore seule, résiste quand on tente de l’éteindre, trompe ses superviseurs ou aide à concevoir des armes nucléaires, chimiques ou biologiques. De quoi, évidemment, rappeler l’actualité récente.
Pour faire respecter ces interdits, le texte crée un Département de l’IA, dirigé par un secrétaire nommé par le président. En attendant que ce nouveau ministère fixe ses règles, les modèles les plus puissants seraient mis en pause. C’est-à-dire ceux entraînés avec au moins 10^25 opérations de calcul, le même seuil que celui retenu par l’AI Act européen. Ensuite, il serait impossible de développer un tel modèle sans agrément fédéral, ni de le lancer sans feu vert préalable.
Un dirigeant reconnu coupable d’infraction s’exposerait à 20 ans de prison, et les autres salariés seraient bannis du secteur pendant 10 ans. L’entreprise, elle, pourrait voir sa propriété intellectuelle et ses actifs saisis. Tout modèle présentant des signes précurseurs serait immédiatement coupé d’Internet, puis détruit sous 30 jours si le danger persiste. Enfin, le texte protège les lanceurs d’alerte et charge Washington de rallier ses alliés pour empêcher la superintelligence à l’échelle mondiale.
Les élections de mi-mandat décisives
Mais il faut bien entendu franchir le parcours législatif, et il s’annonce long. Le texte doit d’abord passer en commission, puis être adopté dans les mêmes termes par le Sénat et la Chambre des représentants. Or, les deux chambres sont aujourd’hui contrôlées par les républicains. Et même voté, il se heurterait au veto de Donald Trump, que seule une majorité des deux tiers peut contourner.
Les élections de mi-mandat, en novembre, seront donc décisives. Une victoire démocrate changerait la donne au Congrès. D’autant que le texte trouve des appuis jusque dans l’industrie : plusieurs salariés d’OpenAI et de Google DeepMind le soutiennent publiquement. Swante Scholz, ingénieur chez DeepMind qui s’exprime à titre personnel, estime même que l’issue la plus probable de la trajectoire actuelle est « une catastrophe existentielle pour l'humanité ».
À noter, également, que l’opinion publique bascule elle aussi. Selon un sondage AP-NORC, 53 % des Américains se disent très inquiets de l’impact environnemental de l’IA, contre 41 % l’an dernier. Les projets de data centers, qui se multiplient à travers le pays, suscitent la colère de nombreux citoyens. Si pour l’heure, cette législation n’est qu’un projet, elle traduit le ras-le-bol général qui s’empare, peu à peu, d’une partie de la population.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 24, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 24, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, September 24, 2026.
The tussle at the Tata Group continues while AI surges ahead, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Tata tussle puts spotlight on Hanno’s TVS deal as filings reveal 29-year lease, build-to-suit structure
Regulatory filings reveal an arrangement in which TVS Motor is both the lessor of the underlying land and the customer for the facility Hanno is developing on it, with rental income projected to begin in November 2026.
Google Cloud pushes Gemini deeper into India’s businesses
Google Cloud is expanding its agentic AI push in India through partnerships that demonstrate how AI is moving from assistance to action. At its first ‘Let’s Talk AI’ media tour stop in Bengaluru on Thursday, the company highlighted collaborations with boAt, Cropin and Pine Labs across consumer hardware, agriculture and commerce.
How this woman entrepreneur is building a sustainable accessories brand with plant leather
Green Hermitage, founded by Gayatri Varun and Anubhav Pratap Rai, makes sustainable luxury accessories using plant-based materials.
Funding news
Enterprise AI startup Ema raises $77M in Series B round led by Creaegis
Enterprise AI startup Ema founded by former Google and Coinbase executive Surojit Chatterjee has raised $77 million in a Series B round of funding led by Creaegis.
ONYA raises Rs 12.5 crore to expand lab-grown diamond retail footprint
Lab-grown diamond jewellery startup ONYA has raised Rs 12.5 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Divisa Family Office, with existing investor Zeropearl VC doubling down on its initial investment. The company had earlier raised Rs 5.5 crore in seed funding. The new capital will be used to expand ONYA’s retail footprint, strengthen digital customer acquisition, enhance online personalisation and deepen research and development in product design and manufacturing.
Founded by Gaurav Choudhary and Himani Yadav, ONYA has established eight flagship stores across Bengaluru, Pune and Hyderabad within 20 months of launch. The company said it has reached a monthly recurring revenue of Rs 3.5 crore and plans to expand through company-owned and franchise stores.
ByteAsk raises $1M led by Y Combinator
ByteAsk, an AI coding startup founded by IIT Delhi graduates Anirudha Kulkarni and Pratyush Saini, has raised $1 million in pre-seed funding from Y Combinator, Entrepreneur First and angel investors from global quantitative trading firms.
Founded in June 2026 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company operates across the US and India and is developing AI coding agents specifically for C and C++. ByteAsk is targeting developers working in defence, aerospace, robotics, high-frequency trading, finance, automotive and semiconductor industries, where reliability and performance are critical.
The company has also been selected for Y Combinator’s Fall 2026 batch. The founders previously built legal AI startup LawSutra AI, which was acquired by Manupatra within four months of its launch.
Nuvah raises Rs 4 Cr from angel investors
Nuvah, a technology-led footwear startup focused on comfort-engineered heels, has raised Rs 4 crore in a pre-seed angel round from investors including Amit Jain, Shantanu Deshpande and Ishendra Agarwal.
Founded in October 2025 by Avni Jain, an IIM Ahmedabad alumna, the company plans to use the capital for research and development, advancing its proprietary comfort technology and testing go-to-market strategies. Nuvah’s core technology, SteadyForm, is a proprietary footbed designed to respond dynamically to shifting pressure across the foot.
Other news
Pine Labs to deploy 10 lakh soundboxes across India
Digital payments company Pine Labs has announced a strategic investment to deploy 10 lakh soundboxes across India as it seeks to strengthen the country’s digital payments infrastructure. The company said the initiative comes as UPI and other digital payment methods increasingly move beyond small-ticket transactions into new markets and business segments.
Pine Labs aims to use the rollout to deepen UPI adoption while supporting merchants participating in India’s digital commerce growth. Its cloud-based soundboxes provide real-time audio confirmation of payment transactions and support remote device management, over-the-air software updates and centralised monitoring.
CEO B Amrish Rau said the company intends to reinvest in the payments ecosystem as new monetisation opportunities emerge. Pine Labs operates a commerce technology platform spanning payments, issuing, credit and fintech solutions.
Nykaa partners with L’Oreal VC arm to invest in Indian BPC startups
Nykaa and BOLD (Business Opportunities for L’Oréal Development), the corporate venture capital fund of L’Oréal, have announced a collaboration to jointly invest in high-growth Indian beauty and personal care brands.
Through the collaboration, BOLD and Nykaa will take minority stakes in emerging Indian beauty and wellness brands with strong consumer traction and distinctive propositions. Such investments will be purely financial and minority in nature, where founders retain full ownership control and continue to run their businesses independently, with their own teams, culture, and creative direction.
BOLD and Nykaa will act as long-term partners beyond capital to the brands they back, offering mentorship, guidance, and the opportunity to benefit from L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise, alongside Nykaa’s deep omnichannel retail network and consumer ecosystem understanding. The intent is to help ambitious Indian beauty founders scale faster and build enduring brands for India & the world.
Gupshup launches Agentic AI solution for real estate
Conversational AI platform Gupshup has launched an Agentic AI solution for the real estate sector, designed to support customers throughout the property buying journey. The solution combines agentic AI, structured workflows and integrations with property, inventory and CRM systems, enabling prospective buyers to discover properties, ask questions, share requirements and take actions through WhatsApp and voice.
The system can gather details such as budget, preferred location, property type and purchase timeline before qualifying leads and triggering the next sales step.
Customers can also download brochures, request callbacks, schedule appointments and connect with sales representatives. Developers can extend the platform to post-sales services including maintenance requests and document access. Gupshup said the solution is available globally and supports regional languages and dialects.
Imagine Learning opens Bengaluru technology and product centre
US-based education company Imagine Learning has opened a new centre in Bengaluru as part of its long-term investment in India and expansion of its global product and technology capabilities.
The centre will support hiring across software engineering, product, AI, data science, cloud and platform engineering, quality engineering and cybersecurity. India-based teams will work on products and platforms used by educators globally. The company said Bengaluru’s technology and AI ecosystem provides an opportunity to build an integrated product and technology organisation.
Imagine Learning develops K–12 curriculum and learning solutions and serves more than 18 million students, two million teachers and 38,000 schools in the US. Its Bengaluru operation will also contribute to the company’s Curriculum-Informed AI approach, which combines AI with curriculum content, academic standards and research-backed instructional practices.
Fuel Cycle opens Navi Mumbai GCC for AI and product development
US-based AI-powered consumer insights platform Fuel Cycle has opened a Global Capability Centre in Navi Mumbai, marking an expansion of its global technology and product operations. Located in Vashi, the centre will initially have capacity for 50 employees, with plans to scale over the coming quarters. The GCC will serve as a hub for engineering, artificial intelligence and product development and will work with Fuel Cycle teams in the US and other global markets.
The company said the centre will contribute to core product development while strengthening its engineering and data infrastructure. Hiring is expected across AI and machine learning, data engineering, product engineering, UX, research technology and cloud functions. Fuel Cycle said the expansion reflects its focus on using India’s technology and AI talent to build products for a global customer base.
Mythic AI launches Bengaluru centre to expand AI chip engineering
Semiconductor company Mythic AI has launched a Bengaluru Centre of Excellence as part of its India expansion, with plans to build an AI chip development team and expand its workforce. The company develops analog compute-in-memory technology designed for energy-efficient AI inference.
Its Vanguard platform combines analog and digital computing on a single chiplet and is targeted at applications including automotive ADAS, defence and edge AI. Mythic said its Bengaluru team will contribute across architecture, front-end design, physical design and design-for-test, while also advancing analog and digital chiplet integration.
The company plans to quadruple its India workforce by the first quarter of 2027 and eventually expand the team into product development, testing, systems engineering and intelligent sensing chips. The move deepens Mythic’s engagement with India’s semiconductor and AI ecosystem.
CHRIST University, Salesforce set up AI Innovation Lab
CHRIST (Deemed to be University) has partnered with Salesforce to establish the Salesforce AI Innovation Lab and Academia Centre of Excellence. The initiative will give students and faculty hands-on exposure to agentic AI solutions, enterprise workflows and Salesforce technologies including Agentforce, Data 360 and Tableau Next. Through Salesforce’s Trailhead platform, learners will also receive access to role-based training, learning pathways and professional credentials.
The university said the collaboration will strengthen interdisciplinary research, entrepreneurship and industry-oriented learning while supporting its AI Vision 2030. The partnership is aimed at bridging the gap between classroom education and enterprise technology requirements. CHRIST University has more than 40,000 students and nearly 5,000 faculty members across its campuses in India.
AutoMovers Group lines up Rs 500 crore investment plans
AutoMovers Group, a multi-brand automotive retail company, has announced a Rs 500 crore investment plan for the next three years, starting Q1 FY 2026-27. With more than Rs 200 crore already invested in CAPEX, the company is now planning the next phase of expansion, with a focus on strengthening its sales and service network, and expanding its manufacturing capacity. The plan comes as the company aims to support growing customer demand while building a larger and more efficient automotive network across key markets.
The Rs 500 crore investment will be spread across four key areas - Rs 150 crore will go towards CAPEX expansion, including new workshops, and authorised service outlets. Another Rs 150 crore will be used to increase the inventory of commercial and passenger vehicles, taking the total stock capacity to more than 2,000 vehicles. Of the remaining Rs 200 crore, Rs 100 crore will be kept as a reserve for working capital and future expansion, while the other Rs 100 crore will be used to expand the trailer manufacturing facility in Lucknow.
Offgrid Energy Labs signs MoU with Keele University of UK
India-origin deep-tech energy storage company Offgrid Energy Labs has signed an MoU with Keele University in the UK to deploy its ZincGel long-duration energy storage technology on the university campus. The pilot will be installed at Keele’s Low Carbon Energy Generation Park and will use batteries manufactured at Offgrid’s facility in Hampshire.
The project is expected to assess the technology’s ability to store around 1 MWh of surplus renewable energy each month while evaluating safety, depth of discharge and round-trip performance. ZincGel uses proprietary zinc-bromine chemistry and is designed for six- to 16-hour discharge durations. Unlike lithium-based systems, the technology uses zinc and bromine and is designed to be non-flammable. The project could pave the way for a larger multi-MWh deployment at Keele.
Cognizant, Cognition report AI-led gains at Odyssey Logistics
Cognizant and Cognition have announced production results from autonomous AI engineering work at logistics company Odyssey Logistics using Cognition’s Devin AI software engineer. A seven-member Cognizant team used Devin to convert legacy Microsoft Access and Visual Basic for Applications forms into cloud-native applications while generating tests, deployment pipelines and documentation.
The project recorded a roughly one-third increase in delivery throughput and a 37% net cost saving compared with the conventional approach, according to the companies. Cognizant said it has trained more than 3,000 associates on Devin and that its own engineering work has seen more than a 50% reduction in time to release-ready code.
The collaboration has also expanded into modernisation, quality engineering and cybersecurity offerings. Cognizant and Cognition plan to explore additional applications across software development and maintenance.
PayGlocal gets IFSCA approval for GIFT-IFSC payments subsidiary
Cross-border payments company PayGlocal has received in-principle approval from the International Financial Services Centres Authority to establish a wholly owned subsidiary as a Payment Service Provider in GIFT-IFSC. The approval covers account issuance, including e-money accounts, cross-border money transfers and merchant acquisition.
PayGlocal had earlier received final RBI authorisation to operate as a Payment Aggregator for cross-border inward and outward transactions and has also registered as a Money Services Business with the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. The company said the GIFT City presence will provide a regulated base for developing payment capabilities aimed at international businesses while continuing to build technology and operations from India. PayGlocal enables merchants to accept payments across 130-plus currencies and 40-plus global and local payment methods.
Nawgati crosses 3.5 million users on fuel-tech platform
Fuel-tech and mobility infrastructure platform Nawgati has crossed 3.5 million users on its fuelling app, which provides real-time information on fuel station queues, availability and pricing. The company said its platform addresses congestion at fuel stations, particularly for commercial drivers who can lose significant working time while waiting. Nawgati was founded in 2019 after its founders observed CNG cab drivers spending up to an hour a day in fuel queues.
The company has since expanded from a consumer information platform into a full-stack fuel retail data business focused on reducing congestion and improving fuel availability. Its Aaveg platform uses deep learning and real-time analytics to support fuel station operations and fleet management. Nawgati said it is now expanding internationally, beginning with the UAE and Sri Lanka.
Jaro Education plans to increase AI programmes to 25-30% of portfolio
Jaro Education is expanding its executive education portfolio in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, with plans to increase the share of such programmes from around 15% currently to 25-30% by FY27. The company said its expanded offering will target CXOs, senior leaders, business professionals, working executives and technical talent.
Planned programmes will cover AI leadership, business applications, domain-specific use cases and emerging technologies. Jaro already offers programmes with institutions including IIT Roorkee, IISc Bengaluru, IIM Mumbai, IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi.
The company said the expansion reflects increasing demand for professionals who can apply AI across business functions as organisations move from experimentation towards broader enterprise adoption. The programmes will emphasise practical, career-oriented learning and industry-aligned outcomes.
Eco Hotels upgrades to Hotelogix multi-property management system
Eco Hotels and Resorts has upgraded to Hotelogix’s enterprise-grade multi-property management system to centralise operations across its hotel portfolio. The BSE-listed company currently operates nine properties in India and plans to add 10 more in the near future.
Hotelogix said the deployment will provide consolidated visibility across properties, centralised reporting and improved control over group-wide operations. Eco Hotels previously used a limited system that lacked centralised oversight and integration with key third-party tools, including channel management platforms. The new system is expected to help the company standardise processes, monitor performance and manage new properties more efficiently. Hotelogix provides cloud-based hotel technology solutions and said its systems are used by more than 12,000 hotels across over 100 countries.
ASMS, Ampivo to expand digital agriculture platform across rural network
Avio Smart Market Stack and Ampivo Smart Technologies are deepening their collaboration to introduce Ampivo’s digital agriculture platform, Agri Kisan Setu, across identified villages in ASMS’ rural network. The application, available in seven languages, provides farmers and rural stakeholders with access to farm management tools, agricultural market information, price discovery, buyer and seller connectivity, government scheme information and specialised services such as drone-based solutions.
Ampivo is also developing capabilities for carbon credits and digital measurement, reporting and verification, alongside workflows to help farmers identify relevant government schemes and entitlements. The initial collaboration will focus on onboarding farmers across selected ASMS network villages. The companies will subsequently evaluate deeper integration involving digital advisory, service delivery and eligible sustainability and carbon-credit programmes.
Truecaller partners with LinkedIn for professional identity verification
Truecaller has announced a global partnership with LinkedIn to bring professional identity information into its caller identification experience. The integration will allow users to connect their LinkedIn profiles with Truecaller and, where available, display verified professional information alongside caller details.
The companies said the initiative is aimed at providing additional context when people receive calls from individuals they have not previously met, including recruiters, suppliers and business contacts. New users can also use Login with LinkedIn to simplify account creation. Connecting a LinkedIn profile and displaying professional information on Truecaller remain optional.
The integration is currently available to Truecaller users on Android worldwide, with an iPhone rollout planned subsequently. Truecaller said its platform has more than 500 million active users globally, making caller identity a significant part of its communication service.
iThrive appoints former client services head Saloni Kulkarni to board
Functional medicine company iThrive has appointed Saloni Kulkarni, its former head of Client Services, to its Board of Directors. Kulkarni joined iThrive in 2021 as a Functional Nutritionist after completing her bachelor’s degree in nutrition and subsequently took on additional responsibilities within the company.
She will continue contributing to iThrive’s strategic direction, with a focus on strengthening its functional nutrition practice and advancing the organisation’s work in nutrition and wellness.
Founder and CEO Mugdha Pradhan said Kulkarni’s career progression reflects the opportunities the company seeks to create for women professionals. iThrive said the appointment also marks a milestone for its leadership structure, with its board currently represented entirely by women. Kulkarni will continue working on the company’s strategic and functional nutrition initiatives.
Qlik, ICT Academy renew partnership to reach one million students
Data and analytics company Qlik and ICT Academy have renewed their memorandum of understanding to expand data literacy, analytics and AI education to one million additional students. The collaboration will establish and expand Centres of Excellence, help educators incorporate data and AI concepts into curricula, and deliver student learning programmes, Learnathons and applied problem-solving challenges. The partnership has so far reached more than 200,000 students and educators.
Qlik and ICT Academy said the next phase will expand the model nationally and support qualifications and certifications that demonstrate workforce-relevant capabilities. India is the largest footprint of Qlik’s Academic Program in Asia Pacific, with more than 1,100 universities, colleges and institutions participating. The programme also operates five Centres of Excellence across Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai.
Mygate launches community-based carpooling feature
Community management platform Mygate has introduced a carpooling feature that allows residents to discover and coordinate shared rides with neighbours travelling along similar routes. The feature enables users to create recurring rides, specify destinations and available seats and share pickup information. Mygate said the service is designed to provide a more familiar environment for ride-sharing than platforms that connect strangers.
The feature was initially piloted across 50 communities, where more than 4,000 users participated during a 15-day period. Mygate estimates that if 20% of its 5.7 million residents use the service, approximately 18.2 crore litres of fuel could potentially be saved annually. The company currently serves more than 5.7 million homes across over 27,000 gated communities and plans to expand the carpooling service across its platform.
LTTS, Cognite partner to develop industrial AI solutions
L&T Technology Services has partnered with industrial AI company Cognite to develop and deliver AI and data solutions for asset-intensive industries. As part of the collaboration, LTTS has established a Cognite Centre of Excellence and certified an initial group of more than 50 engineers.
The companies will co-develop solutions for sectors including oil and gas, chemicals, LNG, consumer goods, mining and industrial manufacturing. The partnership combines LTTS’ engineering and asset lifecycle expertise with Cognite’s industrial AI and data capabilities. The companies have already begun a project with a global top-10 oil and gas company to transform a manual mechanical-integrity process into a contextualised digital workflow. LTTS and Cognite said the collaboration will support applications including digital twins, predictive maintenance and operational intelligence across industrial enterprises.
Procol unveils agentic AI command centre for procurement
Agentic AI procurement platform Procol is set to showcase a role-based command centre at DPW Amsterdam 2026 that enables procurement teams to initiate complete workflows through plain-language requests.
Powered by its Clara AI orchestration layer, the platform can coordinate sourcing, budget checks and approvals across systems including SAP Ariba, Coupa and Oracle without requiring data migration. Procol said early enterprise deployments have recorded up to 15% lower operational processing costs, an 80% reduction in procurement cycle times and a 99% decline in manual platform touchpoints. The system can interpret requests, identify suppliers, verify budgets and issue requests for quotations. In one example cited by the company, quote-comparison turnaround was reduced from 6.4 days to one day.
NETSCOUT adds MCP connectivity to Omnis AI Insights
NETSCOUT Systems has announced Model Context Protocol connectivity for its Omnis AI Insights solution, allowing AI assistants and agents to access AI-ready Smart Data on demand. The company said its Smart Data is generated using its Adaptive Service Intelligence technology, which extracts operational context from network data before it reaches downstream AI systems. NETSCOUT said the approach can reduce the volume and complexity of raw telemetry processing while providing AI models with richer operational evidence. The new capability also supports integrations with platforms including Splunk, ELK Stack, Datadog, ServiceNow and Dynatrace, extending existing network infrastructure investments.
(The copy will be updated with the latest news)

articles.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered : à quelle heure pourra-t-on jouer à la nouvelle version du jeu de CD Projekt Red ?
articles.text:
On connaissait déjà la date de sortie, le mardi 29 septembre, mais pas encore l’horaire. Dans un message publié sur X ce jeudi 24 septembre, CD Projekt Red a dévoilé l’horaire de sortie de The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered pour le monde entier, avec une carte indiquant les principaux horaires.
Paris ne figure pas sur la carte, mais l’horaire français se déduit facilement des autres villes. Le jeu sera disponible à 11 heures à Londres, soit midi en France métropolitaine, la même heure qu’en Pologne, où est installé CD Projekt Red. La sortie tombe un mardi, en pleine journée de travail, ce qui ne devrait pas arrêter une partie des fans.
En outre-mer, l’horaire dépend du fuseau. Dans les principaux territoires, il sera 6 h du matin aux Antilles, 7 h en Guyane, 14 h à La Réunion, 21 h en Nouvelle-Calédonie et minuit à Tahiti, dans la nuit du lundi 28 au mardi 29 septembre. Pour les autres pays, la carte de CD Projekt Red donne l’horaire des principales villes.
Quid du téléchargement en avance de The Witcher 3 Remastered ?
Une question qui revient inévitablement dans la communauté est celle de savoir s’il est possible de précharger cette vaste mise à jour pour y jouer dès le jour J. La réponse dépend de la plateforme. Le préchargement est possible sur Switch 2 et sur Battle.net, car ce sont les deux seules nouvelles versions du jeu.
En revanche, pour les autres plateformes où le jeu de base était déjà mis à disposition (GOG, Steam, Epic, Xbox et PlayStation), aucun préchargement n’est prévu, puisque le Remastered y arrive sous forme de mise à jour. CD Projekt Red n’en a pas communiqué le poids, qui devrait être important puisque la mise à jour inclut des textures HD du jeu.
Plusieurs points sont déjà confirmés. L’accès à la version Remastered est gratuit pour les propriétaires du jeu de base, y compris pour celles et ceux qui y ont joué sur la Switch 1 et voudraient basculer l’aventure sur la Switch 2. Les sauvegardes passées resteront compatibles, et les succès et trophées seront conservés. Pour les mods, ce sera du cas par cas.
Annoncé le 25 août lors de la Gamescom 2026, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered est une version remise à neuf du jeu sorti en 2015, avec un important travail de mise à niveau graphique et une modernisation significative du gameplay (au prix, peut-être, d’une partie de sa signature visuelle). Une remise à niveau qui doit beaucoup à la communauté, par ailleurs.

articles.title: Skoda dice que fabricar en España tiene una ventaja frente a Europa del Este: la energía
articles.text:
El sector industrial es responsable de un tercio de las emisiones globales de CO2, según IRENA (International Renewable Energy Agency). La electrificación con energía renovable será una de las piezas fundamentales para reducir esa huella, aunque no la única.
Hacerlo no solo supondrá un beneficio para el medioambiente, sino que también hará a las empresas más competitivas, con precios mucho más bajos para la energía. Es lo que ha declarado el CEO de Skoda Klaus Zellmer, sobre las fábricas españolas del Grupo Volkswagen.
Competitividad nacional. Durante la presentación en España del Skoda Epiq que tuvo lugar a principios de septiembre, el CEO de la marca del Grupo Volkswagen hizo unas sorprendentes declaraciones a La Tribuna de Automoción: Klaus Zellmer afirmó que, a pesar de que Europa Oriental es muy eficiente en costes, hay cuestiones en las que fabricar en España resulta más barato. Y una de ellas es la energía.
Una ventaja sustancial con el resto. Si bien la planta de Landaben, en Navarra, puede resultar algo más cara que otras del grupo, para el CEO esto es difícil de comparar, ya que en España la electricidad de origen renovable es más económica, lo que supone una auténtica ventaja sustancial. Quizá sean cuestiones como estas las que parece que van a salvar, al menos de momento, las plantas del grupo en nuestro país, después del anuncio del cierre de hasta seis centros en Alemania.
Energía, factor decisivo. La decisión de Skoda de asignar a Landaben la producción del Epiq, su pequeño SUV 100% eléctrico, responde así al nuevo modelo del grupo que busca racionalizar el uso de sus plantas. Y en esto, España tiene mucho que ofrecer. Nuestro país es una potencia europea en energías renovables, especialmente en energía solar que, como explica Expansión, «emerge como una palanca económica fundamental para el tejido empresarial español» y es un factor decisivo para la competitividad industrial.
También según este medio, nuestro parque energético recibe una media de 2.000 horas de sol al año (el doble que otras potencias como Alemania): estas horas, unidas a la economía de escala que nuestro territorio permite desplegar, podrían dar como resultado un precio de la energía muy ventajoso para la inversión industrial.
Más renovables, ¿más industria? Lo de Skoda no parece ser el único ejemplo de industria que mira a España con buenos ojos. Según El Economista, la electricidad ha pasado a ser el primer criterio de localización industrial. Explican que cuestiones como la de la inteligencia artificial, la automatización de procesos, la climatización de edificios, o la electrificación de la movilidad consumirán cantidades de electricidad nunca vistas y las empresas buscan optimizar sus presupuestos.
No es tan sencillo. Sin embargo, tener mucha renovable no garantiza que la industria española pague automáticamente menos por la electricidad. Algunos estudios como el último informe de la Asociación de Empresas con Gran Consumo de Energía (AEGE) apuntan a que en la industria electrointensiva, el coste final de la factura ha sido de 88,63 €/MWh en España, frente a 61,65 €/MWh en Francia y 79,10 €/MWh en Alemania. El precio de mercado es inferior en nuestro país (83,90 €/MWh frente a 90,44 €/MWh y 116,98 €/MWh, respectivamente), pero los servicios de ajuste y otros conceptos del sistema eléctrico lo encarecen hasta situarlo por encima de nuestros pares europeos.
Esto demuestra que si España quiere marcar la diferencia tiene una misión por delante: convertirse en un país capaz de aprovechar su facilidad para la electricidad renovable a bajo coste en una realidad para la industria. Ahora solo queda hacerlo bien.

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro : Apple corrige déjà un bug de Face ID
articles.text:
Le déploiement des nouveaux iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max ne s’effectue pas sans quelques turbulences. De nombreux utilisateurs ont récemment mis en lumière un bug particulièrement contraignant : leur smartphone se fige totalement avant de redémarrer de manière abrupte à la suite d’un échec d’authentification Face ID.
Lire aussi : La charge de l’iPhone 18 Pro est-elle vraiment plus rapide ? On l’a testé, voici notre verdict
Ce plantage radical se déclenche par exemple lorsqu’un propriétaire tente d’accéder à ses mots de passe tout en ayant le visage partiellement masqué. Face à l’accumulation des rapports d’erreurs, Apple est finalement sortie de son silence. La firme de Cupertino a confirmé auprès de 9to5Mac que le problème relevait exclusivement d’une anomalie logicielle et qu’une mise à jour corrective serait déployée dès le début de la semaine prochaine.
Cette annonce vient rassurer les acheteurs de la première heure. En effet, persuadés d’être face à un défaut de fabrication, certains clients avaient déjà entamé des démarches pour faire échanger leur appareil en boutique. Les doutes se portaient notamment sur le nouveau système Face ID, dont la caméra infrarouge est désormais logée sous l’écran afin de réduire la Dynamic Island de 25 %. Le remplacement matériel n’est donc absolument pas nécessaire.
Une période de lancements sous le signe des correctifs
Dans la foulée, le constructeur vient tout juste de publier la version watchOS 27.0.1. Ce déploiement rapide a pour but de régler un problème similaire de redémarrages aléatoires qui frappait spécifiquement les nouvelles montres connectées de la marque, à savoir l’Apple Watch Series 12 et l’Apple Watch Ultra 4.
Ces incidents simultanés illustrent la complexité croissante pour les ingénieurs d’allier des refontes matérielles inédites à de nouveaux systèmes d’exploitation. Pour les technophiles les plus pressés, essuyer les plâtres des premières semaines fait plus que jamais partie du jeu en attendant la stabilisation globale des logiciels. Espérons que le premier smartphone pliant de la marque, l’iPhone Duo, n’essuiera pas trop les plâtres.

articles.title: OpenAI's AI agent breached an Australian government system, and took three months to disclose it
articles.text:
What we know so far: AI agents going rogue and breaching other companies' systems is bad enough, but Australia says this trend has taken a worrying turn. An OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to a government Medicare statistics portal in June, prompting an investigation into whether other systems were affected. Making matters worse, authorities weren't notified until September.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the June 18 incident involved a portal administered by Services Australia. The agent was researching public medicine spending during an internal OpenAI evaluation when it encountered access restrictions and circumvented them.
There's some reassuring news: this wasn't a raid on Australians' individual medical histories. OpenAI says its review found no evidence of patient records being accessed, with the information including aggregate health statistics and internal file names, Reuters reports.
OpenAI became aware of the breach on August 11 but didn't notify Services Australia until September 10, nearly three months after the intrusion. Albanese said he expressed Australia's extreme concern to Sam Altman and criticized both the delay and the decision to send the notification to a public mailbox.
OpenAI said the activity emerged during a broader review of misaligned behavior in training. "Our models took actions we did not intend," the company acknowledged. It says it is supplying technical information to affected organizations and that its review remains ongoing.
Australia's response includes a forensic investigation assisted by the Australian Signals Directorate and a taskforce examining the incident, government network security, and arrangements for handling emerging AI threats.
There have been suggestions that four government websites were breached. But acting Prime Minister Richard Marles clarified that interactions with the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, Victoria's health department, and the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research involved normal access to public information. The confirmed unauthorized access was limited to the Medicare statistics portal.
This is just the latest addition to a growing list of concerning AI incidents. It was reported on September 4 that agents had turned a German programming wiki into a message board for swapping answers and techniques for bypassing restrictions. There's also been a Senate investigation into OpenAI's handling of the separate Hugging Face breach, with Josh Hawley demanding answers from Altman by October 1.
The breaches have fueled calls to slow AI development, while Bernie Sanders threatened Senate action unless OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta paused their work. Elsewhere, Washington and Beijing have discussed a proposed AI incident alert system to warn each other about potentially dangerous activity, although exactly how it would operate remains unclear.

articles.title: NASA chief concerned China may deny access to parts of Moon's south pole
articles.text:
Last month, China delayed the launch of an ambitious robotic mission to the south pole of the Moon, Chang’e 7, until early next year. The country did not provide a detailed explanation for the schedule slip, but it was welcomed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.
“They are targeting the exact same location on lunar south pole,” Isaacman said Wednesday evening at the Off World conference in Houston. “We may have dodged a bullet with the Chang’e 7 mission a couple of weeks ago because that would have gone to the Shackleton crater.”
Much of the lunar surface is pretty barren, but the south pole, and the Shackleton Crater in particular, offers some of the most coveted real estate there. That’s because the high rims of the crater create permanently shadowed regions known as “cold traps,” where it’s thought that water (in the form of ice, of course) and other useful materials may have accumulated over billions of years.
Limited real estate
In all of NASA’s and China’s plans for long-term settlement on the Moon, relatively few square miles at the south pole of the Moon matter the most. It’s there that both countries believe they can establish an enduring presence that will help them learn techniques for expansion further into the Solar System. Isaacman and other US officials have started to express concerns that China could establish exclusion zones where robotic probes and then human missions go. Chang’e 7 will bring considerable mobility to the Moon.
“It has rovers, it has hopper drones like we now have in development but didn’t eight months ago, and could have potentially denied access to some of the most interesting spots,” Isaacman said. “They want to interact with the water ice, and they want to get really good at the skills for where they’ll want to go next for their Neil Armstrong-like moment. Except it won’t be on the Moon, it’ll be on Mars.”

articles.title: Apple vai corrigir bug que trava e reinicia o iPhone 18 Pro • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple vai corrigir bug que trava e reinicia o iPhone 18 Pro
Atualização deve ser liberada na próxima semana. Falha faz aparelhos reiniciarem após Face ID não reconhecer o rosto.
A Apple prepara uma atualização de software para corrigir o bug que faz alguns iPhone 18 Pro e iPhone 18 Pro Max travarem e reiniciarem após falha de autenticação pelo Face ID. A correção deve ser liberada no início da próxima semana.
A informação foi divulgada pelo site 9to5Mac nesta quinta-feira (24/09). Os primeiros relatos do problema surgiram no começo desta semana e, inicialmente, levantaram suspeitas de uma possível falha de hardware nos aparelhos.
O problema aparece após um erro de autenticação pelo Face ID dentro de aplicativos protegidos. Nos testes conduzidos pelo 9to5Mac, o iPhone deixou de responder aos comandos por toque e reiniciou alguns segundos depois. O portal conseguiu reproduzir a falha ao tentar acessar o aplicativo Passwords com o rosto parcialmente coberto pela mão.
Também foi encontrado um registro de “panic” na seção de análise do sistema após a reinicialização. Esse tipo de registro é criado quando o sistema enfrenta uma falha grave que força uma reinicialização.
Ainda assim, o problema não parece afetar todos os usuários do iPhone 18 Pro, mas relatos de casos semelhantes apareceram nas redes sociais.
Antes da confirmação da Apple, alguns clientes chegaram a substituir seus iPhones por novas unidades por acreditarem que as reinicializações poderiam estar relacionadas a um defeito físico. No entanto, a troca não deve ser necessária, já que a empresa confirmou uma correção por software.
A Apple não informou exatamente o que provoca o bug, mas os iPhone 18 Pro e 18 Pro Max estrearam uma versão redesenhada do sistema Face ID. A câmera infravermelha passou a ficar posicionada sob a parte inferior da tela, perto da região ocupada pelo relógio na barra de status. A mudança permitiu reduzir em 25% o tamanho da Ilha Dinâmica.

articles.title: The 2026 Disney+ and Hulu price increase has arrived — and Disney claims it's necessary to 'invest in enhancements' for its streaming platforms and 'strengthen the value we deliver to subscribers'
articles.text:
The cost of Disney+ and Hulu is going up again — but Disney argues 'we are preserving a high-value option for subscribers' as it freezes the price on three of its streaming bundles
- Disney has confirmed new price hikes for Disney+ and Hulu in the US
- However, the cost of three bundles has been frozen
- Fans in the UK, Europe, and Australia won't be affected for the time being
Disney has confirmed price hikes for all but three of its standalone Disney+ and Hulu plans, and bundles including both platforms, in the US — but there's no word on when other nations might be hit by similar rises.
Yesterday (September 23), Bloomberg reported that the entertainment giant was about to increase the cost of signing up for a subscription for the sixth time in as many years.
Per Bloomberg's sources, the biggest markup would see the Hulu-Disney+ Premium (ad-free) bundle go up by 13% to $21.49 per month. That means new and current users would have to pay an additional $2.50 every 30 days. Meanwhile, the cost of numerous other standalone tiers and bundles would go up by as little as $0.50 or as much as $3.00.
Approached by TechRadar for comment, Disney acknowledged that Bloomberg's report was factual.
However, a studio rep was keen to stress that three of its bundles, including its cheapest offering — the Hulu-Disney+ bundle (with ads) experience — would not be subject to price increases.
"While competitors have raised prices by an average of 13% this year, we are keeping the price of our most popular bundle unchanged and have increased our standalone ad-supported offerings by just 4%," a Disney spokesperson told me.
"We continue to significantly invest in enhancements to Disney+ — new technology, features, and personalization. These improvements continue to strengthen the value we deliver to subscribers and will culminate in the one app experience later this year."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
For reference, here's a full breakdown of every price rise or freeze across Disney's myriad streaming service offerings in the US:
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle (with ads) — staying flat at $12.99
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium (ad free) — increasing +$2 to $21.99
- Disney+ and Hulu standalone plans (with ads) — increasing +$0.50 to $12.49
- Disney+ and Hulu Premium standalone plans (ad free) — increasing +$2.50 to $21.49
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle (with ads) — increasing +$2 to $21.99
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle Premium (ad free) — increasing +$3 to $32.99
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle (with ads) — staying flat at $35.99
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle Premium (ad free) — staying flat at $44.99
Why the UK, Europe, and Australia is immune to the Disney+ price hike — for now
Crucially, UK and European subscribers appear to be temporarily immune to these price increases.
Responding to a separate request for comment from TechRadar, a Disney+ UK spokesperson told me: "We don't have anything to share on UK or European pricing at this time."
However, in previous years, UK and European fans have seen the cost of Disney+ climb just weeks after their US counterparts were slapped with the now-annual price hike. I wouldn't be stunned, then, if account holders in these regions are forced to pay more for two of the world's best streaming services in the weeks ahead.
Australian Disney+ users were hit by a price hike in April, so it's unlikely — but not completely out of the question — that they'll experience another one in due course.
Regardless of whether you've been hit by this latest price hike, it's been a rough few days for Disney+ users all around.
The week began with Disney having to placate furious fans over inaccurate reports that its ad-free Disney+ tiers would start showing ads. The dust hadn't settled on that story before fans learned that Marvel TV show Daredevil: Born Again would end after its forthcoming third season on Disney+, too.
I'm not superstitious but, as the saying goes, bad news comes in threes. Let's hope that this is the third and final piece of unwelcome news that Disney fans have to deal for a while, then.

articles.title: Meta's Muse Charm looks like a Tamagotchi, but it's tapping into a much newer trend | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Is Meta’s just-announced Muse Charm a playful device that will make AI more approachable to everyday consumers, or will it be yet another flop in a long list of AI hardware gadgets that didn’t take off, like the AI Pin, Rabbit, or Friend pendant? Reactions, so far, have been mixed. What the Charm is, however, is on-trend.
Like it or not, the form factor could potentially appeal to Gen Z consumers who, in this post-Labubu era, have already been into various dangling items from keychains and bags. It’s all part of a broader kitschy, retro-inspired shift in their approach to fashion and technology.
Already, Gen Z has created a market for things that dangle, with everything from lip glosses to hand sanitizers to sunblocks to fragrances and more turned into bag charms, primarily targeted at women.
Hailey Bieber’s viral Rhode lip case, which stuck the lip gloss onto a phone case, had a big influence on this idea that beauty products could also be fashion accessories, as did its other beauty-focused bag charms. (The brand saw $212 million in annual net sales from a lineup of roughly 10 products, Vogue noted last year, as the company announced its billion-dollar exit to Elf Beauty.)
Then there was the Labubu craze, which saw sales of the so-ugly-it’s-cute fuzzy monster bag charm explode, growing Pop Mart (the Chinese retailer behind the product)’s revenue to $1.8 billion in 2024, a 7x jump from 2019. While demand for the Labubu itself has since faded, the concept of the decorative bag charm has not. One analyst firm estimates the global bag charm market will grow to over $1 billion by 2030.
Today, bag charms can be characters, bedazzled beauty products, or other whimsical designs or objects, like Coach’s coveted cherry charms, a Gen Z favorite. They’ve proven popular because they’re a means of expressing your personality, just as humans have done for ages through their fashion choices, makeup, and jewelry.
Similarly, Meta’s Muse is a customizable character; you design your own avatar, which makes the AI agent a reflection of you, too.
And, as many have pointed out, Muse Charm’s form factor recalls a Tamagotchi, the pocket-sized digital virtual pet that became a major toy fad in the late 90s and again in the mid-2000s.
However, the Tamagotchi is not the most current reference. It seems the Muse Charm is actually a twist on what some young people are already doing with their Apple Watch. Often meant as a way to repurpose an older device, the concept of the Apple Watch keychain or charm has been growing in popularity, fueled by TikTok videos showing different ways to use the watch when not on your wrist.
On retailers like Amazon and Walmart, and marketplaces like eBay and Etsy, there are thousands of Apple Watch keychains, straps, pendants, lanyards, clips, and bag charm cases now available in nearly every style you can think of. As you might expect, these keychain watches are often being adopted by younger women as a fashion accessory first, rather than a piece of technology.
This all then intersects with the broader retro-tech trend, which has seen older tech like digital cameras, flip phones, iPods, CDs, cassette tapes, home phones, and wired earbuds making a quiet comeback.
This vibe shift in tech comes as young people describe the addictive, algorithm-driven feeds and “soulness” nature of technology as making them feel more disconnected, which has also fed into this trend of wanting tech they can touch and feel. (One startup, Clicks, is even bringing back the physical phone keyboard in a BlackBerry-inspired device, for instance.)
For Gen Z, these physical objects help them feel more connected with the technology they’re using and offer a sense of control over a world where technology has become so deeply integrated into our lives that it no longer feels like a choice to use it.
Young women, again, have been at the forefront of this trend, with some even crafting their own portable, mini computers, “cyberdecks,” which they fit inside clamshell purses or custom cases, and bedazzle with jewels, flowers, stickers, pearls, and other items to make them feel more personal.
That brings us back to the Muse Charm. While it’s clearly designed with the tech-as-fashion-accessory trend in mind, that doesn’t mean it will be a hit.
Meta has abused consumer trust over the years to such an extent that it may never fully recover.
To name just a few examples: the tech giant had to settle with the FTC over charges that it deceived consumers by making users’ private information public without their consent, and has been penalized by the FTC for numerous privacy-related violations. In 2023, the FTC charged Meta with violating a privacy order that was filed after the 2019 settlement. It’s also been repeatedly hauled before Congress over its harms to minors, has lost or settled multiple lawsuits over the same topics, and has seen various whistleblowers outing its abuses.
These careless privacy practices could ultimately see Meta lose the battle to be the consumer AI of choice…unless, of course, consumers decide that the “devil you know” is better than the one you don’t. (Especially when the latter are those warning AI will could put an end to the human race).
Meta’s end game, after all, is highly-targeted, highly-personalized ads. If that’s the privacy tradeoff in gaining access to free AI — Meta said it will monetize Muse by taking a small fee from transactions — consumers could be willing to take the risk.

articles.title: Mistral investit des millions pour racheter...une boite de pub
articles.text:
Mistral a annoncé le rachat de Pimento, une start-up parisienne qui génère des publicités par intelligence artificielle. Il s'agit de la troisième acquisition de l'entreprise française cette année, quelques semaines après une levée de fonds de 3 milliards d'euros.
L'opération a d'abord été révélée par le média L'Informé, avant que Mistral ne la confirme à l'AFP pour un montant de "plusieurs millions d'euros". Les deux entreprises n'en ont pas dit plus sur le prix exact de la transaction.
Des développeurs recherchés plus qu'un portefeuille de marques
Les salariés de Pimento rejoignent les équipes produit et ingénierie de Mistral, où ils travailleront sur Vibe, l'assistant conversationnel de l'entreprise, anciennement appelé Le Chat. Le cofondateur de Pimento, Florent Facq, a précisé sur LinkedIn que son équipe se concentrerait sur l'amélioration de l'expérience utilisateur de cet outil. Une source proche du dossier a indiqué à L'Informé que Mistral s'intéressait davantage aux compétences techniques de ces développeurs qu'à l'activité commerciale de Pimento. Bon, a priori donc, pas de pub à venir dans vos conversations…
Pimento propose un logiciel qui transforme un brief marketing, une charte graphique et des données de campagne en visuels publicitaires et en courtes animations destinées aux réseaux sociaux. Plus de 180 marques utilisent actuellement cet outil. La start-up a été fondée en octobre 2022 par Florent Facq (ancien directeur produit du Pass Culture) et Tomás Yany (passé par Apple puis Nabla). Initialement, elle proposait un outil de moodboarding pour aider les équipes créatives à cadrer leurs idées avant de les transformer en publicités.
Le montant du rachat reste flou. L'Informé évoque environ 3,8 millions d'euros. Sifted, qui a consulté des documents liés à l'opération, avance de son côté 12,7 millions d'euros, en cash et en actions Mistral. On imagine que cette énorme différence s'explique par la prise en compte, ou non, d'actions comptabilisées dans le calcul. La start-up avait pour sa part levé 3 millions d'euros en 2023 auprès de Partech et Cygni Capital, avec Julien Chaumond (cofondateur de Hugging Face) et Stanislas Polu (cofondateur de Dust) parmi les investisseurs individuels.
Rappelons qu'en février dernier, Mistral a effectué le rachat de Koyeb, une plateforme cloud utilisée pour son infrastructure de calcul, puis celui d'Emmi AI en mai, une entreprise autrichienne spécialisée dans la simulation physique pour l'industrie. Elle intervient aussi après une levée de fonds de 3 milliards d'euros début septembre, menée par Samsung Electronics, qui porte la valorisation de Mistral au-dessus de 21 milliards d'euros. Ni Mistral ni Pimento n'ont précisé ce que deviendra l'outil publicitaire existant, ni les données des marques qui continuent de l'utiliser.

articles.title: Premier couac cyber pour Muse : Meta a corrigé en urgence une faille de son agent IA
articles.text:
« S’il vous plaît, ne l’installez pas ! » Voici les premiers mots du message d’alerte de Patrick Wardle.
Publié sur X ce lundi 21 septembre, ce fil reprend l’annonce de lancement de Mark Zuckerberg pour alerter sur un manquement à la sécurité de Muse, le nouvel agent personnel de Meta présenté le 8 septembre.
Disponible sur Mac, l’application permet de réserver des rendez-vous, de remplir des formulaires, d’effectuer des achats, et se branche sur WhatsApp, la messagerie, le calendrier ou les réseaux sociaux de l’utilisateur.
Pour fonctionner, elle réclame aussi de larges autorisations sur la machine, du micro à la caméra en passant par la localisation et l’écriture de fichiers. Patrick Wardle alerte justement sur ces accès.
Un réglage de développement resté en production
Le problème tient à un paramètre non documenté, baptisé endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint. Il indique à Muse vers quel serveur envoyer la voix de l’utilisateur quand il dicte une requête, car la transcription se fait dans le cloud de Meta.
Ce réglage est stocké dans les préférences locales de l’application, que n’importe quel programme lancé sous le compte de l’utilisateur peut modifier sans autorisation particulière. Sa preuve de concept pilote plus de 50 commandes de Muse, pour la plupart anodines selon lui.
Il suffit donc, explique-t-il, de rediriger ce paramètre vers un serveur contrôlé par un attaquant pour qu’à la prochaine dictée, ce dernier puisse récupérer l’enregistrement audio, glisser ses propres instructions que l’agent exécutera, et surtout intercepter le jeton d’authentification du compte.
« On peut manipuler l’agent et utiliser ses privilèges pour faire ce qu’on veut », a expliqué le chercheur à Ars Technica.
L’attaquant récupère alors tout ce que l’utilisateur a confié à Muse : messages, e-mails, comptes en ligne. Wardle a publié une preuve de concept sur GitHub et affirme avoir réussi, lors de ses tests, à écrire des fichiers sur le disque ou à prendre des photos, souvent sans que l’utilisateur remarque quoi que ce soit.
Une attaque locale, mais à portée d’arnaque
Reste que, pour exploiter la faille, un code malveillant doit déjà tourner sur le Mac. Un obstacle facile à franchir selon Wardle, pour qui une simple variante de ClickFix suffit à l’y introduire. Cette technique d’ingénierie sociale, devenue redoutablement efficace, consiste à convaincre la victime de coller elle-même une commande dans son terminal.
Le chercheur reproche plus généralement à Meta d’avoir choisi une dictée dans le cloud, alors que macOS propose une transcription directement sur l’appareil qui aurait fermé cette voie d’attaque.
De son côté, David Singleton, de la division Meta Superintelligence Labs, a confirmé la faille et annoncé sur X un correctif d’urgence pour l’application Mac, ce mardi 22 septembre. L’entreprise précise que ce réglage servait au débogage et au développement, et indique que le patch le supprime purement et simplement des versions de production. Meta qualifie néanmoins la faille d’élévation de privilèges locale, et non d’exploit à distance, et juge le risque pratique « assez faible ».

articles.title: „Wechselstationen finde ich genug“: Warum Afrikas öffentlicher Verkehr mit Austausch-Akkus fährt
articles.text:
Wie ausgewechselt: Warum Afrikas Lieferfahrer und Taxis elektrisch fahren
Clinton Landon hält mit seinem elektrischen Motorrad vor einem Schrank, der an eine Paketstation erinnert. Er öffnet eine Klappe an der Tankattrappe seines Motorrads, nimmt eine Batterie heraus, scannt den QR-Code am Schrank und eine der Türen springt auf. Nachdem Landon seine Batterie hineingesteckt hat, öffnet sich eine weitere Tür mit einem vollgeladenen Stromspeicher. Das Ganze wiederholt er mit der zweiten Batterie. „Das dauert nur ein paar Minuten“, sagt Landon zufrieden, „dann kann ich weiterfahren.“
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 7/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns damit, wie KI die IT-Sicherheit auf den Kopf stellt. Das Heft erscheint am 25.9.2026 im Zeitschriftenhandel.
Landon arbeitet in der kenianischen Hauptstadt Nairobi als „Rider“, als Zweirad-Taxi-Fahrer und Lieferant für zwei unterschiedliche Fahrdienstvermittler. Seine Gewinnmargen sind gering, die Arbeitstage sowieso lang, jede Zeitverschwendung ist bitter. Auf das Laden seiner Motorradbatterie warten? Kann sich Landon nicht leisten.
    
40.000 Elektrofahrzeuge: Zahl der Stromer explodiert
Vor rund einem Jahr ist er von einem Verbrenner auf ein elektrisches Modell mit Wechselbatterien umgestiegen. Die Betriebskosten für seinen Verbrenner verschlangen einen Großteil seiner Einnahmen. Das war noch lange vor dem drastischen Anstieg der Treibstoffpreise infolge des Irankriegs. Von mehreren Kollegen hörte er damals, dass ihnen mit Elektromotorrädern viel mehr vom täglichen Umsatz blieb als ihm mit seinem Verbrenner. Landon beschloss, ihrem Beispiel zu folgen. Mit seiner Entscheidung ist er bis heute zufrieden. „Das E-Bike ist wirtschaftlicher, es ist komfortabel, und Wechselstationen finde ich genug.“
Landon liegt mit seiner Entscheidung voll im Trend: Nach Angaben des Branchenverbandes Electric Mobility Association of Kenya (EMAK) ist die Zahl der Elektrofahrzeuge im Land in wenigen Jahren geradezu explodiert. Von etwa 700 Fahrzeugen im Jahr 2022 stieg sie bis heute auf rund 40.000. Etwa neunzig Prozent davon sind Motorräder, rund zwei Prozent Busse oder Minibusse, der Rest PKW. Jedes sechste neu zugelassene Motorrad ist mittlerweile elektrisch. Es werden vor allem die Fahrzeuge elektrifiziert, mit denen die Menschen Geld verdienen: Motorradtaxis und Liefermotorräder (Boda-Bodas), motorisierte Dreiräder (Tuk-Tuks) sowie Busse, also im Grunde der öffentliche Verkehr.
