articles.title: Humble Hope Foundation takes grassroots healthcare and livelihoods to Pulwama
articles.text:
Humble Hope Foundation takes grassroots healthcare and livelihoods to Pulwama
Humble Hope Foundation works across healthcare, child protection, mental health and livelihoods to support underserved communities in Pulwama.
For Humble Hope Foundation, community work begins with finding people who may otherwise remain outside the reach of essential services. The non-profit organisation works across child protection, healthcare, mental health, disability inclusion and livelihoods, with a focus on underserved communities in Jammu and Kashmir.
Founded by Ashiq Hussain, a psychologist, along with Co-Founder and Director Rubeena Ali, the foundation works with children, women, youth, persons with disabilities, older people and vulnerable families.
Its approach is built around identifying a need, connecting people with an appropriate service or government scheme, and following up to see whether the support reaches them.
One of its key interventions has been child protection. Humble Hope identified 54 Children in Need of Care and Protection and facilitated their linkage with the Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship Scheme. Under the applicable sponsorship support, the children receive Rs 4,000 per month for areas including education, nutrition and healthcare.
The work received an appreciation certificate from the administration through the Child Welfare Committee in Pulwama.
Taking mental health support into villages
Mental health and psychosocial support is another area where the organisation has focused on early awareness.
Since 2025, Humble Hope has conducted 37 awareness camps across 37 villages in Pulwama. The sessions help parents and caregivers recognise behavioural and emotional changes, understand referral options and address the stigma around mental health.
The foundation also participates in the government's Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, including the 100 Days Nasha Mukt Abhiyaan. Its team conducts awareness activities with students in government and private educational institutions, focusing on prevention, early intervention and informed choices.
The organisation combines these programmes with community activities around child rights, adolescent health, women's empowerment and environmental awareness.
From health camps to livelihood support
Healthcare remains a significant part of its grassroots work.
Humble Hope has organised 12 eye-screening camps across Pulwama and Shopian, screening 1,589 outpatient patients. A total of 108 people were referred for advanced treatment and cataract surgery, while 118 were referred to ASG Eye Hospital, where referred patients received surgical treatment.
The camps have particularly focused on older people and those facing financial, physical or geographical barriers to healthcare.
The foundation has also worked on disability inclusion through a Cutting and Tailoring Training Centre established in Pulwama in collaboration with Chinar International and with support from SIDBI.
Twenty physically challenged youth received training, while seven beneficiaries, including two women, received tailoring and overlock machines to support self-employment.
Building a community network
More than 50 volunteers support Humble Hope's work, from beneficiary identification and health camps to awareness programmes, documentation and follow-up.
The organisation's leadership team includes Danish Ahmad Pala, Secretary and a clinical psychology professional; Dr Arshid, Manager; and Fida Mohammad Bhat, Accountant.
Its programme areas now span child protection, mental health, healthcare, eye care, education, disability inclusion, youth and skills, livelihoods, drug abuse prevention, climate and environment, digital literacy and community development.
The foundation's next phase is focused on moving from individual interventions towards community programmes that can be piloted, documented, measured, improved and scaled.
For Humble Hope, that means measuring more than the number of people reached. The organisation's stated focus is on what changes afterwards, whether that means a child accessing protection, a patient receiving treatment, a young person gaining a livelihood or a family finding support before a problem becomes a crisis.

articles.title: Couverture 5G : SFR s'empare de la première place, mais les opérateurs sont au coude-à-coude
articles.text:
Ce classement a été dévoilé ce jeudi 24 septembre en exclusivité par DegroupTest, avant sa mise en ligne complète par nPerf ce vendredi 25 septembre. Il montre surtout que les quatre opérateurs sont désormais au coude-à-coude : 1,27 point sépare SFR d’Orange, contre 11,51 points dans l’édition 2024. Vous hésitez entre deux forfaits 5G ? La couverture 5G nationale ne vous aidera pas beaucoup à choisir.
nPerf est une société française qui édite une application de test de débit. Son baromètre repose sur des mesures relevées sur le terrain par ses utilisateurs de smartphones Android. Les cartes de couverture publiées par les opérateurs sont, elles, simulées par ordinateur.
Le score final fait la moyenne de deux indicateurs : la part du territoire où les abonnés ont capté la 5G, et la part de la population couverte en mobilité. SFR arrive premier avec 72,78 %, devant Bouygues Telecom (72,34 %), Free (71,55 %) et Orange (71,51 %).
Le détail est plus nuancé. SFR a la meilleure couverture géographique (58,62 %), mais le plus faible score sur la population (86,94 %). Free présente le profil inverse : dernier sur le territoire (54,49 %), premier sur la population (88,61 %).
Pour la rentrée, BNP Paribas propose une offre de bienvenue étudiante avec carte Visa incluse, paiements sans frais à l’étranger, prêt à 0,99% et jusqu’à 175€ d’avantages offerts (80€ offerts + 1 an gratuit à Esprit Libre).
Orange reste quatrième, mais il revient de loin : son score a grimpé de 23,13 points depuis 2024, la plus forte hausse des quatre. Attention toutefois, cela ne veut pas dire qu’Orange couvre 23 % de territoire en plus. L’indicateur ne porte en effet que sur les zones fréquentées par ses propres abonnés.
Surtout, ce baromètre dit seulement si la 5G est présente. nPerf prend en compte toutes les bandes de fréquences, y compris le 700 MHz, qui porte loin mais offre des débits plus faibles que le 3,5 GHz, la bande des hauts débits. Être couvert en 5G ne garantit donc pas une connexion rapide. Si l’on y regarde de plus près, Orange est l’opérateur qui couvre plus la 5G en 3,5 GHz avec 14 302 sites répertoriés sur mon réseaumobilearcep.
Débits et qualité d’appel : Bouygues en tête
Pour les performances, il faut regarder un autre classement de nPerf, publié en janvier 2026 et qui porte sur toute l’année 2025. Bouygues Telecom y a pris la première place. Le même prestataire publie aussi chaque année un classement des fournisseurs d’internet fixe.
L’Arcep, le gendarme des télécoms, mesure elle-même la qualité des réseaux chaque été. Sa dernière campagne, publiée ce même 24 septembre 2026 met en avant d’autres données.
Orange y domine au niveau national. 91 % de ses appels sont en qualité parfaite, c’est-à-dire maintenus deux minutes sans perturbation audible. Bouygues Telecom suit avec 88 %, SFR avec 87 % et Free avec 84 %.
Hors des villes, l’écart grandit. En zones rurales, Orange réussit 83 % d’appels parfaits, contre 76 à 79 % pour les trois autres. Dans les TGV, il maintient 74 % des appels, contre 61 % pour Free, 58 % pour Bouygues Telecom et 56 % pour SFR.
En revanche, Bouygues Telecom fait jeu égal avec Orange en zones denses : 96 % d’appels parfaits contre 95 %, un écart que l’Arcep classe dans la marge d’erreur. Sur l’internet mobile en ville, il passe devant tout le monde au seuil de 3 Mbit/s, le minimum pour naviguer sur le web. Il fait aussi jeu égal avec Orange aux seuils de 8 et 30 Mbit/s, ceux du streaming vidéo et des usages professionnels.
Vérifiez la couverture là où vous vivez
Région par région, les écarts redeviennent nets. DegroupTest a calculé plus de 22 points d’écart entre le meilleur et le moins bon opérateur en Normandie, et plus de 21 points en Bretagne. Dans 9 des 13 régions étudiées par nPerf, l’écart dépasse 10 points.
Pas de panique, l’Arcep propose un outil gratuit pour vérifier chez vous. Lancé en septembre 2017, Mon réseau mobile compare la couverture des quatre opérateurs là où vous vivez et sur vos trajets, en métropole comme en outre-mer. La carte affiche aussi les points de mesure réels de l’Arcep, colorés selon le débit relevé, de moins de 3 Mbit/s à plus de 30 Mbit/s.
Nous vous recommandons de regarder les zones où vous passez le plus de temps : domicile, travail et trajets. Si vous prenez souvent le train ou vivez à la campagne, Orange garde l’avantage dans les mesures de l’Arcep. En ville, Bouygues Telecom fait jeu égal avec lui. La campagne 2026 de l’Arcep n’est pas encore publiée : l’édition 2025 était sortie le 20 novembre.

articles.title: What Is JSA Construction Software and Why Every Site Needs It - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- JSA construction software helps you complete job safety analysis faster and keep job safety records current on active sites.
- It supports hazard identification by guiding teams through each job step and matching risks with control measures.
- Digital JSA software reduces lost paper forms, delays, and messy safety analysis handovers between crews.
- Mobile access lets team members create, review, sign, and update safety documentation on site.
- Built-in templates, checklists, and review flows improve consistency across construction sites in Australia.
- Better records and clearer safety processes help support workplace safety, compliance, and safer work every day.
Introduction
JSA construction software lets you do job safety analysis faster. You don’t need to chase paperwork across the site. Your team can handle job safety, updates, and sign-offs in one digital tool. This is good for construction safety because risks can change quickly. Your safety documentation can keep up and be ready in time.
Understanding JSA Construction Software for Australian Sites
JSA construction software lets you write down how a job will be done in a safe manner. The main aim of a job safety analysis is to split work into small steps, find things that may harm people, and list control measures before you start working.
On construction sites in Australia, this makes safety documentation clearer. It also helps make sure that how you plan to do the job matches what happens on site. The JSA construction software guides you, keeps job safety records, and lets you update these records quickly when site conditions change.
What Is a Job Safety Analysis (JSA) in Construction?
A job safety analysis identifies risks before starting a task by breaking the work into steps, considering potential hazards, and choosing the safest methods.
This process becomes part of your overall safety program. For example, when installing framing, the analysis covers lifting materials, working near edges, and using tools safely.
The main goal is to ensure everyone knows the job, understands the risks, and uses proper controls before work begins. Software streamlines this by making job safety analysis a repeatable routine for all.
How JSA Construction Software Streamlines the JSA Process
Manual forms make the JSA process slow. A digital tool guides you from draft to review, and stores completed safety documents in one place, reducing paperwork time.
A typical software flow:
- Start with a template.
- Adjust hazards and controls for the task.
- Review, submit, and sign on your phone.
This is the main advantage over paper: less time rewriting forms, more time ensuring control measures fit the job.
Why Construction Sites Are Moving Away from Paper-Based JSAs
Paper forms often get lost in utes, site sheds, or the wrong folder. On busy construction sites, this can slow down job safety steps and make it hard to know which safety analysis form is up to date.
Digital systems help to fix this problem. When a job safety analysis can be made, changed, and signed right from a phone, people are less likely to miss updates or use out-of-date paperwork. This keeps job safety strong on the site.
Common Challenges with Traditional Job Safety Analysis Methods
Traditional work methods create challenges for crews and safety managers. Paper forms are hard to read, easy to lose, and slow to share—especially when plans change.
Common problems include:
- Delays in hazard identification due to missing forms.
- Safety documents scattered across multiple folders.
- Slow approvals that stall the JSA process.
A frequent issue arises when subcontractors bring outdated paper forms. If new hazards exist, teams may begin work without reviewing or acknowledging updated controls.
Main Benefits of Using Digital JSA Construction Software
Digital JSA construction software speeds up processes, provides clearer oversight, and ensures consistency. It enhances workplace safety by making critical information accessible to the right people at the right time.
Key benefits:
- Faster completion with guided templates and fields
- Easy updates to control measures
- Better crew access through mobile-first tools
- Clearer records for safety audits
Most importantly, it saves valuable time. With less admin work, teams can focus on the job site, supporting crews, and ensuring safety controls are followed.
Core Features to Look for in JSA Construction Software
If you are picking job safety analysis software, look for the features that fix problems on site. Don’t be distracted by cool extras that you don’t need. The right digital tool will let your team make, check, update, and find safety documents fast.
Look for:
- Editable templates for different trades and tasks
- Hazard and control libraries so crews aren’t starting from scratch
- Mobile sign-off for review and submission on site
- Version control so everyone works from the current form
- Central storage for easy access during audits
- Offline access for areas with poor reception
Good job hazard analysis software should fit in with how your people already do things. This is very important if you have more than one subcontractor or you run many jobs at the same time.
How JSA Construction Software Improves Site Safety and Compliance
Job safety analysis software helps make construction safety better by making safety protocols simple to follow and show. This is important in the construction industry because lost or old records can lead to big risks.
The software also makes it easier for the team to follow the rules, as all documents will be kept, checked, and changed in a more careful way. When safety processes are clear, people in the team are more likely to do the job the right way.
Conclusion
JSA construction software is essential for modern construction sites, improving job safety and streamlining workflows. Switching from paper to digital tools speeds up safety analysis and boosts productivity while helping teams comply with Australian safety regulations. The software offers digital templates and mobile access, enabling workers to identify and manage risks efficiently on site. As the industry evolves, digital tools safeguard your team and keep projects running smoothly. Make your site safer—try our free trial today!
Frequently Asked Questions
What’s the difference between JSA and SWMS, and when is each used in Australia?
A job safety analysis (JSA) reviews a task, listing steps, hazards, and controls. A safe work method statement (SWMS) is legally required for high-risk construction work—like falls over 2 metres or demolition of load-bearing structures—under WHS Regulations in most Australian states and territories. It must be prepared before work begins. Victoria uses its own OHS Act, so check requirements separately. JSAs are more flexible and can be used for any task. Teams often use both: SWMS for mandated high-risk activities, JSAs for other tasks.
Is JSA construction software suitable for small projects or subcontractors?
Yes, JSA software is useful for small projects too. It streamlines paperwork, speeds up sign-offs, and keeps all safety records organised. Subcontractors benefit from a mobile tool that provides quick access to information on site as they move between jobs.

articles.title: Google Maps vient de changer sa manière d'afficher les intersections
articles.text:
Conduire dans un endroit que vous ne connaissez pas peut parfois donner des sueurs froides, surtout lorsqu’un stop ou un feu tricolore se cache derrière un virage. Conscient du problème, Google déploie une mise à jour de Maps qui vient simplifier la lecture des intersections sur l’application, mais aussi sur Android Auto.
Des indications plus lisibles pour anticiper les intersections
Cela fait déjà six ans que Google Maps place sur la carte des repères pour les feux tricolores et de stops, mais ils s’affichaient jusqu’alors uniquement sous la forme d’icônes fixes qui ne permettaient pas d’anticiper au mieux. Désormais, un nouveau système de pop-up vient s’afficher juste à côté du nom de la rue que vous devez emprunter lors de votre prochain changement de direction.
Cette nouvelle intégration rend l’information immédiatement plus claire et permet de garder les yeux sur la route tout en ayant un maximum d’informations rapidement. Le repère indique précisément si un feu rouge ou un stop vous attend au bout du virage, ce qui offre une indication simple et efficace pour lever le pied à l’approche d’une intersection délicate.
Un déploiement progressif pour tous les automobilistes
Repérée cette semaine, la nouveauté s’invite d’abord sur les interfaces Android Auto, mais elle commence également à apparaître directement sur les smartphones, ce qui laisse penser qu’une compatibilité avec les utilisateurs d’iPhone via CarPlay pourrait arriver par la suite.
À lire : Android Auto : le compteur de vitesse de Google Maps ne s’affiche qu’à une condition
Comme c’est souvent le cas pour les services de Google, le déploiement s’effectue côté serveur. Il faudra donc patienter de quelques jours à quelques semaines pour que l’ensemble des conducteurs profite de ce nouvel affichage sur leur tableau de bord ou leur téléphone. Pas mal, non ?

articles.title: Le blender Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU nous a surpris par sa puissance et son intelligence : notre verdict complet
articles.text:
| Chauffant | Non | 
| Nombre de vitesses | 10 | 
| Mode pulse ou turbo | Oui | 
| Capacité du bol | 1.8 L | 
| Puissance | 1200 W | 
| Matière du bol | Plastique | 
| Lames amovibles | Oui | 
| Dimensions (LxHxP) | 21 x 44.5 x 17.5 cm | 
| Garantie | 2 an(s) | 
Le blender Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU se destine à la pulvérisation des aliments grâce à son moteur surpuissant et sa triple paire de lames. Il compte aussi sur de nombreux accessoires pour assurer sa polyvalence.
C'est un euphémisme que de dire que le blender Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU paraît particulièrement bien équipé pour assurer sa mission en cuisine. Sous sa coque noire (Ninja oblige), il dissimule un moteur de 1200 W qui entraîne non pas une ni deux, mais trois paires de lames placées les unes en dessous des autres. Un moyen simple pour être sûr que tous les ingrédients rencontreront bien les éléments coupants pendant la préparation pour être hachés menu.
Pour maîtriser cet outillage, le fabricant a prévu un mode manuel (10 vitesses), mais aussi de nombreux programmes automatiques. Plus original, un mode Blend Sense adapte tout seul la vitesse de rotation des lames selon le type d'ingrédients présents dans le (grand) bol en plastique de 2,1 l. Précisons d'ailleurs que le carton contient, outre cette carafe principale, trois gourdes pour une dégustation nomade, qu'on peut équiper d'un couteau pour mixer et emporter sa boisson dans la foulée. Enfin, on retrouve une cuve de robot de cuisine munie d'un disque de découpe adéquat pour faciliter la préparation du repas, mais aussi une lame à pétrir pour réaliser sans peine ses pâtes à pain ou à pizza.
Si l'ensemble a été lancé à 249 €, on peut aujourd'hui le trouver, sans grande difficulté, pour un peu plus de 200 €.
Quand on le déballe, le Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU fait plutôt bonne impression, malgré un plastique qui règne en maître. Ainsi, son bloc-moteur est-il entièrement recouvert d'une coque en plastique, alors que nous aurions préféré ici des matériaux un peu plus nobles, comme ce que propose le Magimix Power 5 Connect et sa carrosserie tout en métal.
La large carafe de 2,1 l (1,9 l de volume utile) est, elle aussi, en plastique, ce qui permet néanmoins de limiter son poids. Car le Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU est un mastodonte qui prend beaucoup de place sur le plan de travail : 20 cm de largeur, 20 cm de profondeur et surtout 45 cm de hauteur avec le bol ! Attention donc à sa manipulation en présence de meubles au-dessus du plan de travail.
Comme souvent, un ensemble de ventouses sous le bloc-moteur a pour mission de maintenir le blender en place, même pendant un mixage prolongé à la vitesse maximale. Ce quatuor remplit sa fonction avec brio, peut-être même un peu trop efficacement. En effet, en raison du poids du blender, l'accroche est immédiate. En cas de mauvais placement, ou quand on le sort de son placard pour l'utiliser, il va falloir tirer fort sur l'appareil pour l'arracher du plan de travail ou de l'endroit où on l'a rangé.
De son côté, le bol est particulièrement bien conçu. Nous l'avons dit, il est en plastique et ne pèse que 1,37 kg quand certains modèles en verre dépassent allègrement les 2 kg. Et si cela n'a l'air de rien, votre poignet vous le rappellera quand vous préparerez un smoothie pour toute la famille et qu'il faudra servir les verres en rafale.
En dehors de ce poids relativement convenu, le bol du Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU fait aussi la part belle à la sécurité. Si le couvercle n'est pas parfaitement positionné, il est impossible de lancer un mixage. Autre astuce intéressante, il suffit de relever la partie noire prenant la forme d'une anse pour libérer le mécanisme de blocage et retirer ledit couvercle sans aucun effort. Enfin, le bec verseur nous a semblé particulièrement efficace, même si le capuchon qui empêche les liquides de ressortir par l'orifice de distribution est parfois dur à relever.
On n'hésitera d'ailleurs pas à utiliser cet orifice de distribution pour le service et on évitera à tout prix d'ôter le couvercle pour verser la préparation hors du bol. En effet, le couteau n'est pas fixé à ce dernier de quelque façon que ce soit, comme c'est le cas sur l'immense majorité des blenders du marché. Il est simplement posé sur l'arbre de transmission, à la base, et une empreinte dans le couvercle maintient l'ensemble de la pièce en place, même si celle-ci tourne à grande vitesse. Vous l'aurez deviné, en ôtant le couvercle, on libère le couteau qui va irrémédiablement choir si on fait pencher le bol (et si on ne l'a pas retiré auparavant) pour servir un verre.
Justicia ! Droitiers et gauchers sont traités sur un pied d'égalité puisqu'on peut placer l'anse de la carafe vers la droite ou la gauche. Il faut cependant croire que les Étasuniens (et les Britanniques) sont plutôt droitiers et le reste du monde plutôt gaucher, car les unités de mesure sérigraphiées sur la paroi en plastique ne sont pas les mêmes selon la position de la poignée : impériales (la bonne blague…) quand l'anse est tournée vers la droite, métriques (la bonne science…) quand elle pointe vers la gauche.
Les gourdes de mixage et de transport sont bien moins remarquables. Assez banales, elles ne sont pourvues d'aucun système facilitant la vie du fan de smoothie en promenade, comme une poignée de transport ou un petit trou au-dessus de l'orifice de dégustation pour éviter les vides d'air et ainsi fluidifier l'ingestion… Elles atteignent néanmoins un volume confortable de 700 ml, à relativiser puisque plus elles peuvent contenir, plus elles sont lourdes et plus elles sont compliquées à caser dans un sac à dos.
media id="1247169" alt="Ninja Detect 1200W TB401EU" align="center" copyright="Les Numériques" watermark="yes" exif="no"]Un panneau de commandes clair comme de l'eau de roche.[/media]
Après avoir rempli le bol, bien fermé le couvercle et positionné le tout sur le bloc-moteur, on peut passer au mixage des aliments. Le panneau de commandes du Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU n'est pas bien compliqué à maîtriser, même si l'utilisateur dispose de trois méthodes d'utilisation, à sélectionner en appuyant sur l'un des trois boutons situés entre la carafe et la large molette.
Les moins à l'aise avec l'usage d'un blender se tourneront vers la fonction BlendSense dont le principe ne saurait être plus simple. On introduit les aliments dans le bol, on appuie sur le bouton central de la molette pour laisser le Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU décider de la vitesse des lames. Bon point, on suit les étapes de la préparation grâce aux indications lumineuses de la molette sans avoir rien à faire. D'un seul coup d'œil, on sait si le Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU analyse les ingrédients, adapte sa vitesse…
Si cela ne convenait pas, on peut se tourner vers l'un des trois modes automatiques : Mince (émincer), Small chop (hacher finement), Large chop (hacher grossièrement). Tout cela nous semble un peu juste, et sans aller jusqu'à la profusion de programmes automatiques dont bénéficie un blender comme le Moulinex Perfect Mix Cook LM835D10, des modes assez répandus comme glace pilée ou smoothie, voire lait végétal, n'auraient pas été de trop. Pour utiliser ces programmes automatiques, il faudra appuyer sur le bouton Mode et effectuer son choix grâce à la molette.
Enfin, les blendérophiles avertis se tourneront vers le mode manuel à 10 vitesses. Après avoir enfoncé la touche Manual, on choisit la vitesse de rotation des lames parmi les 10 grâce à la molette, on appuie sur le bouton central de la molette et… c'est tout. Bon point, on peut moduler la puissance en temps réel, ce qui n'est pas toujours le cas.
Le blender Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU a passé nos tests de mixage haut la main. Il a pulvérisé les 250 g de glaçons en trois coups de pulse. Et même après 10 coups (notre protocole de test en l'absence de programme dédié à la glace pilée), le résultat aurait fait une excellente margarita puisque les minuscules particules de glace ne ressemblaient pas à de la neige, comme cela arrive parfois.
Le smoothie, pour sa part, a été parfaitement réalisé : après 1 min de mixage en passant par toutes les vitesses, le résultat s'est montré très convaincant. Nous n'avons remarqué aucun morceau de glaçon ou de fruit trop gros pour nuire à la dégustation. On sent encore quelques particules de peau de pomme (que nous ne pelons pas pour juger de la finesse du mixage), sans que cela soit gênant.
Le nettoyage du Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU est des plus simples. Nous l’avons dit, le bloc de lames n'est fixé à la carafe en aucune manière. Il suffit de le tirer vers le haut, sans aucun effort ni quart de tour à imprimer, pour l'extraire de son logement. Il ne reste plus qu'à le passer sous un filet d'eau claire, voire à sortir l'éponge au besoin, pour débarrasser les lames des reliefs de nourriture.
Quant au bol, il passe au lave-vaisselle. Et si la préparation était trop épaisse pour que tout soit éliminé ainsi, l'ouverture est assez large pour laisser passer la main. Ce qui ne gâche rien, l'intérieur est relativement dépourvu de petits recoins où la nourriture pourrait aller se loger pour devenir compliquée à retirer. On peut établir un constat similaire pour les gourdes de transport.
Est-ce en raison de sa taille ? De son moteur de 1200 W ? Toujours est-il que le Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU n'a rien de la discrétion sonore du guerrier de la nuit, dont le fabricant tire son nom. En l'occurrence, nous serions plutôt face à un chevalier en armure d'apparat, grelottant qui plus est, monté sur un cheval équipé de sa barde complète, trottinant maladroitement sur un terrain particulièrement cahoteux.
En effet, à la puissance de 250 W, le niveau sonore du Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU atteint déjà 80 dB(A) à 1 m de distance. En poussant le moteur à fond, on grimpe à 420 W à peine (ce qui est un peu étrange pour un modèle censé développer 1200 W) et notre sonomètre indique 82 dB(A).
Certes, ce n'est pas le blender le plus bruyant de notre comparatif, mais il figure en bonne place dans notre peloton de tête.
Le Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU n'est pas parfait et il lui manque, selon nous, quelques programmes automatiques plus adaptés à l'utilisation d'un blender que ceux que propose le fabricant. On aurait également aimé un peu plus de métal dans sa construction et peut-être un niveau sonore mieux contenu. En revanche, dès qu'il passe à l'action, il se montre redoutablement efficace en pulvérisant tout ce qui a pour destinée de tomber entre ses lames. Qui plus est, on apprécie son système de blocage du couvercle innovant, mais avant tout l'extrême polyvalence dont il est capable, aussi bien pour réaliser des smoothies que pour découper rapidement les aliments, râper des carottes ou pétrir de la pâte.
Le Ninja Detect 1200 W TB401EU n'est pas le blender au meilleur rapport performance-prix de notre comparatif. Le Moulinex Perfect Mix Cook LM835D10 (pour un tarif comparable) ou l'antédiluvien Lagrange 609010 (plus de deux fois moins cher, pour sa part) nous semble mieux positionnés sur ce secteur. En revanche, il est incontestablement le modèle le plus polyvalent de notre sélection et aucun appareil de notre sélection ne lui arrive à la cheville sur ce point, même pas le Russell Hobbs 23180-56.

articles.title: Razer Naga V3 Pro, análisis: resulta que tener 23 botones intercambiables en un ratón gaming puede tener mucho sentido
articles.text:
Una de las desgracias de mi vida es que me gusten los MMOs. Me encantan estos juegos, pero tiendo a mantenerlos lejos porque no soy capaz de jugar un ratito. La última vez que me descargué 'Guild Wars 2' acabé metiéndole 89 horas en un mes y, viendo que se acercan 'AION 2' y 'World of Warcraft: Forever', algo me dice que se vienen meses complicados.
"Y Jose, ¿por qué me estás contando esto?". Porque llevo unas semanas jugando a 'Path of Exile 2' y 'Guild Wars 2' con el Razer Naga V3 Pro, el nuevo ratón de Razer enfocado a MMOs con botones laterales intercambiables. Y si alguna vez te habías preguntado si es necesario tener 23 botones en un ratón, la respuesta es "posiblemente no, pero lo mismo sí".
✅ Cómpralo si...
- Juegas mucho a MMOs y MOBA. Puedes usarlo también en shooters, pero brilla realmente en estos títulos.
- Estás dispuesto a aprender a usarlo. Si vienes de un ratón convencional o más "normal", es un proceso.
- Quieres un ratón premium, robusto, que funcione y responda bien en todas las situaciones.
❌ No lo compres si...
- Buscas un ratón barato, porque este no lo es.
- No vas a aprovechar las placas intercambiables y/o juegas solo a shooters o títulos con menos combinaciones.
- Quieres aprovechar la tasa de 8.000 Hz. Eso requiere de una compra aparte.
Lo esencial en 30 segundos
El Razer Naga V3 Pro es un ratón de gama alta pensado para MMOs y MOBA, y su gracia está en el panel lateral izquierdo intercambiable. Vienen tres placas imantadas en la caja: una de 12 botones tipo pad numérico para las rotaciones de MMO, otra de 6 botones para MOBA (el del 'League of Legends', con seis palanquitas de sobra para ataques, ulti y flash) y una de dos botones para shooters. A eso hay que sumarle los botones que trae de serie, que no son pocos, todos remapeables desde Razer Synapse. Cuesta unos 200 euros, así que ni es barato ni pretende serlo.
Como apuntes positivos, el rendimiento del ratón es excepcional, aunque mención honorífica merece la rueda: la sensación al hacer scroll es de las mejores que he probado. Los switches ópticos responden rapidísimo, la construcción es robusta y funciona igual de bien por cable, por Bluetooth o por dongle de 2,4 GHz. Llega a 1.000 Hz de serie, suficiente para casi todo el mundo.
Los "peros" llegan por dos frentes. El primero, que aprender a usar los paneles laterales tiene su historia: si vienes de un ratón normal, los primeros días son un proceso y hay que asumirlo. El segundo, que para exprimir los 8.000 Hz de tasa de sondeo necesitas comprar un dongle aparte que, a este precio, habría agradecido encontrar dentro de la caja.
Razer Naga V3 Pro - Ratón Gaming inalámbrico para Juegos MMO con Placas Laterales Intercambiables (HyperScroll de 2.ª generación, Switches ópticos para ratón 4.ª Gen)
Nuestra experiencia con el Razer Naga V3 Pro
¿Botones intercambiables? La placa lateral izquierda del ratón, como en anteriores modelos, es intercambiable y nos permite modificar las funciones del dispositivo por completo. Razer incluye en la caja tres (imantadas y con un acople fantástico), que son las siguientes:
A todos estos botones les tenemos que sumar los que el ratón trae de serie, que no son pocos. Entre ellos, faltaría, uno que sirve para lanzar una herramienta de IA generativa de textos. Todos los botones funcionan bien, se pueden remapear con Razer Synapse 4 y responden con velocidad, algo que se da por sentado en un ratón de 200 euros con switches ópticos. No obstante, es buena noticia que los botones de los paneles laterales lo hagan también.
Muy cómodo, dependiendo del agarre. En lo que a ergonomía se refiere, me parece que el ratón está bien rematado, bien diseñado y que tanto palma como dedos descansan donde tienen que descansar. Tiene un peso de 117 gramos más el panel que pongas, por lo que no es precisamente ligero. No obstante, que los pies sean de PTFE ayuda a que el deslizamiento sea suave.
En cuanto a comodidad de uso, como siempre, dependerá del tipo de agarre. Yo tiendo más al agarre con garras y este ratón se presta más a un agarre de palma, pero es cuestión de acostumbrarse. Lo que sí es todo aventura es hacerse y aprender a usar los botones laterales.
Reaprender los gestos. Si bien en 'Path of Exile 2' no me ha costado en exceso aprender a usar el panel de seis botones, jugar a 'Guild Wars 2' con el pad de 12 empezó siendo una verdadera locura. Llevo una build de nigromante Power Reaper, por lo que tengo que alternar a menudo entre espadón, lanza y utilidad. Cada rotación de ataque son seis botones, cambio, seis botones, cambio, seis botones y repetir. Con el teclado lo tengo dominadísimo, pero aprender a hacerlo con el ratón fue... desafiante.
Luego encontré el truco: mapear los cinco ataques y el cambio en los botones 1-6, mapear las utilidades en los botones 7-9 y dejar las curaciones y el acceso a la habilidad de Élite en los botones superiores del ratón. Así las rotaciones de ataque eran siempre los mismos botones. Tardé en acostumbrarme, pero una vez hecho el camino se hizo mucho más plano. Sigo siendo más competente con el teclado, pero creo que podría acostumbrarme a dejarlo de lado sin problema.
De todas maneras, la realidad es que usar este ratón y exprimirlo al máximo es un proceso y hay que afrontarlo. Asumo que cualquier persona interesada en él será consciente de ello, pero nunca está de más dejarlo claro: funciona muy bien, pero al principio es bastante difícil de usar.
Clics y rueda, ¡ay, la rueda! Los switches ópticos de los botones son moderadamente ruidosos, o sea, se escucha el click. Sin ser muy sonoros, tampoco es que sean especialmente discretos. La parte positiva es que los switches van de verdadero miedo y responden a una velocidad magnífica, aunque la verdadera joya de la corona es la rueda.
Desde Razer Synapse podemos configurar el desplazamiento de la rueda para que sea libre, dentado o dentado preciso. Notar cómo se aplica el mecanismo al cambiar de uno a otro es espectacular y la sensación al hacer scroll es fantástica, de las mejores que he experimentado. Poder configurar esto a placer me parece un verdadero puntazo, y más cuando funciona así de bien.
Conectividad (team cable). Finalmente, cabe destacar que el Razer Naga V3 Pro se puede usar por cable (que es como recomiendo usarlo si de verdad os importa el rendimiento), por Bluetooth o por red de 2,4 GHz vía dongle. La tasa de sondeo es de hasta 1.000 Hz, suficiente para casi todos los mortales, aunque se puede aumentar a 8.000 Hz usando un dongle dedicado que se compra por separado. En un ratón de ese precio, habría agradecido que el accesorio viniera incluido en la caja. En cualquier caso, en esta casa somos team cable y, en ese sentido, funciona estupendamente (como, todo sea dicho, era de esperar).
Ficha técnica del Razer Naga V3 Pro
|  | Razer Naga V3 Pro | 
|---|---|
| dimensiones y peso | 119,5 x 75,5 x 43,5 mm 117 gramos Panel lateral de 12 botones: 20 gramos Panel lateral de 6 botones: 17 gramos Panel lateral de 2 botones: 15 gramos | 
| rueda | Razer HyperScroll de 2ª generación de 4 direcciones Modos de desplazamiento dentado de 24 y 48 pasos, y de giro libre Modo de carrete inteligente configurable en Synapse | 
| base | 100% PTFE | 
| conexión | USB tipo A USB tipo C Razer HyperSpeed Wireless Bluetooth | 
| tasa de sondeo | 1.000 Hz 8.000 opcional (dongle por separado) | 
| switches | Switches ópticos para ratón de 4ª generación 100 millones de clicks de vida útil | 
| aceleración máxima | 90 G | 
| velocidad máxima | 930 IPS | 
| sensibilidad máxima | 50.000 PPP | 
| sensor | Sensor óptico Focus Pro de 50 000 PPP de 3ª generación | 
| iluminación | Razer Chroma RGB (logotipo, rueda de desplazamiento y placa lateral de 12 botones) | 
| batería | Hasta 155 horas (en modo HyperSpeed Wireless) Hasta 280 horas (en modo Bluetooth) | 
| software | Razer Synapse | 
| precio | 199,99 euros | 
Razer Naga V3 Pro, la opinión de Xataka
El Razer Naga V3 Pro es un ratón de gama alta que ofrece una experiencia propia de la gama alta y que, a diferencia de otros competidores, requiere de cierto esmero por nuestro lado. Acostumbrarse a los paneles laterales y a usar todos los botones puede ser, y es, desafiante, pero superada la curva de aprendizaje, jugar a MMOs con él es, sencillamente, fantástico.
Ese es, precisamente, su gran punto "negativo": no es un ratón para todo el mundo. No me gastaría el dinero que cuesta si buscase un ratón más "normal". Hay que saber que es un ratón para un tipo de uso muy concreto al que se le saca partido en ciertos juegos.
Me habría gustado que el dongle para los 8.000 Hz viniese en la caja, habría sido un detalle, pero por lo demás, reconozco que me ha gustado mucho.
¿Te lo recomiendo?
Sí, pero si sabes a qué vienes. Si tienes intención de darle caña a 'WoW: Forever', le metes horas al 'LoL' o, como yo, tienes marcado el último trimestre del año que viene para darle candela a la beta de 'Guild Wars 3', este ratón te va a encantar. Si quieres algo plug-and-play que funcione bien, hay alternativas más baratas.

articles.title: Microsoft revives the Surface Mouse with haptic feedback, six-month battery life
articles.text:
First look: At Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit event in Maui, Hawaii, Microsoft unveiled multiple new Surface devices, including a 12-inch Surface Pro convertible and a 13-inch Surface Laptop. The company also debuted a redesigned Surface Mouse almost 10 years after the original model launched alongside the Surface Studio in November 2016.
The second-generation Surface Mouse includes several new features, including haptic feedback, which uses an internal vibration motor to deliver subtle pulses and tactile responses to confirm clicks. It can also provide feedback for on-screen interactions such as snapping windows to the edge of the screen or aligning objects and layouts in PowerPoint, Affinity, Concepts, Filmora, and other supported applications.
The new Surface Mouse also gets a customizable Action Button that summons Copilot by default but can also be configured to work with other actions and Windows shortcuts. According to Microsoft, the button can be used to launch any app or support any shortcut, but it can only be customized using the Microsoft Surface app.
The mouse supports Bluetooth 6.0 and can connect to multiple devices simultaneously, allowing users to move between them seamlessly. It sports a large battery that Microsoft claims can last up to six months on a single charge, meaning users won't have to recharge it frequently.
The new Surface Mouse has an ergonomic ambidextrous shape specially designed to be comfortable for both left-handed and right-handed users. The company highlighted that it's built with 30% recycled content, including more recycled plastic than previous models such as the 2025 Surface Arc Mouse and the 2018 Surface Precision Mouse.
The new Surface Mouse will go on sale on October 13 in Black and Platinum colorways. It is priced at $79.99, which is a steep hike over the $50 asking price for the original 2016 model, but Microsoft would likely justify the higher price by citing the additional features, customization options, and improved battery life.
Alongside the Surface Mouse, Microsoft also debuted the new Surface Pro and Surface Laptop, starting at $1,149.99 and $1,199, respectively. Both devices are powered by the Snapdragon X2 Plus SoC, which the company claims offers up to 18% more battery efficiency, over 60% faster graphics performance, and 95% faster on-device AI inference compared to the Snapdragon X Plus.

articles.title: Meta puts its AI assistant on a keychain
articles.text:
Mark Zuckerberg said Meta’s new personal AI agent Muse has become the “centerpiece” of his AI vision, as he unveiled a new handheld AI “charm” device that will feature the interactive assistant.
The Meta chief used the company’s annual Connect event at its Silicon Valley headquarters to announce Muse Charm, a small pendant-like device that fits on a keychain and is activated by a fingerprint sensor.
The device, which features a screen showing the Muse avatar, will also have real-time voice interactivity and is set to be released in December.
“If you’re not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show what’s going on around you,” the chief executive said.
Muse, development of which was first revealed by the FT in May, has helped change the momentum of Zuckerberg’s huge bet on AI, quickly becoming the most downloaded app on both the Apple and Android app stores in the US since its launch two weeks ago.
The easy-to-use app offers consumers a team of autonomous bots to carry out everyday tasks, such as ordering groceries, booking travel and organising finances.
Zuckerberg on Wednesday also announced new capabilities for Muse, including the ability to have live conversations with the interactive AI assistant, and insisted that it has “state-of-the-art privacy and security.”
The Meta founder has come under increasing pressure from Wall Street as he pours billions of dollars into AI infrastructure and talent, with Meta’s share price falling by more than a quarter between last September and the beginning of August.
But Meta’s stock has bounced back since the September 8 launch, adding $300 billion to its market capitalisation. The stock was slightly higher in after-hours trading on Wednesday.
The release of a breakout product to Meta’s 3 billion users caps a turbulent two years in which Zuckerberg has repeatedly struggled to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic in developing frontier AI models and features.
Zuckerberg on Wednesday said he believed Muse would “make users money.” As a result, the company would offer a free Muse tier “with the expectation that over time we will profit by taking a small fee from transactions.”

articles.title: Melhor VPN para iPhone: como blindar aplicativos e reduzir o rastreamento de dados • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Resumo
- A utilização de uma VPN no iPhone é essencial para proteger os dados de usuários, uma vez que o ecossistema restrito da Apple não impede a interceptação de informações em conexões abertas.
- A NordVPN oferece recursos de privacidade, desempenho e proteção contra ameaças, incluindo protocolos como NordLynx e OpenVPN e proteção contra chamadas fraudulentas.
- A configuração da VPN no iPhone é simples e pode ser feita por meio do aplicativo oficial da NordVPN ou da configuração nativa do iOS.
O ecossistema restrito da Apple consolidou a ideia de que o iPhone é imune a falhas de segurança. No entanto, embora a blindagem do iOS proteja o sistema operacional, ela pode não ser suficiente para os dados que percorrem na rede, que costumam ficar vulneráveis ao rastreio de provedores e possíveis interceptações.
É aí que uma VPN pode atuar. Ao criar um túnel criptografado entre o aparelho e um servidor remoto, ela protege o tráfego da conexão, oculta o endereço IP e amplia essa camada para aplicativos que não estão restritos ao navegador.
Por que usar uma VPN no iPhone? 📱
A segurança de um celular também depende da rede. Mesmo com recursos nativos de privacidade do iOS ativados, o tráfego da maioria dos apps de terceiros pode continuar exposto. Uma VPN adiciona criptografia ao tráfego e pode ser usada em diferentes situações:
✅ Wi-Fi público: ajuda a proteger senhas, mensagens e outros dados transmitidos em redes abertas.
✅ Aplicativos: a conexão VPN pode abranger diferentes apps, e não apenas o navegador.
✅ Viagens: permite escolher um servidor em outro país para manter a rota de conexão mais próxima da habitual.
✅ Privacidade: o endereço IP real fica oculto do serviço acessado.
✅ Redes restritas: recursos como NordWhisper ajudam a manter a conexão em ambientes com filtros ou bloqueios.
Conheça os planos da NordVPN para o iPhone.
Retransmissão Privada do iCloud e VPN: qual é a diferença?
A Retransmissão Privada do iCloud (Private Relay) pode passar a impressão de que o iPhone já conta com uma VPN integrada. Os recursos têm objetivos semelhantes em alguns pontos, mas não funcionam da mesma maneira.
A Retransmissão Privada foi desenvolvida principalmente para proteger a navegação no Safari e usa uma arquitetura com dois relays para separar a identidade do usuário do destino acessado. Já uma VPN cria um túnel para encaminhar o tráfego pela rede privada do serviço.
| Recurso | Retransmissão Privada do iCloud (Apple) | NordVPN | 
|---|---|---|
| Cobertura | Restrita prioritariamente ao Safari, consultas DNS e tráfego HTTP não criptografado. | Pode proteger o tráfego de aplicativos e navegadores. | 
| Visibilidade do Provedor (ISP) | O provedor de internet continua vendo o destino do tráfego dos seus aplicativos. | Oculta o tráfego da atividade do provedor. | 
| Controle de Localização | Mantém o país e fuso horário reais do usuário. | Permite escolher servidores em mais de 224 locais pelo mundo para alterar o IP de saída. | 
| Proteção contra ameaças online | O iOS utiliza o ITP no Safari, com foco em reduzir o rastreamento entre sites. | Antivírus Next Gen bloqueia anúncios, rastreadores e URLs maliciosas. | 
| Kill Switch | Não possui recurso equivalente. | Interrompe o acesso à internet em caso de queda da VPN. | 
| Monitoramento de vazamentos | Não possui recurso equivalente. | O Dark Web Monitor alerta quando credenciais do usuário aparecem em vazamentos. | 
| Arquitetura | Separa a identidade e o destino acessado entre dois servidores operados por empresas diferentes. | Túnel VPN com política no-log e auditorias independentes. | 
O que a NordVPN oferece no iPhone?
A NordVPN vai além da função básica de alterar o IP. O aplicativo reúne recursos de privacidade, desempenho e proteção contra ameaças em uma mesma conexão.
- Desempenho e rede: em testes independentes conduzidos pelo West Coast Labs em 2025, a NordVPN atingiu uma média de 817 Mbps, sendo classificada como a VPN mais rápida em comparação a concorrentes avaliados.
- Protocolos: a NordVPN utiliza NordLynx, NordWhisper e OpenVPN, com criptografia AES-256-GCM ou ChaCha20-Poly1305.
- NordWhisper para redes restritas: o recurso ajuda a contornar firewalls e filtros rígidos de rede, ajudando a manter a conexão em ambientes que dificultam o uso de VPNs tradicionais.
- Proteção contra chamadas: identifica números associados a golpes e exibe alertas antes do atendimento.
- Antivírus Next-Gen: bloqueia sites maliciosos, anúncios invasivos e rastreadores.
- Dark Web Monitor: alerta quando credenciais do usuário aparecem em vazamentos.
Como configurar a VPN no iPhone
A configuração de uma VPN no iOS não exige ajustes complexos no sistema. A ativação pelo aplicativo oficial é direta e automatiza a criação do túnel criptografado:
- Escolha a assinatura ideal para você no site da NordVPN.
- Baixe o aplicativo da NordVPN na App Store.
- Abra o aplicativo e faça o login ou crie uma conta.
- Autorize a configuração de VPN quando o iPhone solicitar.
- Toque em “Conectar” para iniciar a conexão.
Caso prefira não usar o aplicativo, o iOS permite a configuração nativa com os dados do seu provedor:
- Abra Ajustes > Geral > VPN e Gerenciamento de Dispositivo > VPN.
- Toque em Adicionar Configuração de VPN….
- Escolha o protocolo de conexão e informe os dados solicitados, como servidor, ID remoto, nome de usuário e senha.
- Toque em OK ou Salvar para concluir a configuração.
- Para ativar a conexão, volte à tela de VPN e ligue a chave correspondente.
Depois disso, o aplicativo passa a encaminhar o tráfego pela rede VPN.
Privacidade estendida a todo o ecossistema
A mesma assinatura pode ser usada em até 10 dispositivos simultaneamente, incluindo computadores com macOS, Windows e Linux, tablets e smart TVs. Isso permite manter a proteção da rede também em outros aparelhos usados no dia a dia.
A NordVPN também afirma seguir uma política de no-log, sem registro das atividades de navegação. Segundo o material, a política já passou por seis auditorias independentes.
VPN no iPhone é mais do que trocar o endereço IP
No celular, uma VPN pode cumprir um papel mais amplo do que simplesmente mascarar a localização. Ela adiciona uma camada de criptografia ao tráfego, pode proteger conexões de diferentes aplicativos e oferece mais controle sobre a rota usada pelo aparelho.
No caso da NordVPN, esse conjunto é complementado por recursos como servidores especializados, proteção contra chamadas fraudulentas, bloqueio de ameaças e monitoramento de vazamentos.

articles.title: Databricks buys Row Zero and is scouting for more startups to acquire | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Databricks announced on Thursday that it has acquired an early-stage spreadsheet startup called Row Zero.
The story goes that Databricks’ finance team fell in love with Row Zero because it was a cloud tool that could scale beyond 1 million live spreadsheet rows. They were combining Row Zero with Databricks’ homegrown AI agent called Genie. With Genie, Databricks users can use natural-language prompts to ask complicated business questions of their data stored in Databricks systems, such as analyzing profit margins or the status of sales prospects.
When the executive team asked the finance team about this cloud tool they were using, a light bulb went off.
“Spreadsheets are one such interface that every business analyst loves. So it makes a lot of sense to intermarry Business Intelligence (BI), Agents, and Spreadsheets!” Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi posted on X about how the acquisition went down.
So an enterprise’s secure data lives in Databricks’ cloud storage, and AI agents and humans interact with it through the spreadsheet format and formulas they know well, rather than using and learning some other business intelligence software. By integrating Row Zero with Databricks, the data can be manipulated in a spreadsheet form but remain secure, rather than transferred to an insecure spreadsheet that is shared around.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed. Row Zero, founded by former AWS and Tableau engineers, raised $10 million in May 2025, at an estimated $40 million valuation at the time, according to PitchBook.
Databricks, which closed another $5 billion in funding in August and hit $7 billion in annualized revenue run rate, has been busy shopping in 2026 and is eager to keep doing so. “We intend to do many more acquisitions like this in the future,” Ghodsi told TechCrunch.
In March, Databricks bought two startups, Quotient AI, which does evaluation and reinforcement learning for AI agents, and very early-stage interactive notebook SiftD.ai. In June, the company bought AI security operations center startup Panther, previously valued at $1.4 billion in 2021. Last month, it bought Electric, makers of a small, lite Postgres database known as PGlite, useful for agents running locally on devices.

articles.title: Save $149 on this 3-item gaming combo from Newegg — $1,050 buys a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB of Corsair DDR5 RAM, Asus TUF Gaming X870E-Plus motherboard, and a free 240mm AIO and AMD game bundle
articles.text:
Save $149 on this 3-item gaming combo from Newegg — $1,050 buys a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB of Corsair DDR5 RAM, Asus TUF Gaming X870E-Plus motherboard, and a free 240mm AIO and AMD game bundle
Get 32GB of RAM for only $351 in this 3-item Newegg combo
With the RAMpocalypse in full swing and little relief in sight, we need to look for combo deals to get the best prices on items like RAM (and even those are fleeting today). This 3-item combo from Newegg is one of the better ones lately, offering the wicked-fast gaming processor Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB of Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 RAM, and a quality motherboard in the Asus TUF Gaming X870E-Plus Wifi for only $1,050. A savings of $149. And if you apply the discount to the RAM, it’s only $351, which many would consider reasonable (for the times).
First is one of the most popular and fastest current-generation CPUs for gaming: the Ryzen 7 9800X3D. This 8-core/16-thread Zen5-based processor has a base clock of 4.6 GHz and a max boost of 5.2 GHz, which is plenty of speed for any task. The X3D variant's 96MB of L3 cache helps with gaming (among other things), making it one of the fastest gaming CPUs available. It is also a well-rounded performer that excels in games and suits most applications. This combo also includes a free Rosewill FrostMax 240mm AIO with digital display (a $70 value), which easily handles the 120W processor.
The RAM portion of the bundle, Corsair’s Vengeance RGB 32GB (2x16GB) DDR5-6000 CL36 RAM kit, is currently available on Newegg for a wallet-emptying $499.99 (the price keeps going up) when bought separately. The good news is that the discount brings this RAM down to $351. This black kit matches the Asus TUF Gaming X870E-Plus Wifi board in this combo and features a frosted RGB light bar that runs the length of the sticks. If RGB lighting isn’t your thing and you prefer a stealthy, unassuming look, you can turn it off. The DDR5-6000 speed lands in the sweet spot for the AM5 platform and is a worthwhile, good-looking option. The SK Hynix ICs under the heatsink pair nicely with the board and offer plenty of overclocking headroom.
Save big on this 3-item combo from Newegg and get snag 32GB of Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 RAM for less. You get the awesome Ryzen 7 9800X3D CPU, a quality Asus X870E TUF Gaming motherboard, and Newegg even throws in a free 240mm AIO and AMD gam bundle ($140 value)
Last, the Asus TUF Gaming X870E-Plus Wifi 7 is a solid all-around motherboard for the AM5 platform. It delivers sufficient power to support flagship-class processors and easily handles the 9800X3D in the combo, even with some overclocking. It comes with four M.2 sockets (one PCIe 5.0), two SATA ports for storage, fast networking with integrated Wi-Fi 7 and 2,5 GbE, ample USB ports on the rear IO (13, including two USB4 40 Gbps Type-C), and a quality audio solution based on the last-gen Realtek flagship (ALC1220P). Asus’ AI solutions (AI Cache Boost, Overclocking, Cooling II, and Networking II) and the DIY-friendly design make it easy to build and get the most out of your system.
Newegg used to offer several Combo deals with RAM. Still, over the past few weeks, as stock continues to dwindle, we’ve seen them whittle down to only a couple that are worthwhile, so when you see something like this and are ready to pull the trigger, do it, as you never know how long it will last. If you’re in the market to buy a new AM5-based system, this 3-item $1,050 combo from Newegg, sporting 32GB of RAM, the venerable Ryzen 5 9800X3D, and a quality motherboard (don’t forget the free 240mm AIO and AMD game bundle!), is currently one of the least expensive ways into the platform.

articles.title: No wallet? No problem - Revolut's new till will let UK customers pay with a smile
articles.text:
No wallet? No problem - Revolut's new till will let UK customers pay with a smile
Pay with a smile with Revolut
- Revolut reveals new payment method which just needs a smile
- Facial recognition technology will help identify Revolut customers
- Technology could help protect SMBs from losses caused by tech outages
If you've ever been about to pay for something in a shop and suddenly realised you've misplaced your wallet, Revolut may have the answer to help avoid any more embarrassing situations.
The payments giant is launching Revolut Pay with Smile, the UK’s first in-store facial recognition checkout, meaning customers can pay with a glance or even a smile - no need for a wallet or even a phone.
The move looks to make sure that UK small businesses don't lose money from payment terminal issues, whether hardware or software-related, offering a new way to accept payments.
Pay with Smile
We were invited along to try out the new Revolut Pay with Smile at a Kiss the Hippo Coffee shop in central London, where customers could try out the new technology.
Guests who paid in-store with a smile were able to order from a special Revolut menu, with speciality coffees at £1 - a bargain in today's market.
We gave it a go, and found the process to be pretty painless - much like authenticating yourself on a phone app, or having your photo taken at passport control, it was fairly quick and smooth to get through - and the coffee wasn't bad either.
All it took was a quick facial scan, and the system verified the payment in a matter of seconds - quicker than many contactless payments, we'd say.

Users will have to be existing Revolut customers, as the system uses advanced facial technology to verify the user's identity against the selfie ID checks they added when first signing up to Revolut to authenticate and process a payment securely.
Powered by the new Revolut Register, a modular, two-screen register designed to bring together payments, banking, and floor operations, Pay with Smile offers 0% processing fees for merchants, a huge boost when overhead costs are higher than ever.
Transactions are authenticated with end-to-end encryption managed inside the Revolut app, with no personal data stored by merchants
Revolut Register is available now with a special 50% discount for £349.50 + VAT (RRP: £699 + VAT) on a merchant's first terminal until 31st December 2026 for both new and existing customers.

articles.title: Five neat things we learned about Meta's first-ever VR Glasses
articles.text:
It was a big week for Meta.
During its annual Meta Connect conference, the company unveiled a suite of new products, including the VR Glasses, the camera-less Ray-Ban Meta Audio, a Canadian launch of the Meta Ray-Ban Display and more.
But naturally, Meta’s first-ever VR glasses garnered a particular amount of attention, and they were certainly my favourite thing that I saw at Connect. It’s pretty impressive tech, honestly, offering the full VR experience across entertainment and personal computing in a cozy 100g package and small tethered puck.
After my hands-on demo, I also got to attend a media roundtable with Angela Chang, Meta’s VP of product management. In a wide-ranging conversation, we learned a lot more about the making of the glasses and Meta’s long-term ambitions with them. Here are some main takeaways.
It’s built on the Quest architecture
Impressively, the small, lightweight VR Glasses use “the exact same OS underneath” as the much bulkier Quest, according to Chang. Not only does this mean that developers will be able to more smoothly develop products across Meta’s entire line-up of VR devices, but it means that the thousands of titles already in the Quest library will be available on the Meta Glasses. These join the dozens of experiences that are being crafted specifically for the VR Glasses, including around 75 games that can be played simply with hand gestures.
Of course, this also means that anyone looking to upgrade could carry over their catalogue as well. For someone like me who’s spent hours across both the Quest 2 and 3 over the years, that should help make for a more seamless transition.
No compromises, technical challenges be damned
Of course, it’s one thing to have these experiences be compatible, but it’s another to have them look and run even better thanks to beefier specs, including 2.4K micro-OLED displays and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset.
But Chang says one of the biggest challenges actually pertains to point of view.
“Trying to find this perfect sweet spot between the field of view [being] wide enough, big enough to be compatible with the traditional Quest content, immersive content, not feeling like you have to basically cut off all the years of content that we have invested in, while small enough to fit in this glasses form factor,” she explains. “We tested many different fields of view, sizes, resolutions, shapes and whatnot, and pushed our team very hard to try to innovate around the display, the display and optical stack to really get to the sweet spot.”
Another big challenge, she says, was figuring out how, exactly, to connect the puck, given that it handles battery, storage and compute.
“There’s concerns around whether that’s going to get in your way, and so we have to really think through the user experience, both in seated experiences, but also when you’re walking around on mobile,” she says.
“How do you get the wire to be malleable enough, soft enough, even though it’s a custom optical cable with lots of data bandwidth going up and down, to just be like smooth enough so that it doesn’t tangle? But at the same time, gracefully be able to drape behind your back, so you can clip the puck onto your pocket and have the fan vents face up, so we’re not causing it to heat up in your pocket or in your bag?”
(It should be noted that my demo was at a stationary chair and desk, so outside of standing briefly to try out the new hand-tracking Beat Saber Flux, I didn’t get a feel for how intrusive the optical tether could be.)
It’s been specifically designed with airplane use in mind
As someone who travels a lot for work, I’m always looking for a variety of things to do on flights, especially when I get restless. For that reason, I was really intrigued to see Meta specifically citing being on a plane as a major use case for the VR Glasses.
Right off the bat, the puck will help with portable use since it serves as the power source, no outlet required. And, of course, its tiny form factor compared to something like the Apple Vision Pro is a huge benefit. But it’s the other features that are particularly promising.
For one, the virtual private movie theatre functionality is a nice change of pace from the often small (and sometimes completely absent) in-flight entertainment systems. And for another, the productivity features, which include a fully interactive virtual keyboard that lays out on a flat surface in front of you, provide an alternative to using your laptop on the painfully small sliding table on the back of the seat. (Or, in another example I posed to Chang, those classroom-type chairs with a mini table attached.)
As Chang explains, the size of the surface doesn’t really matter, but rather the positioning of your hand for calibration. She adds that the surface’s material and contrast are also important, with higher contrasts yielding better results. “But in general, we’ve trained even for white tables so that it works well,” she says. However, she did acknowledge that hand-tracking becomes difficult in low-light situations, so you might run into some issues if it gets dark on the plane.
Lots of opportunities for refinements
Obviously, any first-generation product like this leaves a lot of room for iteration. But something that’s particularly unique about the VR Glasses is that they’re fuelled by the puck, not the frames themselves, which suggests the possibility of swapping it out with different models of varying power levels. In theory, that could be a way to help offset the fact that this debut model costs US$1,299 (about C$1,800), as it’s easy to imagine giving customers more flexibility down the line.
When another journalist asked about this during the roundtable, Chang smiled knowingly.
“I like where you’re thinking. It’s certainly something that’s been on our mind. I think for this first generation, given that it was many leaps of innovation all in one go, we had to use a pretty proprietary interconnect on both the glasses and the puck side,” she says. “So it’s not easily interchangeable with other types of standard interconnects. So in future generations, that’s certainly our aspiration, to be able to have more standard interconnects between the puck and the glasses, so you can actually mix and match.”
Meta VR, including Quest, is here to stay
Given that Meta was all about the metaverse and Quest headsets not that long ago, it would be easy to assume that the company is largely moving away from VR. While these new glasses obviously feature that technology prominently, the company is also merging it with the smart glasses format that’s become such a focus of its business.
That begs the question: what does this all mean for Meta VR in general? According to Chang, it signals the future, which is paying off longer-term work.
“We’re pretty proud of the fact that, earlier this year, we basically transitioned to a sustainable business model for the VR business. Because we want to be in this business for a very long time,” she said.
She also notes that the Meta VR Glasses aren’t meant to replace Quest because they serve different purposes.
“The Meta VR Glasses is our vision for many years, working towards that general purpose computing platform where you can do many things on it. You can do many things really well on it [now], but it’s not particularly optimized for any singular use case,” she says.
“We just want to make sure if you like to do work on it, you can do that. If you like to watch movies on it, you can do that. If you like to take it away with you anywhere you want to go, you can do that. Whereas the Quest is truly more of a bespoke product for specific audiences, gamers, and for specific use cases, [like] gaming, fitness, dynamic motion type of immersive experiences. So that’s how we think about it.”
The Meta VR Glasses are set to launch sometime in spring 2027. Specific Canadian pricing and availability have yet to be confirmed.

articles.title: Ryan Murphy relance Glee : le créateur a écrit la suite avec l'équipe d'origine
articles.text:
Dix-sept ans après sa première diffusion sur Fox, en 2009, la série musicale Glee pourrait revenir. Les rumeurs d’un retour, qui circulaient depuis plusieurs mois dans les coulisses d’Hollywood, ont pris corps ce mercredi 23 septembre 2026, quand Ryan Murphy a confirmé l’existence d’un scénario.
Lors d’un entretien accordé à Entertainment Tonight, le showrunner prolifique a révélé avoir bouclé l’écriture d’un premier scénario avec ses acolytes de la première heure, Brad Falchuk et Ian Brennan. Une démarche motivée par l’envie de tâter le terrain avant de lancer officiellement la machine.
Ces trois auteurs ont créé Glee et écrit ses deux premières saisons. Personne n’a encore lu le scénario. Ryan Murphy explique vouloir en écrire plusieurs pour recueillir des avis, d’abord celui des acteurs, dont l’équipe était « très proche » pendant le tournage. La série s’est arrêtée en 2015, après six saisons.
Une dizaine d’acteurs d’origine de Glee déjà sondés
Afin de prendre la température, le créateur a d’ores et déjà pris son téléphone pour sonder la distribution historique. Ryan Murphy affirme avoir contacté une dizaine de comédiens emblématiques du casting original. Selon lui, tous ont posé « beaucoup de questions », mais tous se sont montrés « très enthousiastes » à l’idée.
Cette annonce intervient une semaine après la prise de parole de Lea Michele, qui a joué Rachel Berry pendant les six saisons. Interrogée par E! News, l’actrice avait réaffirmé son amour inconditionnel pour la franchise et son intention de suivre Ryan Murphy les yeux fermés sur n’importe quel projet. Un retour se ferait sans plusieurs figures de la série, dont Cory Monteith, mort en 2013, et Naya Rivera, morte en 2020.
Au-delà de la nostalgie et du fan service, ce reboot devra relever le défi de réinventer la formule Glee dans un paysage télévisuel et culturel qui a profondément changé. La série originale avait marqué son époque par son humour irrévérencieux, ses reprises pop omniprésentes et son traitement précurseur des problématiques LGBT. En réunissant le trio d’auteurs original, Ryan Murphy cherche manifestement à retrouver l’étincelle et l’énergie des premiers épisodes, tout en s’adaptant aux attentes d’une toute nouvelle génération de téléspectateurs.
