articles.title: Aspirateurs-robots : avec ses nouveaux DEEBOT, ECOVACS veut pousser la concurrence au bout du rouleau
articles.text:
Avec ses nouveaux aspirateurs-robots laveurs DEEBOT, ECOVACS poursuit le développement de sa technologie OZMO ROLLER, lancée en 2024 avec le DEEBOT X8. Et la marque compte bien faire de son rouleau-serpillière actif le marqueur premium de ses appareils de nettoyage.
Cela fait déjà quelques années que les performances d’un aspirateur-robot ne se mesurent plus seulement à sa capacité à aspirer efficacement les poussières. La partie dédiée au lavage des sols durs est désormais de plus en plus scrutée par les consommateurs, et ça, ECOVACS l’a bien compris. C’est pourquoi la marque a lancé dès 2024 sa technologie OZMO ROLLER, apparue pour la première fois sur le DEEBOT X8.
Ce système repose sur un rouleau-serpillière actif qui répète en continu un cycle breveté de pulvérisation, lavage, raclage et collecte. En d’autres termes, le rouleau est nettoyé au fur et à mesure qu’il lave le sol, ce qui contribue à maintenir son efficacité et à éviter les contaminations croisées.
OZMO ROLLER, la technologie qui roule pour ECOVACS
Bien que cette technologie soit finalement assez jeune, il est évident qu’elle séduit : en juillet 2026, plus de 2,8 millions d’unités équipées de l’OZMO ROLLER avaient déjà été expédiées dans le monde. De quoi pousser ECOVACS à l’améliorer constamment. Cette année, la marque inaugure la troisième génération de son système.
Dans sa version 3.0, l’OZMO ROLLER gagne en maturité : au programme, un rouleau en microfibre plus long, ainsi que l’intégration de TruEdge 3.0 et d’AI Stain Detection 2.0 en fonction des robots.
Soutenue par plus de 3 100 brevets et plus de 5,2 milliards de RMB investis en R&D depuis 2018, cette technologie permet à ECOVACS de rester fidèle à son credo : « Une serpillière ne devrait pas devenir plus sale au fur et à mesure qu’elle nettoie. » Reste à savoir sur quels modèles d’aspirateurs-robots laveurs on la trouve en cette rentrée.
DEEBOT T90S Pro Omni : OZMO ROLLER 3.0 à l’honneur
Le DEEBOT T90S Pro Omni est le premier aspirateur-robot laveur de cette sélection et, sans surprise, il embarque le système OZMO ROLLER 3.0. Cela donne accès à un rouleau 50 % plus long que celui de la précédente génération et à une technologie de lavage sous pression. À cela s’ajoute TruEdge 3.0, qui améliore le nettoyage des bords des murs et des plinthes.
Sur la partie aspiration, le DEEBOT T90S Pro Omni peut monter jusqu’à 40 000 Pa BLAST, pour un flux d’air atteignant 16,45 l/s. Cette puissance est complétée par ZeroTangle 4.0, dont la conception anti-enchevêtrement à flux d’air dirigé permet de réduire l’accumulation de cheveux autour de la brosse.
Côté navigation, le robot s’appuie sur TruePass et AIVI 3D 4.0 pour se repérer dans son environnement, franchir les seuils et éviter les obstacles. Enfin, sa station OMNI automatise plusieurs tâches d’entretien, notamment le lavage du rouleau, la gestion de l’eau sale et le vidage de la poussière. Le DEEBOT T90S Pro Omni est disponible au prix de 799 €.
Deux autres robots pour élargir la gamme OZMO ROLLER
Si le DEEBOT T90S Pro Omni se présente comme l’aspirateur-robot laveur le plus équilibré de cette rentrée, ECOVACS met en avant deux autres références dotées de l’OZMO ROLLER 3.0.
DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone : redoutable contre les taches
Le DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone est une autre nouveauté d’ECOVACS
qui ne cache pas ses ambitions. Il s’agit du premier robot de la marque à
combiner les technologies FocusJet et OZMO ROLLER 3.0, en plus de disposer
d’une station OmniCyclone sans sac.
FocusJet peut faire la différence dans les logements où les taches tenaces et les salissures incrustées font partie du quotidien. Ses deux buses d’atomisation sous pression pulvérisent une solution nettoyante à l’avant
de l’appareil afin de pré-dissoudre les taches avant son passage. L’OZMO ROLLER 3.0 prend ensuite le relais avec un lavage actif sous pression.
Le robot profite également de TruEdge 3.0, de ZeroTangle 4.0 et d’AIVI 3D 4.0. Sa station OmniCyclone intègre quant à elle la recharge intelligente PowerBoost Charging Plus, tout en fonctionnant sans sac afin de limiter l’entretien. L’ECOVACS DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone est proposé au prix de 1 299 €.
DEEBOT T90 Max Pro : une porte d’entrée vers OZMO ROLLER
Enfin, le DEEBOT T90 Max Pro est le modèle le plus accessible de cette sélection. Il permet de découvrir la technologie OZMO ROLLER 3.0 à un tarif plus abordable : il bénéficie du long rouleau et du lavage sous pression, mais aussi d’une aspiration de 40 000 Pa associée aux systèmes ZeroTangle 4.0 et TruEdge 3.0. Sa station OMNI propose également une maintenance automatisée qui comprend notamment le lavage à l’eau chaude à 100°C.
Proposé à 599 €, le DEEBOT T90 Max Pro permet à ECOVACS de rendre sa technologie OZMO ROLLER 3.0 plus accessible, sans la réserver à ses modèles les plus onéreux. De quoi contribuer à installer davantage le rouleau dans les foyers.

articles.title: Kurz vor wichtigem Feiertag: Smarte Samsung-Kühlschränke fallen nach Update komplett aus
articles.text:
Kurz vor wichtigem Feiertag: Smarte Samsung-Kühlschränke fallen nach Update komplett aus
Smarte Haushaltsgeräte sind nützlich – bis es zu einem technischen Fehler kommt. Genau das ist kürzlich Samsung in Südkorea passiert. Nach einem Update berichteten Besitzer:innen smarter Kühlschränke des Unternehmens, dass diese nicht mehr funktionierten. Ein:e Samsung-Sprecher:in bestätigte das Problem und erklärte, dass entsprechende Notfallmaßnahmen ergriffen worden seien.
Smarte Haushaltsgeräte werden beliebter
Es gibt inzwischen zahlreiche Smart-Home-Geräte auf dem Markt, die sich durch Internetanbindung, geräteübergreifende Integration und eine Vielzahl weiterer praktischer Funktionen auszeichnen. Die Menschen in Deutschland stehen dieser Entwicklung offen gegenüber: Laut einer Umfrage des Digitalverbandes Bitkom nutzt schon mehr als die Hälfte der Einwohner:innen Smart-Home-Anwendungen im eigenen Haushalt. Fast genauso viele können sich sogar grundsätzlich vorstellen, einen KI-gesteuerten humanoiden Roboter für die Hausarbeit einzusetzen. Am häufigsten wurden dabei Aufräumen, das Verräumen von Einkäufen und Putzen als mögliche Einsatzbereiche genannt.
Allerdings gibt es auch Vorbehalte, die der Nutzung im Weg stehen: So fürchten 59 Prozent der Nicht-Nutzer:innen, über ein smartes Haushaltsgerät Opfer eines Hacking-Angriffs zu werden. Weitere 40 Prozent haben Angst, dass ihre persönlichen Daten missbraucht werden könnten. Auch ein möglicher Ausfall spielt eine Rolle: 54 Prozent der Smart-Home-Nutzer:innen berichten von technischen Problemen. Meist wüden diese im Zusammenhang mit der Internetverbindung stehen. Dass smarte Haushaltsgeräte nicht immer zuverlässig funktionieren, zeigt auch der aktuelle Fall aus Südkorea.
Samsung erwischt ungünstigen Zeitpunkt
Im Samsung-Community-Forum berichten viele Nutzer:innen, dass ihre Kühlschränke nicht mehr funktionierten, wodurch Lebensmittel verdarben. Auch die automatische Türöffnungsfunktion und die Innenbeleuchtung seien bei einigen Geräten ausgefallen. Ein:e Samsung-Vertreter:in bestätigte das Problem am 22. September: „Gestern trat während des Testprozesses für ein Software-Update für Samsung-Kühlschränke ein Fehler auf. Bei einigen Kund:innen wurden Störungen bei der Stromversorgung und der Anzeige des Kühlschranks festgestellt“, heißt es in der Antwort des Unternehmens. „Wir ergreifen derzeit mit höchster Priorität Notfallmaßnahmen über den Kund:innen-Service von Samsung Electronics.“
ZDNet Korea vermutet, dass das Update aufgrund eines Systemfehlers an die Kund:innen ausgespielt wurde. Ein:e Samsung-Sprecher:in teilte gegenüber der Redaktion allerdings mit, dass das fehlerhafte Update inzwischen gestoppt worden sei. Das Unternehmen riet Betroffenen, sich an den Kund:innen-Support zu wenden. Viele forderten neben der Reparatur ihrer Geräte aber auch eine Entschädigung für die verdorbenen Lebensmittel. Für koreanische Nutzer:innen kam das Problem zu einem besonders ungünstigen Zeitpunkt, da das Land am Freitag den Chuseok-Feiertag begeht. Dabei handelt es sich um eines der wichtigsten traditionellen Feste Koreas, das oft auch als koreanisches Erntedankfest bezeichnet wird.

articles.title: Your Employees Work Everywhere. Your Infrastructure Has to Follow Them - Tech Guide
articles.text:
For most of the history of corporate IT, infrastructure was built around a place. Employees travelled to an office, connected to a corporate network and accessed applications running in a company data centre.
The boundaries were relatively obvious. IT knew where users were, where applications lived and which networks connected them.
That model has largely disappeared, but many organisations are still operating technology environments shaped by its assumptions.
An employee might now start the day answering emails from home, join a video meeting while travelling, access a cloud-based CRM from a customer site and return to the office in the afternoon. During that same day, they may move between Microsoft 365, an ERP platform, an AI assistant, collaboration software and several SaaS applications. Customers and partners are similarly distributed.
The workplace has become geographically fluid, while the technology supporting it has become more interconnected.
This creates an infrastructure challenge that is easy to underestimate. The objective is no longer simply to connect offices. It is to give people reliable and secure access to the applications, data and services they need, regardless of where any of those things happen to be.
The Office Is No Longer the Centre of the Network
Traditional corporate networks were designed around predictable traffic. Employees connected inside the office and most important applications lived within environments controlled by the organisation. Even remote access was generally treated as an exception to normal working patterns.
Cloud computing, SaaS and hybrid work reversed that relationship.
For many employees, travelling through the corporate office network to reach an application hosted somewhere else can make less sense than connecting directly to the service. At the same time, organisations still need to maintain security, visibility and consistent performance across those interactions.
AI is adding another layer. Employees increasingly use cloud-based AI tools alongside traditional enterprise applications, while software vendors embed AI functionality directly into their platforms. The modern working session may therefore involve connections between a user, identity provider, cloud application, corporate dataset, AI service and several external APIs.
The network has not disappeared. It has become distributed.
That distinction matters because infrastructure strategies designed primarily around locations can struggle when work is increasingly organised around identities, applications and data.
Employees Experience Infrastructure Differently From IT Teams
Infrastructure teams naturally monitor technical indicators such as uptime, latency, bandwidth utilisation and availability. Employees experience infrastructure through something much simpler: whether they can get their work done.
Those two perspectives do not always align.
A network can technically be available while an employee waits repeatedly for a cloud application to respond. Wi-Fi can remain online while video calls become unstable. A remote worker can successfully authenticate yet encounter enough latency to make a business application frustrating to use.
None of these situations necessarily creates a major incident. That is precisely why they can persist.
Employees are remarkably good at adapting to small technology problems. They reconnect to meetings, switch networks, restart applications and create manual workarounds. After a while, they stop raising tickets because they assume the inconvenience is simply part of the system.
This creates a blind spot for organisations. The absence of support tickets does not necessarily indicate the absence of technology friction.
A useful principle for modern infrastructure teams is that reliability should be measured not only by whether systems are available, but by whether people can use them without repeatedly thinking about the infrastructure underneath them.
More Flexibility Creates More Dependencies
There is an operational contradiction at the centre of the modern workplace. Businesses have made technology more flexible for employees while simultaneously making the environment supporting that flexibility more complex.
A salesperson can work from almost anywhere, but their productivity may depend on home broadband, identity services, cloud connectivity, CRM availability, collaboration platforms and security controls all functioning together.
When everything works, that complexity is invisible.
When something fails, ownership becomes much less obvious.
Is the problem the employee’s connection? The corporate network? The cloud provider? The application vendor? Authentication? A security policy? An integration?
Modern technology incidents increasingly cross organisational and vendor boundaries. This means one of the biggest infrastructure challenges is no longer simply fixing individual components. It is understanding the relationships between them.
The complexity is in the connections.
AI Will Put Even More Pressure on Connectivity
The next phase of workplace technology will make this issue more pronounced.
Generative AI is moving from standalone chat interfaces into productivity suites, customer service platforms, development tools, analytics environments and enterprise applications. Increasingly, an employee will not consciously “use AI”. It will simply be part of the applications they already use.
This matters for infrastructure because AI often depends on access to data and services distributed across multiple environments. An employee may request an AI-generated analysis that requires information from a cloud application, corporate database and external service before returning a useful result.
As these interactions become routine, connectivity becomes part of AI performance.
A sophisticated application is of limited value if employees cannot reliably reach the systems and data it depends upon.
This is where managed infrastructure becomes relevant to a broader operational conversation. Monitoring networks, maintaining secure connectivity and understanding performance across hybrid environments are no longer background IT tasks when so much of the employee experience depends on them.
The Cost of Poor Connectivity Is Usually Distributed
A major outage is easy to calculate. Systems stop, employees cannot work and customers may be affected.
Persistent minor friction is harder.
Imagine 500 employees each losing only several minutes per day to slow connections, unstable calls, authentication delays or applications that intermittently fail to respond. There may never be an incident serious enough to reach senior management, yet the accumulated productivity loss can be substantial.
More importantly, technology friction changes behaviour.
Employees avoid unreliable tools. Teams develop alternative workflows. People download information locally because accessing the central system feels too slow. Departments adopt new software to solve problems they believe existing technology cannot handle.
Infrastructure problems can therefore create application sprawl and process inconsistency elsewhere in the organisation.
This is why apparently small connectivity problems deserve more attention than their individual severity suggests. Operational friction compounds.
Infrastructure Has to Follow the Business
The most important change may ultimately be conceptual.
Businesses once built infrastructure around buildings. Increasingly, they need to build connectivity around people, applications and data.
That means understanding how employees actually work rather than assuming where they work. It means considering customer and partner access alongside internal connectivity. It also means recognising that cloud adoption, AI and SaaS are making the corporate technology environment more distributed rather than less dependent on infrastructure.
The organisations that handle this transition well will not necessarily be those with the newest networking technology. They will be the ones that make complexity least visible to the people trying to do their jobs.
As work continues moving across offices, homes, customer locations, cloud platforms and increasingly AI-enabled applications, managed infrastructure becomes less about maintaining a traditional corporate network and more about sustaining secure, reliable connections across a business that no longer has one obvious technological centre.
Employees should not need to understand that complexity.
They should simply be able to work wherever the business requires them to be.

articles.title: Google Maps déploie une nouveauté sur les feux et stops qui va vous épargner bien des amendes
articles.text:
Google Maps déploie une nouveauté sur les feux et stops qui va vous épargner bien des amendes
Google Maps affiche désormais les feux et les stops dans l’alerte du prochain virage pour vous éviter les mauvaises surprises.
Les feux et les stops sont annoncés depuis maintenant six ans sur la carte de Google Maps, mais leur affichage restait bien trop discret pour être réellement efficace en conduisant. Pour éviter de se faire surprendre par ces signalisations à un embranchement, une récente mise à jour sur Android Auto vient les intégrer directement dans l’alerte visuelle du prochain changement de direction.
Google Maps : une alerte visuelle pour anticiper les feux et panneaux stop
Jusqu’à présent, ces signalisations se limitaient à un affichage purement informatif qui n’aidait pas vraiment à anticiper en temps réel, sans compter que ces repères se retrouvaient souvent masqués par le tracé bleu ou le curseur de navigation au moment précis d’aborder le croisement.
Il aura finalement fallu attendre septembre 2026 pour que Google Maps rectifie le tir avec un ajustement bien pensé. Désormais, les feux tricolores et les panneaux stop apparaissent directement au sein du bandeau d’indication flottant, là où s’affiche habituellement le nom de la prochaine rue.
D’un coup d’œil rapide sur l’écran de bord, vous savez ainsi exactement à quoi vous attendre avant même d’amorcer votre manœuvre. Ce changement s’avère particulièrement utile dans les zones urbaines denses ou inconnues, où un panneau dissimulé derrière un obstacle, ou plusieurs signalisations successives, peuvent vite provoquer un refus de priorité involontaire. Résultat : un coup de frein brusque ou une lourde amende si la police se trouve dans le coin.
Android Auto et Apple CarPlay : un déploiement progressif et des bugs persistants
Déjà observée sur Android Auto ainsi que sur smartphone, cette nouveauté visuelle devrait également s’étendre prochainement aux utilisateurs d’Apple CarPlay. Comme souvent, Google procède à un déploiement progressif côté serveur, qui s’étalera sur quelques jours ou quelques semaines.
Outre ce changement, Google court toujours après les bugs liés à l’affichage de la limitation et du compteur de vitesse sur Android Auto, tout en apportant des nouveautés. En parallèle, des utilisateurs se plaignent d’une mésaventure qui peut coûter très cher en PV : le basculement inopiné de l’affichage en miles par heure (mph) à la place des km/h.

articles.title: 600 000 cartes bancaires piratées : trois IA ont compromis des centaines de boutiques en ligne
articles.text:
Les chercheurs de Gambit Security révèlent avoir découvert une nouvelle campagne de piratage entièrement pilotée par l’intelligence artificielle. Survenue entre juillet et septembre 2026, l’attaque a permis de compromettre au moins 119 sites marchands. Sur ces sites, les IA ont dérobé plus de 600 000 numéros de carte bancaire non expirées.
Les investigations pointent du doigt un cybercriminel isolé, résidant en Chine. Dans les faits, son rôle s’est résumé à donner de brèves instructions à ses agents d’IA… avant de les laisser travailler seuls pendant des heures, sans la moindre supervision.
« L’attaque a été menée de façon presque entièrement autonome », estime Gambit Security, qui a pu analyser le serveur de commande du pirate.
Trois IA impliquées dans la cyberattaque
Trois intelligences artificielles open source sont à l’origine de l’offensive. Dans un premier, le pirate chinois a chargé un agent intitulé Strix de scanner les sites à la recherche de failles de sécurité. Une fois les brèches débusquées, une IA appelée Cairn prenait le relais. En toute autonomie, elle exploitait automatiquement les failles jusqu’à décrocher un accès administrateur.
Dans un troisième temps, un agent baptisé Hermes entrait en scène. C’est cette intelligence artificielle qui pilotait toute la campagne, prenait les décisions stratégiques et dirigeait les deux autres outils, de l’intrusion à la prise de contrôle. Pour fonctionner, l’agent s’appuyait sur le modèle Claude Opus 4.6 d’Anthropic. Entre le 10 et le 15 septembre, l’attaquant a lancé 105 attaques reposant sur cette procédure. Au moins 27 entreprises ont été piratées par le trio sur cette période de cinq jours.
« Là où l’accès a été obtenu, cela prenait généralement moins d’une journée. […] Dans de nombreux cas, il n’a fallu que quelques heures », explique Gambit.
119 sites marchands piégés
Au total, les chercheurs ont recensé 119 sites compromis. Parmi les victimes de l’opération, on trouve une grande chaîne hôtelière du Fortune 500, une importante compagnie aérienne américaine, un distributeur industriel et une enseigne de mode en ligne. Durant l’attaque, les sites ont été infectés par des scripts « skimmers ». Il s’agit de bouts de code malveillant, directement glissés sur les pages de paiement pour intercepter les données bancaires au moment de l’achat.
Quand un internaute entre ses numéros de carte, les scripts s’en emparent, sans que la victime ne se rende compte de quoi que ce soit. Sur un site marchand américain, les pirates ont même installé une tâche automatique qui réinjectait le script malveillant toutes les deux minutes s’il venait à être supprimé.
À lire aussi : 30 000 cartes bancaires françaises sont en vente sur un « Amazon » du dark web
Une cyberattaque rentable
Selon les chercheurs, les agents avaient reçu l’ordre de faire le ménage après leur passage. Une fois les données volées, ils devaient supprimer les informations bancaires directement dans les bases de données des sites compromis. Cette instruction, débusquée dans les fichiers de configuration d’Hermes, a fait des dégâts collatéraux. Dans certains cas, des sauvegardes internes ont été effacées, un peu comme si un ransomware était passé par là.
Les chercheurs estiment que l’attaquant a dépensé entre 12 000 et 18 000 dollars en deux mois pour orchestrer la cyberattaque. Le pirate s’est en effet servi de modèles d’IA facturés à l’usage. Plus il demandait à ses trois IA de pirater des sites, plus il devait débourser de l’argent. L’opération s’est néanmoins avérée très rentable. Rapporté au nombre de cibles, l’opération revient à 25 dollars par entreprise attaquée. La cible la moins chère lui a coûté 3 dollars. Au vu du nombre de cartes de crédit siphonnées, l’attaque peut être considérée comme très lucrative.
À lire aussi : ChatGPT a lancé une nouvelle cyberattaque – le site d’un gouvernement a été piraté
L’attaque démontre que des agents IA sont désormais capables de mener une attaque de bout en bout, sans intervention humaine au cours du processus. Jusqu’ici, ce genre d’opération à grande échelle reposait sur l’expertise d’une équipe de pirates chevronnés. Avec des outils comme Strix, Cairn et Hermes, n’importe quel attaquant, même peu qualifié, peut lancer l’attaque et dégager des bénéfices substantiels. Les chercheurs précisent que l’attaque « se poursuit toujours ».

articles.title: Claude ya está descubriendo nuevos sistemas celulares. El problema es que el cuello de botella de la ciencia no está ahí
articles.text:
Claude ha encontrado en millones de secuencias de ADN un sistema biológico que no había sido caracterizado previamente. Anthropic lo ha llamado ART (Array-associated Reverse Transcriptase o transcriptasa inversa asociada a matrices) y aparece sobre todo en bacteriófagos, que no son otra cosa que virus con la capacidad de infectar a algunos tipos de bacterias. Sí, es el enésimo descubrimiento de una inteligencia artificial (IA). Y con toda seguridad llegarán muchos más. Sin embargo, este hito en biología nos invita a hacernos una pregunta muy importante.
¿Estamos ante auténticos descubrimientos científicos o delante de sistemas extraordinariamente buenos encontrando candidatos que después necesitan pasar por el lento proceso de la ciencia? Las aportaciones que los modelos de IA de frontera ya están haciendo en el ámbito de la investigación científica ponen encima de la mesa este interrogante tan incómodo. Si nos ceñimos al descubrimiento que acaba de hacer Claude, comprobaremos que, una vez más, el conocimiento que ha entregado a los científicos va a desencadenar una nueva línea de investigación.
Y aquí está la clave: descubrir una posibilidad puede llevar horas a una IA, pero demostrar que esa posibilidad es realmente importante puede exigir años de trabajo científico. En esta ocasión, Claude ha identificado una combinación anómala de elementos que había pasado inadvertida y la ha transformado en una hipótesis que los investigadores han llevado al laboratorio. Según Anthropic, su modelo de IA ha examinado más de 200.000 transcriptasas inversas, ha identificado unos 3.500 candidatos y ha seleccionado 20 para un análisis más profundo.
La IA ya está empezando a comprimir años de búsqueda científica
La reflexión que estamos haciendo es pertinente y necesaria. No cabe duda. Pero no debe propiciar que menospreciemos el valor de lo que ya está haciendo la IA en el ámbito de la investigación científica. El auténtico valor de esta tecnología reside en su capacidad de explorar espacios de hipótesis a una velocidad que un investigador humano no puede igualar. Según Anthropic, en este proyecto 950 agentes de Claude trabajaron durante 21 horas y consumieron unos 210 millones de tokens para rastrear esas secuencias.
El auténtico valor de esta tecnología reside en su capacidad de explorar espacios de hipótesis a una velocidad que un investigador humano no puede igualar
Necesitaron solo 21 horas para llevar a cabo su hallazgo. Es asombroso. No obstante, para entender su valor es imprescindible ponerlo en contexto. Los modelos de IA de frontera revisan la literatura, llevan a cabo análisis, buscan anomalías, descartan candidatos y producen informes que posteriormente los científicos pueden llevar al laboratorio. Por el momento es aquí donde reside su valor en este campo. En el cribado científico masivo. Nature describió el pasado 30 de junio este proceso en un artículo interesantísimo.
En cualquier caso, hay un matiz muy importante que merece la pena que no pasemos por alto: no es lo mismo encontrar una anomalía que descubrir para qué sirve. Anthropic lo ha reconocido al presentar ART como un nuevo sistema enzimático con características reminiscentes de CRISPR, pero admitiendo que todavía no sabe cuál es su función. El potencial de este descubrimiento es indudable, pero ahora es necesario llevar a cabo experimentos para averiguar qué hace realmente este sistema celular.
El escenario en el que nos encontramos nos recuerda lo necesario que es mirar con cierta cautela los grandes anuncios de las compañías de IA. Lo sucedido hace solo unos días con OpenAI y su anuncio de la resolución de uno de los Problemas del Milenio, el de existencia y suavidad de Navier-Stokes, nos invita a aceptar estos descubrimientos con un escepticismo sano, aunque no radical. La IA ya está liberando a los investigadores de una parte del trabajo científico, pero el ser humano por el momento continúa sujetando con firmeza el timón debido a que una parte de este esfuerzo todavía no puede ser resuelto por la IA simplemente aumentando el número de agentes.

articles.title: Catalonia deepens India push, targets New Opportunities in AI, deeptech, and semiconductors
articles.text:
Catalonia deepens India push, targets New Opportunities in AI, deeptech, and semiconductors
Minister Miquel Sàmper Rodríguez’s visit comes as Catalan exports to India reach €652 million and the region prepares to open a new office in New Delhi.
Miquel Sàmper Rodríguez, Minister for Business and Labour, Government of Catalonia, is in India to strengthen the growing economic relationship between Catalonia and India and to promote new opportunities in the fields of artificial intelligence, deeptech, healthcare, semiconductors, space technology, energy, and advanced manufacturing.
Catalonia is one of Spain's major economic drivers and a leading European center for industry, technology and innovation with an economy worth €334.8 billion in 2025. Rodríguez’s visit, organized by the Catalan Ministry for Business and Labour and Catalonia Trade & Investment (CTI), the internationalization and investment agency of ACCIÓ, shows Catalonia's ongoing commitment to further strengthen its trade, investment, and business relationships with India.
The visit comes at a time when the commercial relationship is steadily growing. In the last 10 years, exports between Catalonia and India have more than doubled. Catalan exports to India amounted to €652 million in 2025. The relationship is also backed by a strong two-way corporate presence, with 166 companies from both India and Catalonia operating in both markets.
As part of its ongoing dedication to India, Catalonia Trade & Investment is opening a new office in New Delhi this year to complement its existing presence in Mumbai and more than 30 years of activity in the country. The new office will strengthen institutional dialogue and offer more effective support to Indian companies, investors, and institutions looking into opportunities in Catalonia, as well as to Catalan companies that wish to expand operations in India.
Reflecting on the significance of this growing relationship and the goals of his visit, Minister Rodriguez said Catalonia and India already have strong and growing business ties, but there is much more they can do together. “This visit is an opportunity to build on that relationship and create more practical connections between our companies, startups, research institutions, and innovation ecosystems,” he said.
He added that cooperation with Nasscom was an important step in that direction, particularly in areas such as AI, deeptech, semiconductors, healthtech, energytech and spacetech. “We want to see these connections translate into new investments, partnerships, and opportunities for companies on both sides.”
Focusing on next-generation Sectors
The minister will be holding talks with important government and industrial stakeholders, such as Manjinder Singh Sirsa, Minister of Industries, Food & Supplies and Environment, Forest & Wildlife (Government of NCT of Delhi), and representatives of major industry associations including FICCI and NASSCOM. The discussions will concentrate on the possibilities for greater economic cooperation, trade and investment, especially in sectors in which Catalonia and India have complementary strengths.
Barcelona has emerged as an international technology hub; IBM's Global Location Trends 2025 show that it ranks third in the world and first in the European Union for attracting foreign investment projects in artificial intelligence, with only London and Singapore ahead of it.
Another area with great potential is healthcare and life sciences. Catalonia is presently the fourth region in the world and the leading one in Europe for attracting foreign technology investment projects related to digital health.
Manjinder Singh Sirsa, Minister of Industries, Food & Supplies and Environment, Forest & Wildlife (Government of NCT of Delhi), said
Delhi is emerging as a strong hub for industry, technology and innovation. “We see good potential to strengthen our engagement with Catalonia and create new opportunities for investment, technology partnerships, and business collaboration. The visit is a welcome opportunity to take this relationship forward.”
Kalyan Kumar, President, HCL Software, shared his belief that sovereignty isn't about isolation, but is about choice. “Catalonia's strength in cybersecurity talent, AI and deeptech, and its place among Europe's largest ICT hubs, reflects the shift we're building for. Enterprises deciding where their software runs, where their data resides, and how their AI is governed, without external dependencies.
“Our IP-led engineering 'F1 squad' across experience, data, and intelligent operations, alongside our team on the ground in Catalonia, exists to partner with local enterprises and service providers to co-create secure, sovereign, scalable digital solutions. We're glad to host Minister Miquel Sàmper and the Catalonia delegation at HCLTech (HCLSoftware), Kumar said.
Turning business interest into investment opportunities
The visit occurs at a time when new investment opportunities are emerging between Catalonia and India. Barcelona-based technology company Submer has proposed an investment of $2 billion in Madhya Pradesh's semiconductor ecosystem, which is expected to generate about 5,000 direct jobs. This shows the potential for Catalan technology and expertise to play an important role in India's rapidly growing high-tech economy.
The Catalonia Trade & Investment–NASSCOM Letter of Intent (LOI) represents yet another potential turning point. Its aim is to stimulate business, technology and investment connections, to link up companies, startups and research institutions, to promote collaboration in the areas of AI, deeptech, semiconductors, healthtech, energytech and spacetech, and to help business delegations and innovation exchanges.
Shivendra Singh, Vice President, Global Trade Development at NASSCOM, said Catalonia offers a strong gateway for Indian technology companies to deepen their presence in Spain and the wider European market. “This collaboration will create greater opportunities for NASSCOM member companies to build partnerships, explore new markets, and expand their business and investment footprint through Catalonia, particularly in AI and other strategic technology areas such as Health tech, Energy and Space technologies,” he said.
Barcelona as a gateway to Europe
The minister's visit also underlines Barcelona and Catalonia's wider role as a global destination for technology, innovation, entrepreneurship, and international business.
Through events such as Mobile World Congress and Catalonia’s thriving technology ecosystem and increasing expertise in AI, healthcare, and deeptech, Indian companies and investors are able to gain access to European markets and open the door for Catalan businesses to expand operations in India.
Tapping the existing relationship, the minister’s current visit is opening up new possibilities with regard to investment, innovation, technology partnerships and market access between the two regions.

articles.title: Netatmo lance sa nouvelle tête thermostatique, bien moins cher — Frandroid
articles.text:
Même si cela semble difficile à croire à la vue des températures, l’été touche bel et bien à sa fin et l’hiver va bientôt pointer à l’horizon. Aucune surprise donc à voir Netatmo revenir avec une solution prête pour l’allumage du chauffage.
La Tête Thermostatique Original se pose sur les radiateurs à eau chaude et gère la température de chaque pièce séparément. Elle communique en Zigbee, un protocole radio basse consommation pensé pour les objets connectés, et rejoint l’écosystème Matter par l’intermédiaire d’une passerelle maison, le Thermo Hub. Concrètement, ce hub sert de pont vers Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, SmartThings et Home Assistant, sans intégration spécifique à chaque plateforme.
Côté caractéristiques, Netatmo annonce 18 mois d’autonomie avec deux piles AA, un moteur plus silencieux que l’ancienne génération et jusqu’à 24 têtes par système, de quoi couvrir une grande maison. Une tête seule coûte 60 euros ; le pack avec le Thermo Hub monte à 120 euros, utile pour ceux qui partent de zéro. La marque prévoit aussi un Thermostat Additionnel à 100 euros pour piloter plusieurs zones et un répéteur Zigbee à 20 euros, dont la disponibilité au lancement n’est pas confirmée.
Deux passerelles pour un seul logement
C’est là que ça coince pour les clients historiques. En passant au Zigbee, Netatmo abandonne son ancien protocole radio propriétaire sans prévoir de pont entre les deux mondes. Les nouvelles têtes ne communiquent donc ni avec l’ancien thermostat Netatmo ni avec les anciennes vannes de la marque.
Migrer petit à petit reste possible, mais oblige à conserver deux passerelles et deux installations distinctes le temps de tout remplacer. Autrement dit, un foyer déjà équipé garde son ancien système en marche d’un côté, monte le nouveau de l’autre, et pilote les deux séparément jusqu’au bout de la transition. La nouvelle tête est livrée avec six adaptateurs pour se fixer sur la plupart des radiateurs déjà munis d’une tête thermostatique.
Un pari sur l’écosystème plutôt que sur la vanne
Netatmo arrive après la concurrence sur ce terrain. Aqara propose déjà avec sa W600 une tête compatible Zigbee et Thread, utilisable en Matter sans passerelle maison et annoncée jusqu’à deux ans d’autonomie. La réponse française mise plutôt sur l’intégration : gérer chaudière, radiateurs et différentes zones de chauffe depuis une seule application. Elle peut aussi mettre en avant la conception réalisée en France.
En revanche, si Netatmo vantait la fabrication en Europe dans les usines Legrand de son Thermostat Original, on peut pas en dire autant de la nouvelle tête. En effet, présent lors de l’annonce, Frandroid a pu poser la question aux équipes, la marque admet que la fabrication de la tête se fait en Asie, bien loin de l’Europe.
À 60 euros, le chauffage pièce par pièce devient plus abordable pour un nouveau venu. Pour un foyer déjà équipé en Netatmo, l’addition grimpe : il faut racheter le Thermo Hub, remplacer les têtes et vivre avec deux systèmes en parallèle. La disponibilité en dehors de la France n’a pas encore été précisée.

articles.title: Disney+ raises prices again as ad-free plan climbs to more than three times its launch price
articles.text:
What just happened? Sick of streaming services constantly increasing their prices? Given that Disney is making Disney+ and Hulu more expensive, again, it appears that these companies just don't care, frankly. The increase comes exactly one year since the two services introduced their last price hike. Disney is trying to appease angry customers by pointing out that the increases aren't as high as those introduced by competitors.
The standalone ad-free plans for Disney+ and Hulu are each increasing from $18.99 to $21.49 per month – a $2.50 rise, or approximately 13.2%. The ad-free Disney+/Hulu bundle goes up by $2, from $19.99 to $21.99 per month.
The standalone ad-supported plans are each increasing by 50 cents, from $11.99 to $12.49 per month. However, the ad-supported Disney+/Hulu bundle, the most popular option, remains unchanged at $12.99 per month.
That means the two-service bundles cost just 50 cents more than either corresponding standalone subscription. Compared with buying both services separately, the bundles save approximately 48% with ads and 49% without ads.
The largest monthly increases across the wider lineup affect Hulu + Live TV: its standard and Premium packages each rise by $10, to $99.99 and $109.99, respectively.
Disney spouted the usual lines about investing in enhancements, such as new technology, features, and personalization, to strengthen the value it offers subscribers. It also pointed out that competitors have introduced larger price increases.
"While competitors have raised prices by an average of 13% this year, we are keeping the price of our most popular bundle unchanged and have increased our standalone ad-supported offerings by just 4%," a Disney spokesperson told TechRadar.
Disney has raised the US monthly price of Disney+'s ad-free subscription six times since launch, once each year from 2021 through 2026. The service arrived in November 2019 at $6.99 per month, rising to $7.99 in 2021, $10.99 in 2022, $13.99 in 2023, $15.99 in 2024 and $18.99 in 2025, before reaching $21.49 in September 2026. That's $14.50 more per month – a 207.4% increase, making the ad-free service just over three times its original price.
It's not just Disney, of course. The eight major subscription services now cost slightly more than $151 a month combined for ad-free plans purchased separately, without bundles, compared with roughly $90 for a similar lineup four years ago. That's far above the rate of inflation: consumer prices have increased by an average of 3.84% annually since 2019.

articles.title: There's a new way to break RSA that's faster than anything we've seen before
articles.text:
The world has known for decades that the RSA cryptosystem’s days are numbered. Once quantum computing becomes practical (estimates for that range from 3 to 20 or more years), the foundational security it provides will crumble. New research has revealed a novel method that uses classical computing to reduce the current RSA security level to an unacceptably low threshold.
The practical risk is limited, but still significant. Applying the attack against the deprecated use of 1024-bit keys took a handful of months on an academic CPU cluster, significantly less than the current estimates for 1024-bit factoring that would require resources that only nations or companies with massive resources could achieve. Widely used RSA implementations are also safe.
Nonetheless, the research has taken cryptographers by surprise because it introduces signature forgery, a new way to break RSA keys without factoring. Equally important, this novel method reduces the required computing resources by orders of magnitude.
Out of reach no more
“If this result holds up under peer review, it would indeed be a conceptual break-through,” Karsten Nohl, a cryptography expert and the head of innovation at Allurity, said in an interview. “RSA is as difficult to break as it is to factor large integers, at least so we thought. The researcher suggests that you can practically break RSA without cracking its key.”
Nadia Heninger, a University of California at San Diego professor and lead author, elaborated:
Cryptographers thought that the only way to compute valid RSA digital signatures was to first compute the private key by factoring, and then use the private key to compute the signatures. For 1024-bit RSA, this was thought to be very expensive, albeit probably doable if you have the computational resources of the large tech companies or the NSA—on the order of tens of millions of dollars of computation time for a single key. For 2048-bit RSA, it was thought to be totally out of reach.
The key forgery attack Heninger and the other researchers devised poses an immediate threat to 1024-bit RSA. Even for 2048- and 4096-bit keys, the method reduces the security of RSA to unacceptable levels. The National Security Agency, National Institute of Standards and Technology, and European Union Agency for Network and Information Security require that any cryptosystem should provide a level of no less than 128 or more bits, meaning the operations required must exceed 2128.
Most people (myself included) have no idea how some of this wizardry works on a technical level, but basic computer functions we take for granted and/or require depend on cryptography.
It's both frightening and awe inspiring to see how a clever set of minds can undercut what previously looked like a sturdy wall into an abbatoir. And there's always a nagging worry about who found this first and when.
So, lets do the math with current tech. No sci-fi involved.
1,380 core-years corresponds to approximately 12.09 million core-hours, which translates to roughly 63,000 to 94,500 wall-clock hours on a single modern high-density CPU socket, or roughly 200 to 600 hours on a single modern high-end GPU.
Under an optimized CUDA pipeline (yielding a conservative 250×–500× throughput advantage over a standard single CPU core), a single high-end GPU would complete the computation in approximately 24,000 to 48,000 hours.
A contemporary current-gen GPU cluster with a mere 64-128 racks (basically a large dedicated basement floor less than a quarther of Langley), housing 4,000 GPUs ... would finish this in about 6-12 hours.
You can find universities with that kind of compute. Allowing it to take a few days ups the pool as well.

and to add to that - energy usage (not that it's - a huge factor, but I found it interesting to think about 🙂)
assuming: H200 servers running 8 GPUs each @ 10.2kw, you'd end up using 5.1 mw for 6-12 hours, or ~ 30-60 mwh. Quite possibly higher (I'm not factoring in networking, cooling, power losses etc).
Enough to drive a 4 mi/kwh car 120,000 miles

articles.title: Funcionários da Toyota treinam robôs para executar suas funções • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Funcionários da Toyota treinam robôs para executar suas funções
Montadora japonesa afirma que ideia não é substituir os trabalhadores. Toyota planeja investir US$ 6,4 bilhões por ano em automação a partir de 2028.
A Toyota é mais uma grande montadora a investir em inteligência artificial. Funcionários da empresa japonesa estão treinando robôs humanoides para executar tarefas nas linhas de produção. No entanto, a Toyota afirma que não pretende substituir esses trabalhadores.
Segundo o Nikkei Asia, o objetivo da Toyota é investir US$ 6,4 bilhões (R$ 31,5 bilhões, em conversão direta) por ano a partir de 2028 para inserir mais robôs em suas fábricas, alcançando 400 mil unidades de robôs distribuídos entre os processos da empresa.
Além da gigante japonesa, outras fabricantes pelo mundo já têm robôs atuando em suas linhas de produção. Entre elas estão a sul-coreana Hyundai, que utiliza modelos Atlas da Boston Dynamics, e a chinesa BYD, com modelo de fabricação própria.
Os robôs ELEY têm design sobre rodas com dois braços e mãos, que serão utilizados em trabalhos de precisão. O treinamento é realizado pelos próprios funcionários das fábricas, em uma espécie de “estágio”. Segundo o site Ars Technica, os trabalhadores utilizam moldes baseados nas mãos dos robôs para realizar algumas tarefas que envolvem maior precisão. Os movimentos serão integrados ao aprendizado de máquina e reproduzidos pelos próprios humanoides em algum momento.
Vale lembrar que, em junho deste ano, cerca de 300 funcionários da Ford foram recontratados para atuar no treinamento da IA implementada pela montadora, numa tentativa de corrigir falhas no processo de automação. Apesar de ser um indicativo de como a força de trabalho humana continua sendo essencial, não é raro ver casos de demissões em massa após esse período.
Essa nova função de treinamento para os trabalhadores humanos vem em meio aos receios com o futuro da inteligência artificial pelo mundo. Um relatório recente do Pew Research Center destacou o temor da população em relação à IA no ambiente profissional, inclusive no Japão e nos Estados Unidos, países que concentram cerca de 70 fábricas da Toyota.
Antes mesmo dos robôs humanoides, as montadoras já utilizavam modelos industriais em suas linhas de produção. Braços mecânicos e outros componentes automatizados fazem parte dos processos de fabricação de peças, montagem e mais etapas.
Segundo a Federação Internacional de Robótica, o Japão é o segundo país com maior presença de robôs industriais, com mais de 450 mil unidades registradas em 2024, seguido dos Estados Unidos, com 34,2 mil. O mercado é liderado pela China, com 2 milhões de modelos empregados.
Considerando os novos robôs humanoides, também há uma tendência no mercado automotivo, com diversas montadoras pelo mundo adotando o uso de IA física. Em junho, a vice-presidente executiva da BYD, Stella Li, afirmou que a fabricação de unidades do tipo é facilitada pelas semelhanças entre as tecnologias utilizadas no desenvolvimento de hardware e software para os carros elétricos.

articles.title: Google Photos 'Clueless'-inspired virtual closet is now available on Android and iOS | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s new AI-powered feature that turns photos of your outfits into a virtual closet — one seemingly inspired by Cher’s iconic virtual wardrobe app featured in the movie “Clueless” — is now available to everyone in the U.S., Brazil, and India, on both iOS and Android devices.
The company announced the feature earlier this year with plans to begin the rollout in the summer. Android users gained access first, starting in June, and now the virtual closet is available to all Android and iOS users in the supported markets.
The idea of a digital closet in “Clueless” was meant to highlight Cher’s privileged life, where she had so many outfits that she needed a digital system to help her choose what to wear and keep everything organized. Now, you don’t have to be a rich Beverly Hills teenager to take advantage of such technology.
Instead, Google uses AI technology to create a copy of your wardrobe, based on the items you wore in your photos. From the app, you can also filter items by category — like tops, bottoms, jewelry, and more — then mix and match them to create different outfits.
Google says the feature is designed to assist the user, and the data about how you dress or what you wear is not being shared with third parties, like retailers.
The broader rollout of the virtual closet feature arrives alongside a handful of other Google Photos updates, including a way to select, brighten, and share photos using a single prompt in Gemini Spark, an upgraded markup tool, and more Remix templates that use AI to transform your photos. (The Gemini Spark feature requires a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription in the U.S.)
With Markup, you’ll be able to use a redacting pen to blur sensitive information like license plates, access precise thickness sliders for custom sketches, and pick from different fonts when adding text to photos.
For Android users, there are also new photo filters, called “Moods,” that let you give your images different looks, like 35mm film, 2000s digicam, and more.

articles.title: Micron discontinues 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs as it pivots toward higher-density memory for AI — chipmaker reportedly pivots to high-margin 3GB silicon for AI GPUs
articles.text:
Micron discontinues 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs as it pivots toward higher-density memory for AI — chipmaker reportedly pivots to high-margin 3GB silicon for AI GPUs
Samsung and SK Hynix already lead the 2GB GDDR7 market
Micron is reportedly pulling the plug on its 2 GB (16Gb) GDDR7 memory chips, ending production and sales of both the 28 Gbps and 32 Gbps variants. According to an X post by UNIKO’s Hardware, the chips — some of which shipped on some GeForce RTX 50 graphics cards — are now designated as “End of Life” on Micron's site. Tom’s Hardware can confirm that the pages for module norms return “No results found.”
Micron just began supplying its 2GB GDDR7 to Nvidia earlier this year, with Samsung and SK Hynix being the main GDDR7 suppliers. As a result, Micron's 2GB module only shipped on a few Nvidia models, such as retail variants of the GeForce RTX 5060. Samsung and SK Hynix cover the vast bulk of 2 GB GDDR7 modules for the standard RTX 50 retail lineup, so the risk of immediate shortages is minimal. Micron’s uncompetitive position in the 2 GB segment also appears to have made a fast exit logical to free up fabrication capacity.
The company is reportedly shifting its focus toward higher-density 3 GB (24 Gb) GDDR7 chips. These larger packages are considered impractical for Nvidia's RTX 50 lineup because they are more expensive and result in less conventional consumer memory capacities. However, they yield higher profit margins and are actively utilized in Nvidia's high-end RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs tailored for generative and agentic AI workloads.
Micron’s decision follows the ongoing trend of memory suppliers prioritizing AI-facing technologies over their consumer and retail counterparts. The company exited its Crucial consumer memory and SSD business earlier, explicitly saying that surging AI data-center demand had prompted it to prioritize larger strategic customers in faster-growing segments.

articles.title: Gemini estrena una función que hace llamadas por ti desde el móvil
articles.text:
Pedirle a la IA que llame al supermercado para saber si ya llegaron tus galletas favoritas ya no suena a una escena de ciencia ficción. Google implementó una función que permite a Gemini tomar el control de tu móvil para que realice llamadas por ti sin que digas una sola palabra.
De acuerdo con 9to5Google, la nueva función se conoce como "Llamar por mí" y habilita a Gemini para que realice llamadas telefónicas reales en tu nombre. A diferencia de las herramientas de llamadas asistidas de Google, esta versión puede hablar con una persona real y compartir información personal que autorices. Gemini marcará desde tu móvil usando tu número, por lo que pasará los filtros que bloquean los sistemas automatizados.
Durante la llamada, Gemini se presentará como un asistente de IA que actúa en tu nombre y aclara que la llamada puede ser grabada. El usuario puede seguir todo en tiempo real a través de una transcripción en vivo y se ofrece la opción de tomar el control de la conversación en cualquier momento presionando un botón. En teoría, no tendrías que preocuparte de que la herramienta se haga pasar por ti, emule tu voz o realice cosas que no le pediste, ya que Google ni lo permitirá.
Gemini puede llamar para preguntar si un producto está disponible en una tienda, reservar mesa en un restaurante, cambiar la fecha de una cita ya programada o pedir que aparten un artículo. La IA también es capaz de navegar en los menús automáticos de esos sistemas telefónicos que te hacen marcar mil opciones antes de hablar con alguien, o esperar hasta que un humano atienda.
Gemini puede llamar por ti, pero no a todos los números
A pesar de que "Llamar por mí" suena práctica, existen algunas limitantes impuestas por Google para su nueva función. De entrada, esta característica solo está disponible para quienes tienen un Pixel 11 y pagan una suscripción de Gemini en Estados Unidos. El gigante tecnológico dijo que se trata de un experimento a pequeña escala, ya que las conversaciones del mundo real son impredecibles y necesita pulir su IA para que responda como se espera.
Gemini no puede llamar a servicios de emergencia como el 911 o 112, ni realizar compras usando los datos de tu tarjeta de crédito. La IA tampoco puede transmitir información sensible, como contraseñas, historiales médicos o números de seguridad social. Por último, los usuarios no podrán aprovecharse de esta característica para hacer llamadas de telemarketing, así que olvídate de que te sirva para vender algo.
Para usar "Llamar por mí", solo necesitas abrir la app de Gemini y pedirle a la IA que haga la llamada. Por ejemplo, puedes escribir un prompt que diga "Llama al restaurante X y reserva mesa para dos a las 7 de la tarde mañana". Gemini mostrará un resumen de la tarea antes de marcar, incluyendo el número de teléfono al que llamará y los datos que compartirá para que le des luz verde.
En la web de ayuda, Google aconseja que seas específico con las fechas, horarios y preferencias para obtener los mejores resultados. Una vez terminada la llamada, te llegará una notificación con el resultado y podrás revisar tanto el resumen como la transcripción completa desde el historial de la app Teléfono.
Aunque todo suena muy bien a primera vista, Google avisó que hay un límite diario de llamadas, por lo que si te gastas tu cuota, tendrás que esperar hasta el día siguiente.

articles.title: Apple iPhone 'Antennagate' Q&A video emerges online 16 years later
articles.text:
Remember that time Apple blamed iPhone signal issues on how people were holding the phone?
Believe it or not, that was 16 years ago (oh my god, I’m getting old!) with the iPhone 4. ‘Antennagate’ was quite the story at the time, and it’s making a comeback after a recording of Apple’s 47-minute Q&A session with reporters showed up on YouTube.
Spotted by Daring Fireball’s John Gruber (who also attended the press conference all the way back on July 16, 2010), this recording seems to be the first video of the Q&A portion itself.
The press conference included a prepared presentation from Steve Jobs that lasted about 30 minutes, followed by the lengthy Q&A session with Jobs, then COO Tim Cook (who just handed over the CEO role to John Ternus), and hardware chief Bob Mansfield.
The prepared presentation has been available online for a while, initially hosted by Apple itself, but after the company removed it, various copies floated around YouTube. But according to Gruber, all the videos cut off before the Q&A portion. That makes this video particularly notable, especially for the way it shows Jobs’ thoughtfulness when answering questions.
Unfortunately, it’s not entirely clear where this recording originated from, or how this YouTube channel got hold of it. But whatever the answers are there, it’s worth a watch.
