articles.title: Google Cloud pushes Gemini deeper into India’s businesses
articles.text:
Google Cloud pushes Gemini deeper into India’s businesses
At an event in Bengaluru, Google Cloud outlined its India strategy, which combines Gemini AI models and infrastructure, to take AI from pilots into production environments via industry partnerships.
Google Cloud is expanding its agentic AI push in India through partnerships that demonstrate how AI is moving from assistance to action.
At its first ‘Let’s Talk AI’ media tour stop in Bengaluru on Thursday, the company highlighted collaborations with boAt, Cropin and Pine Labs across consumer hardware, agriculture and commerce.
Together, they showed Google Cloud’s strategy of pairing its Gemini AI models with sector-specific data, devices, software and payment infrastructure.
The company’s broader pitch is built around an integrated AI stack, including infrastructure, local processing for its latest Gemini models, and Gemini Enterprise, its platform for deploying AI agents.
“As Indian organisations move beyond pilots to rethink how work gets done, they need sovereign flexibility alongside trusted models and enterprise-grade platforms,” said Amit Kumar, Managing Director of Digital Natives Business at Google Cloud India.
The company said Google Cloud customers adopting AI products use 1.8 times as many products on an average compared to customers that do not.
What the partnerships are working on
Google Cloud is working with boAt's parent company Imagine Marketing on Crest AI, boAt's platform for next-generation audio devices. Gemini Live is intended to enable conversational voice interactions, while the broader experience supports functions including translation and selected Google Workspace tasks.
Cropin offers a different use case. Its Sage platform, originally launched in 2024, uses Gemini alongside agricultural and geospatial data to answer questions about crops, climate and food production.
Pine Labs is most directly connected to agentic commerce. Its collaboration with Google Cloud is aimed at helping India’s stated 6 crore small and medium businesses participate in AI-led buying. An AI advertising agent will help merchants create campaigns across Search, YouTube and Pine Labs' point-of-sale devices, while Jarvis, a multi-agent system built on Gemini Enterprise, is intended to assist with merchant operations and customer support.
On the payment side, Pine Labs said its P3P layer can handle transactions within an agentic flow, initially through UPI, while the Grantex protocol is designed to make transactions auditable and aligned with Indian financial regulatory requirements. Pine Labs also plans support for Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), an open standard developed by Google to allow AI agents and commerce systems to exchange information across the shopping journey.
Google introduced UCP in January 2026 and later added support for real-time product information, carts and identity linking. At the Google I/O event in May, it introduced Universal Cart, designed to connect shopping activity across Search, Gemini, YouTube and Gmail. Mastercard demonstrated an authenticated agentic-commerce transaction in India in February, while Visa announced a collaboration with OpenAI in June to support Visa payments within agentic commerce.
Google is also building the supporting enterprise machinery alongside these partnerships. The company is expanding its Forward-Deployed Engineer organisation in India, placing Google AI specialists within customer environments to help move projects into production. Gemini Enterprise has also been expanded with support for long-running agents and centralised governance.
The wider question is whether AI agents can operate reliably enough to handle real-world tasks and transactions. Google Cloud is addressing this challenge through governance, cost controls, security and infrastructure, apart from refining its models. India is becoming an increasingly important deployment market for Google as far as agentic AI is concerned.
Last year, Google Cloud said it was expanding local AI hardware capacity using its AI Hypercomputer architecture and Trillium TPUs, allowing customers to train and serve Gemini models in India. The company operates cloud infrastructure regions in Mumbai and Delhi.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Rachat de SFR : 5 000 emplois menacés d'ici 2029, les salariés en grève ce jeudi
articles.text:
Article mis à jour à 15 h 24 pour ajouter la déclaration du consortium.
Alors que le rachat de SFR pour quelque 20 milliards d’euros est acté depuis juin 2026, les conséquences sociales de l’opération commencent à se dessiner. Plusieurs actions se dessinent.
D’un côté, le CSE de l’entreprise, autrement dit les délégués du personnel, attaque les futurs propriétaires, à savoir les trois autres grands opérateurs historiques : Orange, Bouygues et Iliad (Free). De l’autre, on apprend dans Ouest France qu’une grève aura lieu ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026 dans l’après-midi à l’appel de l’intersyndicale regroupant l’Unsa, la CFDT et la CFTC.
« Colère et détermination »
Le motif de la grève est simple : il doit s’agir d’un « coup de semonce » d’après Olivier Lelong, délégué syndical central CFDT auprès de l’AFP et « faire entendre l’inquiétude » des salariés « leur colère et leur détermination ». « On va continuer le combat jusqu’à ce qu’ils reconsidèrent la situation », prévient Abdelkader Chourkane, élu du CSE et de l’UNsa.
Les futurs patrons ont assurés qu’ils garantiraient l’emploi des 8000 salariés de SFR jusqu’en 2029. Passée cette date, seuls environ 3000 d’entres eux conserveront leurs postes, dont une majorité chez Bouygues Telecom (2300 salariés), autour des 300 chez Orange et seulement 54 pour Free, qui récupère RED by SFR, la marque low cost de l’opérateur. Les délégués syndicaux affirment avoir déjà répertorié les boutiques qui devront fermer.
La grève intervient donc dans un contexte de négociation toujours en cours entre l’intersyndicale et les trois repreneurs. D’après Ouest France, une offre de reprise par salarié aurait été offerte, mais les syndicats souhaiteraient monter à trois offres par personne.
Une audience en référé doit avoir lieu ce matin au tribunal judiciaire de Paris juste avant la grève. Les syndicats tentent d’y obtenir davantage de documents sur la vente.
Après la publication de cet article, nous avons reçu un communiqué de la part des trois repreneurs que voici :
« Ce projet apporte une solution d’emploi à chacun des 8 000 salariés du périmètre repris : sur la base de notre proposition, environ 5 000 pourront rejoindre les trois opérateurs au lendemain de l’opération et 3 000 poursuivront leur activité chez SFR pour conduire la migration sur plusieurs années. Notre priorité est claire : préserver l’emploi dans le cadre d’un projet industriel crédible, responsable et qui s’inscrit dans la durée. Pour les salariés qui choisiraient un projet professionnel extérieur, nous proposons des mesures d’accompagnement significatives : pour un salarié au salaire médian de SFR, les indemnités proposées représentent près de trois années de salaire net. Les discussions se poursuivent avec les organisations syndicales et nous restons pleinement engagés dans le dialogue. »

articles.title: Meta VR Glasses : la folle promesse d'un Vision Pro en plus compact (on les a essayées)
articles.text:
Meta VR Glasses : la folle promesse d'un Vision Pro en plus compact (on les a essayées)
Après plus de dix ans de casques Quest, Meta a décidé de changer de formule. Lors de sa keynote Connect, Mark Zuckerberg a levé le voile sur des lunettes VR d'une centaine de grammes seulement, mais sans compromis sur les fonctions. Est-ce vraiment crédible ? Nous avons pu les manipuler suffisamment longtemps pour nous faire un premier avis.
Tous les ans, Meta met les petits plats dans les grands pour sa keynote annuelle Connect. Cette année pourrait toutefois rester dans les annales, car elle a vu Mark Zuckerberg lever le voile sur les Meta VR Glasses. Une nouvelle catégorie de produit qui promet dans un seul appareil un cinéma personnel, une place au bord du terrain, un espace de travail multi-écrans et une console de jeu.
Son argument massue tient toutefois au fait que le tout pèse une centaine de grammes seulement sur le nez, soit cinq fois moins que le Meta Quest 3. Fini donc les sangles et le poids sur le visage, la monture en alliage de magnésium se porte comme une (grosse) paire de lunettes. La comparaison avec la concurrence fait mal, puisque l'Apple Vision Pro pèse 650 grammes et le Galaxy XR de Samsung 488 grammes.
Un boîtier déporté pour alléger la monture
Pour parvenir à ses fins, Meta a tout de même un peu « triché ». Comme le Vision Pro, les Meta VR Glasses reposent sur une architecture en deux parties. Les lunettes ne conservent que les capteurs et l'affichage, tandis qu'un boîtier externe de 300 grammes, relié par un câble optique et doté d'un petit clip pour l'accrocher à une poche ou un sac, embarque la puce, la batterie et le stockage.
À l'intérieur, on trouve le nouveau Snapdragon Reality Elite de Qualcomm (XR2 Gen 3), épaulé par 12 Go de mémoire vive et 128 Go de stockage, extensibles jusqu'à 1 To par microSD. La batterie tient jusqu'à trois heures en lecture vidéo continue, avec une charge rapide 45 W en USB-C et, évidemment, la possibilité d'utiliser le dispositif quand il est branché et en recharge.
Contrairement à Apple qui n'a placé que la batterie en externe sur ses Vision Pro, le fait que la puce Reality Elite qui anime les Meta VR Glasses soit elle aussi dans le boîtier externe permet une légèreté absolument remarquable pour l'ensemble. Nous n'avons porté ces nouvelles lunettes qu'une vingtaine de minutes, mais nous sommes raisonnablement sûrs qu'il sera possible de les porter de longues heures sans aucun inconfort lié à leur ergonomie ou leur poids.
Un affichage qui se rapproche du Vision pro
Côté affichage, Meta dégaine un écran baptisé 5K Infinite Display sur panneaux micro-OLED, avec 2412x2288 pixels par œil, une densité de 37 pixels par degré et un rafraîchissement grimpant à 120 Hz. Les lentilles pancake intègrent même un suivi oculaire assuré par quatre caméras, deux par œil, et le champ de vision atteint 70° à l'horizontale pour 66° à la verticale.
Notez que les caméras de passthrough RGB affichent 26 pixels par degré avec autofocus et détection de profondeur, contre 18 pour le Quest 3, de quoi garder un œil net sur son environnement. Le déverrouillage passe par la reconnaissance de l'iris, et deux tailles de monture sont proposées, la différence se jouant sur la largeur.
Avec la fluidité du contrôle gestuel, les écrans sont sans doute ce qui nous a le plus bluffés lors de la découverte des Meta VR. Le rendu semble quasiment identique à celui du maître en la matière, le Vision Pro. Cette excellente première impression reste toutefois à confirmer lors du test en bonne et due forme.
Disney, IMAX et James Cameron au programme
Sur le terrain du contenu, Meta a sorti l'artillerie lourde. Les VR Glasses sont le premier appareil de réalité virtuelle certifié IMAX Enhanced, l'un des rares moyens de profiter en théorie à domicile du format d'image étendu exclusif d'IMAX. Dolby Vision et Dolby Atmos sont également de la partie, l'audio spatial étant intégré directement dans les branches.
Le partenariat avec Disney donne naissance au format VR Enhanced Cinema, dans lequel la pièce autour du spectateur réagit au film. Avengers: Infinity War et Star Wars: A New Hope seront disponibles dès le lancement dans l'application Disney Immersive Cinema by ILM, avec des environnements thématiques comme Tatooine, la tour des Avengers ou le Scare Floor. Nous avons pu essayer brièvement la version Avengers. C'est un petit plus intéressant, mais qui ne devrait pas changer la face du monde.
Meta s'associe aussi à James Cameron et Lightstorm Vision pour convertir des blockbusters en 3D pour la première fois en 2027. En attendant, le film de concert de Billie Eilish, Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour, co-réalisé avec Cameron, arrive en 3D dès novembre, et la série Open Season, qui suit le quadruple champion NBA Draymond Green en thérapie pendant sa saison, débarque le 29 septembre sur Horizon TV. L'idée est bonne, mais il va falloir enrichir le contenu pour que l'offre soit plus convaincante. Le sport en direct n'est pas oublié, avec du football universitaire diffusé par ESPN en VR180 8K et plus de 100 événements immersifs promis chaque année après le lancement. Espérons que Meta ne s'en tienne pas à des partenariats centrés sur les États-Unis.
Jouer avec les mains, travailler sur un mur d'écrans
Comme dit plus haut, ce qui nous a au moins autant bluffés que l'écran lors de cette rapide prise en main, c'est l'ergonomie générale. Rappelons que les lunettes tournent sous le même OS et le même store que les Quest, ce qui ouvre l'intégralité du catalogue existant, à condition d'y associer des contrôleurs Touch Plus, compatibles avec ceux des Quest 3 et 3S. Xbox Cloud Gaming avec Game Pass permet en prime de streamer des titres console sur écran virtuel géant.
La marque nous apprend par ailleurs que plus de 75 jeux jouables uniquement aux gestes des mains seront disponibles dès la sortie. Beat Saber reçoit pour l'occasion une grosse mise à jour, avec notamment un mode mains nues baptisé Flux.
Pour la productivité, Meta AI est intégré au système et se pilote à la voix, au regard ou aux gestes. Meta nous promet au passage une version plus intelligente de son IA, ainsi que son entrée dans la fameuse ère agentique. Nous jugerons sur pièce, même si ce que nous avons pu en voir est prometteur. Tout comme la fonction Surface Keyboard, qui transforme n'importe quelle surface plane en clavier et trackpad.
De son côté, le Virtual Display connecte un Mac ou un PC, sans fil ou en USB-C, avec un passthrough couleur qui laisse le bureau visible. Le câble USB-C fourni, un modèle USB 3.2 Gen 2 avec DP Alt Mode complet, autorise la connexion de la plupart des sources vidéo, consoles portables comprises. Enfin, pour la visio, la technologie Hologram promet de générer une version numérique photoréaliste de l'utilisateur, expressions et réactions en temps réel comprises, visible par ses interlocuteurs quel que soit leur appareil. Nous n'avons pas pu l'essayer.
Les Meta VR Glasses seront lancées au printemps 2027 dans 25 pays, dont la France. Meta n'a pas communiqué de prix en euros pour le moment, mais on sait déjà que les utilisateurs américains devront payer 1 299,99 dollars pour s'offrir l'appareil.

articles.title: Rayman Legends Retold's PC specs range from a GTX 1660 to an RTX 4080 – with upscaling throughout
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Do any developers release their games' PC system requirements without upscaling enabled these days? Based on the new Rayman Legends Retold reveal, it's become very rare. Once again, the game can run on a potato-like PC, and once again, the caveat is that upscaling is required at every level.
The good news for fans of the long-running platforming franchise is that the latest entry will play at 1080p@60FPS on an Intel Core i3-8100 or Ryzen 3 3100 paired with a GTX 1060, RX 5500 XT, or Intel Arc A580 and 8GB of RAM. However, graphics need to be set to the lowest preset and you still need upscaling (quality).
That quality upscaling setting is present in all four levels. Interestingly, the required hardware for the Recommended (1080p@60FPS with high graphics preset) and 2K (1440p@60FPS high preset) levels is pretty much identical. Only the AMD GPU (RX 5700 to an RX 6750 XT) and Intel GPU (Arc A750 to Arc B580) change.
Finally, the 4K ultra preset level is still quite demanding, considering this is a platformer (an admittedly pretty one) and upscaling is enabled. It asks for an RTX 4080 or Radeon RX 7900 XTX. The CPU requirements are more forgiving: a Core i5-9400 or Ryzen 5 3600.
The modest storage requirement is nice to see: 33GB of SSD space. That's around half of what's needed for The Blood of Dawnwalker, and almost 100GB less than Gears of War: E-Day.
Back in 2023, Remnant II set what was then considered a worrying precedent: it was the first PC game "designed with upscaling in mind."
While developers have avoided that kind of language since then, more games are adopting this thinking. Monster Hunter Wilds, Assassin's Creed Shadows, Rise of the Ronin, F1 25, DOOM: The Dark Ages, FBC: Firebreak, Mafia: The Old Country, Silent Hill f, Resident Evil Requiem, and Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced are just some that explicitly included upscaling in their published PC hardware requirements. Upcoming releases Gears of War: E-Day and Phantom Blade Zero have also included upscaling. Some titles, like The Blood of Dawnwalker, go out of their way to emphasize that upscaling is not part of the requirements.
Rayman Legends Retold is scheduled to release on PC and consoles on December 3, 2026. It had been set to launch on October 1, but Ubisoft delayed it to allow extra time for polish. It also allows the game to land after big releases like Gears of War, Call of Duty, and, of course, GTA 6.

articles.title: Alibaba apresenta o chip de IA mais poderoso da China • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Alibaba apresenta o chip de IA mais poderoso da China
Modelo terá 216 GB de memória e poderá operar com mais de mil chips em um único sistema; o lançamento está previsto para o início de 2027.
Resumo
- Alibaba apresenta o Zhenwu V900, um novo acelerador para treinamento e inferência de inteligência artificial.
- Empresa afirma que o chip oferece três vezes o desempenho do modelo anterior, o Zhenwu M890, mas não divulgou dados para uma comparação direta.
- Produção em massa e lançamento comercial estão previstos para o primeiro trimestre de 2027.
O Alibaba apresentou oficialmente o Zhenwu V900, seu novo chip desenvolvido para treinamento e inferência de modelos de inteligência artificial. Segundo a empresa, o acelerador oferece três vezes o desempenho do Zhenwu M890, da geração anterior, e conta com 216 GB de memória.
A novidade foi anunciada durante a conferência Apsara 2026, em Hangzhou, na China. O CEO do Alibaba, Eddie Wu, afirmou que o V900 é atualmente o “chip de IA mais poderoso da China”. A companhia, porém, não apresentou dados suficientes para verificar a alegação e comparar o desempenho com chips concorrentes.
Como é o Zhenwu V900?
O Zhenwu V900 foi desenvolvido para duas das principais cargas de trabalho de IA: treinamento de modelos e inferência, etapa em que um modelo já treinado realiza os cálculos necessários para gerar respostas. Além dos 216 GB de memória, o modelo oferece 1.200 GB/s de largura de banda na comunicação entre chips – o M890, por comparação, possui 144 GB de memória e comunicação entre chips de 800 GB/s.
A divisão de semicondutores T-Head afirma que mais de mil unidades podem trabalhar juntas como um único sistema. Em uma escala maior, o Alibaba afirma que o acelerador poderá integrar clusters com até 500 mil placas.
A produção em massa e o lançamento comercial estão previstos para o primeiro trimestre de 2027. Apesar da promessa de alto poder de fogo, ainda faltam informações importantes para avaliar o V900. O Alibaba também não divulgou o desempenho em FLOPS, o processo de fabricação, a empresa responsável pela produção do componente ou o seu consumo de energia. Por isso, a afirmação de que se trata do chip de IA mais poderoso da China permanece uma declaração do fabricante.
Modelo Qwen com até 10 trilhões de parâmetros
O novo acelerador também faz parte dos planos do Alibaba para treinar modelos de IA maiores. A empresa pretende desenvolver um futuro Qwen na escala de 5 a 10 trilhões de parâmetros. O Qwen3.8-Max, por comparação, possui 2,4 trilhões .
A expansão dos modelos acompanha os projetos da gigante chinesa para aumentar a sua infraestrutura de computação. O Alibaba pretende superar 20 gigawatts de capacidade de data centers até 2032. Wu afirmou que a escassez na cadeia global de suprimentos para data centers de IA está limitando a velocidade dessa expansão.

articles.title: OpenAI Agents Probed Websites for Vulnerabilities While Fetching Public Data
articles.text:
AI agents performing routine data-gathering tasks resorted to hacking techniques in at least three cases when conventional methods failed, according to new research linking some of the activity to agent swarms previously attributed to OpenAI.
The report, from researchers at Transluce, Corridor, MIT and AIUC, is built on public records from urlquery.net, a URL scanning service that loads submitted web pages in a remote browser.
The researchers found that AI agents used the service to get around access restrictions. On three occasions in May and June 2026, the agents also probed public data providers for security flaws, including an Australian government statistics agency.
The first incident took place on May 25-26. Agents trying to obtain a single photograph from the University of New Mexico’s digital library sent several probes, including tests for SQL injection, command injection and path traversal weaknesses, and hit the server with a burst of 80 requests.
Two days later, agents gathering University of Iowa data from Data USA, a platform offering open access to US government data, ran into errors caused by a malformed query. They responded with 12 probes, including SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), template injection, path traversal, and command injection.
The third incident targeted the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW) on June 20-21. The agents were looking for per-person government costs for a category of medicines across local areas in Victoria. Within minutes of Cloudflare blocking a dataset download, an agent sent a reflected XSS probe to the AIHW dashboard hosting the data, but Cloudflare’s firewall stopped that request as well.
With the main site’s download blocked, the agents pulled the file from an AIHW pre-production server instead, which delivered it in pieces over more than 100 scans. According to Transluce, the file was already public, but the agents circumvented the site’s anti-bot protections in obtaining it.
The researchers said none of the attempts appears to have succeeded and described the probing as limited in scale. They cautioned, however, that the records they examined are incomplete, and that successful attacks carried out through private scans or other channels cannot be ruled out.
Based on matching targets, tactics, and timing, Transluce linked the AIHW and Data USA activity to an agent swarm that OpenAI had previously confirmed as its own. The link for the University of New Mexico case rests only on timing and shared relay services.
“This data reveals that malicious cyber activity is not limited to agents tasked with cybersecurity-related tasks and can arise instrumentally to solve mundane tasks like information retrieval,” the researchers wrote.
Transluce also found agent activity on urlquery.net dating back to at least March 6, roughly two months before previously reported agent incidents, with weaker signs of activity as early as November 2025.
Australia discloses OpenAI agent intrusion
Coinciding with Transluce’s report, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that OpenAI agents had infiltrated several government websites. Transluce said the announcement likely overlaps with the AIHW incident it documented.
According to AAP, an OpenAI research team instructed an internal model on June 18 to research public spending on medicines. The agent attempted to pull data from four government sites: the Medicare Statistics Reporting Portal, the AIHW, the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, and the Victorian Department of Health.
After being blocked repeatedly on the Medicare portal, it found a way around the restrictions and accessed both public and non-public files. Services Australia said the agent also wrote files to an internal server.
While the government has not disclosed how the agent bypassed the portal’s protections, the details released so far suggest it circumvented security controls rather than simply collecting exposed data.
OpenAI said it does not believe any personal details of Medicare customers were accessed, and that the exposed data consisted of aggregate health statistics and file names. Defence Minister Richard Marles said the information was neither sensitive nor related to national security.
OpenAI discovered the breach in August while reviewing incidents in which its agents had gone rogue. The company notified the government on September 10 by emailing a mid-level public inbox at Services Australia, which confirmed the notification was legitimate and reported it to the Australian Signals Directorate’s Cyber Security Centre on September 15.
Albanese spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in New York on Wednesday to express disappointment over the delay and the manner of the notification.

articles.title: Building a Collaborative Platform Culture in a Bank
articles.text:
A platform is a collaboration system, not infrastructure. Culture follows structure: platform teams can build open support sessions, create super user awards for contributing developers, and establish shared open standards to grow an engineering mindset, Marcy Paramonova and Stéphane Cusin explained in their talk Building Cloud Native Culture in a Bank at KubeCon & CloudNativeCon Europe.
Developers and product teams depend on a platform team, Paramonova said. The platform team depends on application teams, and both need to go forward; for that, they need shared standards.
A platform is not a piece of infrastructure; it’s a collaboration system through which lots of communication goes, Paramonova and Cusin explained in How Open Source Enables Collaboration in Creating a Platform.
Cloud native is a cultural shift, not just a technical one; their transformation journey also required a cultural shift, Paramonova argued. The platform team started offering open support sessions where developers could come, and they could solve their problems with them:
We wanted to step back from the usual support for driver tickets and offer something new and fresh to our users. Many people got interested, including infrastructure, cybersecurity, network, identity, and cloud teams. We sit together, share solutions, and help to solve problems collaboratively.
If every action required a ticket, manual intervention, or direct support from a platform engineer, we would unintentionally create a culture of dependency, Cousin said. Teams would wait for the platform team instead of learning and operating independently.
Paramonova mentioned that they created events to recognize adoption of their platform. They introduced super user awards for developers who actively contributed to improving the platform:
Their feedback, sometimes hard to hear for us and a little bit painful, actually helped us to create something more beautiful and better. So we’re grateful for that.
The activities they organized changed how they perceive and value human skills.
When you use open source with open standards, your skills become very transferable, Paramonova said. You don’t relearn something from zero; you build on a shared foundation that’s shared across the open technologies, she added.
An engineering mindset is the most important thing, Paramonova argued. It’s not what you know today, but your capacity and ability to take new technologies, to learn them, to execute and to operate them:
Being an engineer is about problem solving, being passionate about that, and sharing your passion about problem solving.
Culture follows structure. You cannot wait for culture to emerge on its own; you have to design systems that create the culture you want, Cousin explained:
If your team complains about being interrupted all the time, don’t blame the other team. Ask yourself: have you defined a structure for people to reach out to you?
Kubernetes transformed more than our platform. It transformed how our organization builds software, Cousin concluded.
InfoQ interviewed Marcy Paramonova and Stéphane Cusin after their talk.
InfoQ: How did your engineering culture shift over time?
Stéphane Cusin: One principle we established from day one was that platform capabilities should never depend on manual intervention. Instead of opening a ticket and waiting for an engineer to make a change, teams interact with the platform through declarative configuration and automated workflows. For example, enabling a capability can be done through a simple configuration change in Git, which is automatically applied by our GitOps process. This creates a self-service experience while providing full traceability and visibility into platform adoption.
This approach changed how we operate the platform. We can now understand which capabilities are being adopted, which ones are no longer needed, and which users are affected by a change. It has already allowed us to safely retire unused features and migrate teams toward newer platform capabilities with confidence.
InfoQ: How did you design systems that create the culture that you wanted to establish?
Marcy Paramonova: You cannot mandate a culture into existence, but you can design structures that make certain behaviors natural. For us, that meant building rituals around collaboration rather than just talking about it.
We run a "Genius Bar" twice a week, two hours each session. If you have a question about the platform, if something is not working the way you expected, if you just want to understand how a component fits together, you come there. No ticket, no waiting for someone’s calendar to open up. It keeps feedback loops short, and it keeps us honest, because you hear very quickly when something is confusing or painful.
We also run user insights sessions where we share priorities, work done, and visibility gained, and we prioritize together with users rather than for them. And we do demos, showing what is shipped, what is on the roadmap, and how to actually use the platform day today.
Internally, the platform team has its own planning sessions to stay aligned and to make space for deliberate decisions, rather than just reactive work.
None of this is revolutionary. But when you stack these rhythms together, the culture you want starts to emerge from the structure you build. It is not magic, but it is also not accidental.
Cusin: We tried to make platform decisions visible. Platform capabilities are delivered through versioned artifacts, reusable deployment patterns, and documented interfaces rather than individual agreements between teams. This creates consistency and shared understanding across the organization.
Another important design principle was that every platform feature should have a lifecycle. We wanted to know who was using a capability, how it was being used, and whether it was still providing value. That visibility allows us to evolve the platform intentionally instead of accumulating complexity over time.
In many ways, our platform became a mechanism for reinforcing the behaviors we wanted to encourage: self-service over ticket-driven operations, standardization over customization, transparency over tribal knowledge, and shared ownership over dependency on a few experts.
When those principles are embedded into the platform itself, the desired culture becomes the easiest way for people to work.

articles.title: Italy's Clastix raises €2.9 million with Mistral backing to build sovereign Kubernetes infrastructure for Europe | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Clastix, a Naples-based infrastructure software company helping enterprises run Kubernetes more efficiently at scale, has raised €2.9 million in a Seed round. This marks the company’s first external funding round.
The round was led by CDP Venture Capital Sgr, with participation from Mistral and Vertis SGR, through its Vertis Venture 6 Digital Sud fund, which is partially financed by the European Union’s Next-Generation EU programme.
“We are proud to support a team that combines engineering excellence, market vision, and global ambition. This investment reflects CDP Venture Capital’s commitment to backing strategic technologies developed in Italy that can strengthen Europe’s technological sovereignty and long-term competitiveness,” said Alessandro Scortecci, Chief Investment Officer for Direct Investments at CDP Venture Capital.
Founded in 2020 by Adriano Pezzuto and Dario Tranchitella, engineers who previously managed Kubernetes deployments within large enterprises, Clastix builds infrastructure software to reduce the operational overhead of running Kubernetes at scale.
Its journey began with Capsule, an open-source project that brought native multi-tenancy to Kubernetes, before the team built Kamaji, which lets tenant control planes run as pods on shared infrastructure rather than on dedicated machines, a move Clastix calls eliminating the “control plane tax”.
Since then, the company has combined the two technologies into a single enterprise offering called kMetal, the company’s commercial platform for fleet-scale Kubernetes operations. It is already running in production with infrastructure teams across AI labs, telecommunications, cloud services, and the public sector, including customers such as Fastweb, NVIDIA and Mistral.
“The next phase of AI won’t be decided by models alone but by who controls the infrastructure layer beneath them. This funding goes toward building that layer for what’s coming: expanding our R&D to better support AI-scale workloads, and growing our team to bring it into new markets as they build their AI infrastructure,” said Adriano Pezzuto, co-founder and CEO of Clastix.
With the fresh capital, Clastix is positioning itself as a European alternative to hyperscaler-dependent infrastructure, aiming to give enterprises and AI-focused organisations hyperscaler-grade Kubernetes operations while retaining control over their own hardware and data.
Timothée Lacroix, co-founder and CTO of Mistral, said, “Clastix is the backbone of our Kubernetes infrastructure – their work on multi-tenancy and managed control planes helps us to enable our training and inference clusters at scale, with the efficiency that frontier AI demands.
“By backing Clastix, we’re investing in Europe’s AI stack. A sovereign AI ecosystem isn’t just about models – it’s about the infrastructure layer that makes them run.”
The capital will go toward product development, customer success, solutions engineering, and go-to-market expansion as Clastix scales kMetal. Over the next three years, the company plans to grow its headcount to meet rising customer demand and build out the capabilities needed to serve larger enterprise teams. It also plans to continue investing in Kamaji, its open-source Hosted Control Plane engine, which will remain free and unchanged under the Apache 2.0 licence.

articles.title: Obscura VPN finally arrives on Linux — with a GUI, a CLI, and a new open-source license
articles.text:
Obscura VPN finally arrives on Linux — with a GUI, a CLI, and a new open-source license
The privacy-first VPN now covers every major desktop and mobile platform, and it's now fully open source, too
- Obscura VPN has released a native Linux app, with both GUI and CLI
- Official packages cover Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, and other derivatives
- The provider has also switched to an open-source GPLv3 license
Obscura VPN has finally arrived on Linux. The privacy-focused provider has launched a native desktop app for the platform, meaning Linux users no longer need to set up the service manually.
This rounds off a busy year for the newcomer, which only recently landed on Windows. With this release, Obscura now supports macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, and Linux.
For privacy-minded Linux fans hunting for the best VPN for their setup, Obscura's unusual two-party design makes it one of the more interesting options.
The company is also relicensing its code under GPLv3, which will appeal to open-source purists.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
What's new in Obscura's Linux app
Obscura's Linux app ships with a full graphical interface, alongside an experimental command-line interface for users who prefer the terminal. Until now, Linux users had to rely on a manual WireGuard setup guide to connect. The native app means no more juggling configuration files, making the service far more accessible.
Obscura offers official packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora (including Atomic Desktops like Silverblue), and Arch, as well as derivatives like Linux Mint, RHEL, Silverblue, CachyOS, and Omarchy. Minimum requirements include Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 44, and RHEL 10, and the app is installed through Obscura's own package repository.
The Linux client also supports Obscura's QUIC-based stealth protocol, which makes VPN traffic look like ordinary HTTP/3 web browsing. This can help you get past networks that block VPNs.
To mark the launch, Obscura is offering 25% off for a limited time with the promo code LINUX26. The service normally costs around $8 per month, with no free tier.
Obscura goes GPLv3
Alongside the launch, Obscura has moved from the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 to the GNU General Public License v3.0, which it says furthers its commitment to open-source software.
Obscura's code has been public since day one, but GPLv3 is a true open-source license, giving the community more freedom to inspect, modify, and share it. It's the same license Mullvad uses for its own apps.
What is Obscura VPN?
Obscura was founded by Carl Dong, a former Bitcoin Core contributor, and first launched on macOS in February 2025. It promised to set the standard for next-gen VPNs, and has since expanded to iOS, then Android, Windows, and now Linux.
Its big selling point is a two-party relay. Obscura acts as the entry node and sees your real IP address, while Mullvad VPN handles the exit node and sees the websites you visit. This means no single provider knows both who you are and what you browse.
That design has already been tested. Security firm Cure53 audited Obscura and found no major security vulnerabilities, as we reported last December.

articles.title: New wireless Wi-Fi 7 external GPU enclosure comes with a built-in 4TB SSD for local AI — $1,999 box leverages WiFi 7 to present a remote card as local
articles.text:
New wireless Wi-Fi 7 external GPU enclosure comes with a built-in 4TB SSD for local AI — $1,999 box leverages WiFi 7 to present a remote card as local
There's onboard storage for keeping model weights, too.
External GPUs (eGPU) have been tried time and again, and while they have found their niche among laptop users, they're not commonplace. Now that the AI craze is in full swing, more people are looking into owning a graphics card of some sort for the single purpose of running LLMs locally. The WiCi One is designed with that specific scenario in mind, but adds wireless connectivity, multi-device support, and onboard storage.
That list of words usually doesn't belong in the same sentence as GPUs, so it merits close inspection. First and foremost, the WiCi One leverages the WiFi 7 protocol to transmit data to and from the card. The firm says that client machines keep a GPU driver that makes the operating system think it's a graphics card just like any other, while in reality they'll be talking to the WiCi One over the network.
However, as WiCi explains in great detail, just blindly doing that would make for a terrible eGPU, as the standard communication between host and card is extremely chatty. That's not a problem with the sub-microsecond latency of PCIe 5.0, but would quickly turn even basic status querying operations into multi-second affairs. Large computations with lots of data shuffled back and forth could hypothetically take hours.
The company claims its driver software performs a great deal of data caching, deduplication, and compression, and is also very judicious about what type of hardware requests can be handled locally versus those that really do need to go over the airwaves.
This mode of operation and its corresponding separation of concerns bring several advantages: theoretically, the one GPU could be used on multiple machines. There are Python libraries for passing the WiCi One as any other GPU to LLMs, and also a standard HTTP API for network access, once again lending credence to the fact that multiple clients could use the WiCi One without any special configuration.
Running LLMs means shuffling a substantial amount of data back-and-forth, and contemporary models with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture can run locally using an SSD as a fallback. WiCi took a clever approach and incorporated a 4 TB PCIe 5.0 SSD directly into the enclosure, in a bid to store model weights to both enable larger models and indirectly save on cross-network transfers.
WiCi also mentions that the card can also run games without modification, but doesn't elaborate on what kind of performance is expected. The documentation only ever mentions Vulkan and Direct3D, and hedges the fact that "[not] every API must be complete on day one." WiFi makes for a poor technology to underpin a real-time endeavor like pushing millions of polygons and textures in, and the resulting images out, in just 16.67ms for 60 FPS, so we'll venture that gamers will be best served with conventional eGPUs.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The base spec comes with an RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB graphics card, and is slated for a 2026 Q4 preview, with no release date set in stone. WiCi plans to offer a variant with an RTX 5090 and its 32 GB of VRAM, albeit there's no word on when that will arrive, much less at which price — especially considering those cards alone are currently going for well over 7 grand, and have been spotted selling for far more.
The asking price for all this is $1,999 for early signups, and $2,599 otherwise, for the base spec. Those figures might sound steep, but they're actually fairly reasonable if the WiCi packaging and software stack deliver. A quick skim of Newegg puts an RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB graphics card at $800 or more, while an NVMe 4 TB PCIe 5.0 SSD is a little pricier at $850. Once you factor in a hypothetical $100 for a power supply and another $100 for the case, Wi-Fi card, and assorted bits and bobs, you're at $1,850 already.

articles.title: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone
articles.text:
Meta has a new plan to get people to make games for its Horizon social platform. The company today announced two new development tools that will let you create games with AI prompts: Horizon Create, a mobile app, and Horizon Studio, a browser app that offers more granular controls. The apps will be available in early access, and interested users can sign up for a waitlist.
Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone
The next push for Meta’s Horizon platform involves AI-generated video games.
Horizon has struggled as a platform, but Meta has a plan to give these new Horizon games significantly more reach: It’s going to let published games made with Horizon Create and Horizon Studio get recommended on Facebook and Instagram, where they also will be playable.
“Someone scrolling through Instagram can tap a clip of your game and be in a multiplayer session within seconds, without needing to download an app or being redirected,” Meta says. “Your game lives natively in the feeds where people already discover content and connect with friends.” Games that are “engaging, stable, culturally relevant, and keep players coming back” will get more reach, according to the company.
The company’s announcement comes as Roblox, a similar platform to Horizon that is vastly more popular, is also making a significant push into AI-powered development, including a feature in its mobile app that similarly allows users to generate games with a prompt.
Meta’s news about Horizon, which launched as a VR app, follows a recent pivot to primarily focus on mobile. With Meta stuffing AI into basically everything it can, it’s perhaps no surprise that AI is becoming a big part of Horizon as well.
Giving people the tools to quickly make those could give people more options for things to play. I’m pretty skeptical that a bunch of AI-generated games will be as engaging as a handcrafted experience, but the games made in Create and Studio sound as if they’ll at least have the elements of video games (unlike Google’s Project Genie, which can create brief but empty AI-generated interactive experiences). “Both enable creators to turn any idea into a complete 2D or 3D mobile game, complete with progression systems, balanced difficulty, art direction, multiplayer, and more, then refine every element to their standards,” Meta says in a blog post.
Meta also likely has a very long way to go to reach the scale of Roblox, which has 123 million daily active users. Horizon, by contrast, hasn’t ever really taken off; The Verge reported in early 2022 that it hit 300,000 monthly users.

articles.title: OpenAI makes you call sales for a custom voice. Google just made it self-serve.
articles.text:
OpenAI makes you call sales for a custom voice. Google just made it self-serve.
Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS today through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Text-to-speech APIs have historically left developers working with whatever voices were already available, but Gemini 3.8 changes that by letting users create the voice itself.
Now, developers can describe the voice they have in mind or start with a short recording of an existing voice, then save what they create and use it again across an application. Google handles the voice profile from there, so the original recording or description doesn’t have to accompany every new request.
Turning recordings into voice IDs
Replication runs through a new Voices endpoint (POST /v1beta/voices) and two recordings are required from the same speaker; those need to be clean samples between 10 and 30 seconds and a separate consent recording. For that second clip, the speaker reads a statement, confirming that the voice belongs to them and that they agree to let Google create a synthetic version of it. Google confirms that the person giving consent and the reference clip are the same person before proceeding.
Once approved, Google returns a voice_… ID and keeps it in the developer’s project for a year, alongside any voices created with Gemini’s voice-design tools. A project can hold up to 200 voices in total, and developers can retrieve, list, or delete them through the API just as they would other stored resources.
Voice replication can also be used without storing the profile in the project. Setting store=False returns an encrypted voicekey_… instead, which stays with the application and is supplied again when the voice is needed. Because the key expires after seven days, this option makes sense for short-lived jobs.
A few more things are worth noting before building around the feature are the fact that Google marks audio generated by Gemini with SynthID, and replicated voices also carry C2PA content credentials that can be used to trace where the audio came from. Google doesn’t offer voice replication through AI Studio in Illinois, Texas, the European Economic Area, the U.K., Switzerland or India.
A project can hold up to 200 voices in total, and developers can retrieve, list, or delete them through the API just as they would other stored resources.
Prompting a voice from scratch
Voice design generates a persona from a natural-language description of role, accent, and character, and Google says it works across more than 100 languages and dialects. The docs list 130 supported languages for Flash TTS and 101 for Flash-Lite. Google’s announcement also claims a library of more than 2,000 production-ready voices.
The developer docs describe 30 prebuilt studio voices plus hundreds more in an extended library that can be filtered by language, accent, pitch, and use case through GET /v1beta/voices. A remixing feature for adjusting the timbre, pitch, pace, and accent of library voices with prompts is something Google lists as coming soon.
The company recommends creating a voice once and reusing its ID rather than describing the same persona in every request. According to the docs, repeatedly sending long persona descriptions is the most common cause of voice drift. Once the voice is created, subsequent requests need only a short style instruction, if any.
Gemini 3.8 sees input text strictly as a verbatim transcript, a breaking change for anyone who embedded stage directions in prompts to the 3.1 preview model. Sustained direction for a turn, such as whispering, sarcasm, or speaking rapidly, now goes in a speech_metadata annotation, while momentary sounds like <sigh>, <cough>, and <short pause> sit inline in angle brackets. In two-speaker scripts, listener reactions wrapped in pipes, such as |mhm|, produce backchannels and overlapping speech without breaking the script into extra turns.
Gemini 3.8 sees input text strictly as a verbatim transcript, a breaking change for anyone who embedded stage directions in prompts to the 3.1 preview model.
Two-speaker scripts have limits
Native two-speaker generation has one limitation that’s important to mention. A single request supports up to two speakers using prebuilt voices, while dialogue between designed or replicated voices has to be generated turn by turn and stitched together from the 24 kHz PCM output.
Unary requests return WAV by default, streaming requests return raw 16-bit PCM, and mu-law and A-law encodings are available for telephony pipelines. Google says Flash TTS maintains voice quality and timbre across hours of continuous audio, targeting audiobook and podcast production.
Flash for performance, Flash-Lite for volume
Both models share an API schema, so switching between them is a one-parameter change, and both support voice design and replication.
The company positions Flash TTS for demanding acting work, including complex dialogue, heavy use of vocal tags, difficult pronunciations, regional dialects, and long narration. Flash-Lite TTS is the faster, less expensive option and the direct replacement for gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview, tuned for bulk production, read-aloud features, and cascaded voice agents that pair a text model with a separate speech step.
For those agents, Google recommends one TTS call per turn as the LLM’s text arrives, with the stored voice carrying identity across the conversation.
Plugging into voice agent frameworks
A speech model is only one layer of a production voice application, and a real-time agent still needs transport, speech recognition, turn detection, interruption handling, and session state. Google points developers toward frameworks that already handle those layers, naming Agora, LiveKit, Pipecat and Vercel’s AI Gateway as platforms that support Gemini speech generation through the Gemini API.
That lets a team drop Gemini in as the speech layer without rebuilding its audio pipeline, although anyone planning to rely on a replicated voice should confirm their framework passes custom voice_… IDs through before committing. API access through Gemini Enterprise is listed as coming soon.
How OpenAI’s approach compares
OpenAI also offers custom voices, but access is tighter. Customers have to go through sales, are limited to 20 voices per organization and must provide a consent recording alongside a voice sample of up to 30 seconds. The resulting voice ID works across its speech endpoint, Realtime API, and Chat Completions.
What OpenAI doesn’t have is Google’s prompt-based voice design, which can create a voice from a written description. Its 13 built-in voices can be steered for tone or speed, and apps must disclose that the speech is AI-generated.
In comparison, Google’s advantage is that it’s giving developers more ways to create the voice they want before the first line of text ever reaches it.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5124010 update released with 46 changes and fixes
articles.text:
Microsoft released the KB5124010 September 2026 non-security preview update for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2, with 46 changes including Bluetooth improvements and the ability to remap the Copilot key.
KB5124010 is a preview update that lets administrators and users test Windows improvements, bug fixes, and new features before they become generally available during next month's Patch Tuesday release.
However, unlike regular cumulative updates, monthly optional updates like KB5124010 provide only quality improvements and don't include security fixes.
The September 2026 preview update adds support for Emoji 17.0, a new "Open apps maximized" accessibility setting that automatically maximizes app windows as they open, and a recovery remote management plug-in for extending Windows Recovery (WinRE) management capabilities.
Microsoft also resolved an issue where the Bluetooth radio could be turned off while the Bluetooth radio control toggle in Settings still showed as on, and a bug that could cause crashes with error code 0x139 while streaming Bluetooth audio.
It also improved microphone compatibility with certain Bluetooth Classic audio accessories, as well as reliability and performance with LE Audio accessories.
After deploying this preview update, users can also remap the Copilot key on their Windows devices via a new Windows 11 setting to function as the Right Ctrl or Context Menu key.
You can install the KB5124010 update by opening Settings, clicking on Windows Update, and then "Check for Updates."
Because this is an optional update, you will need to click the "Download and install" link unless you already have the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" option enabled, which will prompt the OS to install it automatically.
You can also manually download and install the KB5124010 preview update from the Microsoft Update Catalog.
Windows 11 KB5124010 highlights
Once installed, this optional non-security update will upgrade Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2 devices to builds 26200.9550 and 26100.9550, respectively.
The September 2026 preview update comes with many other changes, some of the more important ones highlighted below:
- This update adds support for using slideshow wallpapers with multiple desktops, so that it won't automatically switch you back to Picture.
- New! Additional gesture controls for precision touchpads are available in Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Touchpad.
- New! This update introduces Camera roll backup in Settings, helping eligible users protect their photos with OneDrive. You can turn on the feature from the Settings Home or Accounts page and complete setup on a mobile phone using a QR code.
In this update, Microsoft also fixed a known issue that was causing the built-in File History backup feature on some Windows systems to fail after installing the September 2026 security updates.
KB5124010 also removes PC-to-PC Migration, a tool that helped users transfer their files, settings, and preferences to a new Windows device. Microsoft now recommends using Windows Backup to migrate to a new PC using OneDrive.
Microsoft also reminded users that KB5124010 is the final preview update for Windows 11 24H2, which reaches end of support in October 2026.

articles.title: Why Mobile RPG Players Are Moving Beyond Smartphones - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Your phone got you into Cookie Run Kingdom, Epic Seven, and Blue Archive. It is also the reason those same games now feel cramped.
If daily commissions leave your device burning, your thumbs aching, and your storage begging for mercy, you are not “playing wrong.” You have simply outgrown the hardware the genre now demands.
Modern mobile RPGs are no longer five-minute time-killers. They are open-world gacha games with console-scale maps, long story patches, and live-ops calendars that punish missed stamina. That is why mobile RPG players are moving beyond smartphones and why so many of them now play mobile games on PC through an Android emulator.
Even a flagship phone struggles during long RPG sessions. Two-hour boss farms and exploration quickly expose its limits.
What actually breaks the phone experience is:
- Thermal throttling: Open-world RPGs keep the SoC loaded. Heat climbs, frames drop, and combat starts to hitch.
- Battery anxiety: High graphics plus 60 FPS can drain a pack in a single session.
- Tiny UI: Mini-maps, relic stats, and team menus were designed for thumbs, not for reading every modifier at a glance.
- Storage pressure. Titles like Genshin Impact already eat tens of gigabytes, and every patch asks for more.
- Touch fatigue: Precise camera control, timed parries, and menu-heavy gacha management do not love a glass slab.
What RPG Players Actually Came For
Mobile RPG players over-index on mastery, progression, and community, not just “something to tap on the train.” They want characters to grow, builds to matter, and time spent to show up on screen.
That motivation collides with phone limits. You cannot study a skill tree, manage two accounts, and farm a domain comfortably on a 6.5-inch panel while the chassis cooks your hand. The genre got bigger. The device did not.
Phone vs. PC: What the Shift Happens
| Pain on smartphone | What changes on PC | 
| Heat and frame drops | Desktop cooling and stable high FPS | 
| Small screen, fat fingers | Monitor, mouse, and keyboard mapping | 
| One account at a time | Multi-instance rerolls and alts | 
| Battery + storage panic | Plugged-in sessions and hard-drive space | 
| Same servers, same UID | Progress stays on your existing account | 
As you can see, the game does not change. The box it runs in does. An Android emulator copies the Android environment onto Windows, so you keep the same Play Store title, the same account, and the same world chat, only now the PC does the heavy lifting.
Why LDPlayer Fits Heavy RPG Play
Players who spend hours in games like Arknights or Chaos Zero Nightmare need stable FPS, multi-instance support, and tools that reduce repetitive tasks.That is why many RPG players choose LDPlayer for PC gameplay.
What RPG mains actually use are:
- High, stable FPS on mid-range PCs for smoother exploration and combat.
- Android 14 compatibility for newer game updates.
- Unlimited multi-instance sync for rerolls and alternate accounts.
- Operation Recorder and macros for daily commissions and auto-battles.
- Key mapping and controller support for more comfortable controls.
- No battery clock. Plug in and play through the story instead of watching the percentage fall.
You still take the phone on the commute. Home sessions which are the ones that decide whether you clear endgame or rage-quit a 20-minute load belong on a monitor.
How to Move Without Losing Progress
- Download and install LDPlayer on an SSD.
- Sign into the same Google account you use on Android.
- Install the game from Play Store or LD Store.
- Log into your existing UID. Cross-progression does the rest.
- Bind keys, cap FPS for stability, then clone instances only if your RAM can hold them.
Start with one window. Add multi-instance after the main account feels locked in. Bind guest data immediately so a wipe does not eat a lucky pull.
Conclusion
So, why does this happen? Why are RPG players moving on beyond smartphones? They are not abandoning mobile RPGs. They are refusing to let a pocket computer limit a genre that now asks for hours, not minutes. Bigger screen, cooler hardware, better controls, and smarter grinding are not “PC elitism.” They are the same mastery instinct that made you pull for a limited character in the first place.
Keep the smartphone for dailies on the bus. When the next patch drops a new region, open it on LDPlayer, and play the game the way it was always trying to be played.
Summary: Why mobile RPG players are moving beyond smartphones, and how the best Android emulator unlocks bigger screens, stable FPS, and smarter PC grinding.

articles.title: « La radio n’est pas une option » : pour éviter sa disparition des voitures, les radios françaises montent au créneau
articles.text:
La radio ne doit pas devenir une simple option payante ou dépendre d’un abonnement à une plateforme de streaming. C’est le message porté conjointement par Radio France, l’Alliance de la radio et les radios associatives dans un communiqué publié le 21 septembre 2026. Alors que Médiamétrie rappelle qu’un tiers de l’écoute se fait en voiture, plusieurs constructeurs automobiles, venus notamment d’Asie ou des États-Unis, suppriment purement et simplement les tuners hertziens des tableaux de bord. Pour écouter un programme, les conducteurs se retrouvent contraints de passer par la radio streaming sur mobile.
Des enjeux de sécurité civile
Derrière cette bataille de constructeurs se pose aussi la question de la gestion des crises et notamment la résilience des réseaux. Les récentes intempéries et les feux estivaux en Gironde ont lourdement endommagé les infrastructures de télécommunication, détruisant notamment des dizaines de kilomètres de câbles de fibre optique et des centaines de poteaux. En situation d’urgence, les réseaux mobiles s’effondrent rapidement lorsque les batteries relais s’épuisent. L’Espagne a connu la même vulnérabilité lors d’une panne géante d’électricité en avril 2025, où les téléphones étaient déconnectés tandis que les autoradios continuaient de diffuser les informations.
Une voiture qui n’a pas de récepteur hertzien représente donc un angle mort pour la sécurité civile. Contrairement à internet ou au streaming, la diffusion FM et DAB+ (ou Radio Numérique Terrestre) reste entièrement gratuite, anonyme et accessible en toutes circonstances, jouant le même rôle d’alerte indispensable qu’un bon vieux poste à piles. C’est ce qu’a rappelé le Secrétariat général de la Défense et de la Sécurité nationale lors des dernières Assises de la Radio de l’Arcom.
Empêcher un contournement de la loi
Les acteurs de la radio appellent le gouvernement à légiférer pour empêcher le contournement de la loi de 2020 qui rendait déjà le DAB+ obligatoire dans les véhicules neufs dès lors qu’un système radio était présent. La parade actuelle des fabricants consiste à supprimer l’équipement radio de base pour échapper à cette règle. Service public et radios privées font désormais front commun pour que la législation évolue.
Au niveau européen, la négociation en cours du Digital Networks Act doit trancher sur l’obligation d’intégrer des récepteurs FM et DAB+ dans tous les véhicules neufs, utilitaires compris, avec une place importante sur la console multimédia. Au niveau français, le secteur attend un avis favorable du gouvernement lors de l’examen de l’article 2 de la proposition de loi portée par le sénateur Laurent Lafon, qui entend verrouiller cette obligation d’équipement dans l’hexagone.

articles.title: The Download: a bid to scrap the virtual wall and AI hits Climate Week
articles.text:
The Download: a bid to scrap the virtual wall and AI hits Climate Week
Plus: an OpenAI agent has executed the first known AI hack of a government site.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
A congressional representative just proposed killing America’s border tower program
Delia Ramirez, a Democratic US representative from Illinois, has announced plans to introduce legislation to terminate the surveillance tower program along the country’s southern border.
The announcement comes just days after publication of an MIT Technology Review investigation, “Dying on Camera,” which looked at deaths near these towers. Nearly one in four deaths we analyzed between 2015 and early 2026 occurred within their advertised range.
Ramirez, who sits on the Homeland Security Committee, cited our reporting that nearly “1,100 people have died within range of a billion-dollar surveillance tower system between 2015 and 2026,” adding, “The towers that we have paid a billion dollars to just don’t work.”
Here’s what she’s proposing and what it could mean for the border surveillance program.
—Eileen Guo
Read all of MIT Technology Review’s groundbreaking “virtual wall” investigation here.
Roundtables: the deadly failures of the virtual border wall
The US spent billions building the “virtual wall” of surveillance towers along its southern border, promising they will help detect and apprehend border crossers and save lives. But MIT Technology Review has documented more than a thousand people who moved through areas watched by these towers without being caught—and ultimately died there.
Next Monday, join our editor-in-chief Mat Honan, senior AI reporter James O’Donnell, and senior reporter for features and investigations Eileen Guo for a subscriber-only conversation about the investigation. They’ll examine the failures of border surveillance technology and uncover the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.
Register now to attend on Monday, September 28 at 19:00 BST / 2:00pm EDT / 11:00am PDT.
Want to join the conversation? Subscribe to MIT Technology Review for exclusive access to all our Roundtables.
AI is dominating the conversation at Climate Week
—Casey Crownhart
AI is the unavoidable topic at this year’s New York Climate Week, with tension growing over its costs and benefits.
The technology is attracting more attention and money to energy technologies, some of which are low- or zero-emission. But the data center buildout has come with a hefty environmental toll, and a whole lot of natural gas is coming online to meet the demand.
Overall, what I’m hearing this week is that many in the climate sector are skeptical of AI, at best. Find out why.
This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 An OpenAI agent has executed the first known AI hack of a government site
It breached an Australian government health data portal in June. (CNN)
+ OpenAI notified Australia three months later through a public mailbox. (BBC)
+ No patient records are believed to have been accessed. (Guardian)
+ Its agents also tried to breach three other sites. (NYT $)
+ Here's why AI agents cheat to reach their goals. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Data stolen in the FBI hack exposes agents’ sensitive intelligence roles
It identifies staff working on China, Russia, and cyber. (Reuters $)
+ And may have exposed the FBI’s own hacking unit. (404 Media)
+ The group behind the incident claims it isn’t financially motivated. (Register)
3 The US rejected calls from OpenAI and Anthropic for global AI standards
A Trump advisor said global rules threatened the country’s AI lead. (BBC)
+ America’s AI leaders had urged the UN to coordinate on safety. (Gizmodo)
+ The AI industry has taken a doomer turn. (MIT Technology Review)
4 Meta has unveiled new AI glasses—and a pendant for Muse
Camera-free smart glasses address growing privacy concerns. (Verge)
+ While the Muse Charm enables hands-free interaction with the AI agent. (BBC)
+ Mark Zuckerberg wants Muse to be a "personal superintelligence.” (Axios)
+ Meta also showed off new VR glasses. (CNBC)
5 China is accelerating its AI push ahead of the Xi-Trump summit
Huawei and Alibaba have both unveiled new flagship chips. (CNBC)
+ The country’s AI industry has shrugged off America’s safety panic. (Atlantic $)
+ The US leads in AI models, but China has talent and political edges. (NYT $)
+ Chinese models have divided the White House. (MIT Technology Review)
6 US lawmakers have proposed new rules for blocking Chinese tech
The bipartisan bill would require broader review of national security risks. (Hill)
+ And give Congress the power to overturn FCC bans. (Reuters $)
7 Tech giants have urged Trump to withdraw $103,265 H-1B fee
They say the charge could weaken US competitiveness. (WSJ $)
8 Scientists have detected radio signals from an exoplanet for the first time
The signals likely come from intense magnetic activity on the planet. (Wired $)
9 An invisible force has a mysterious effect on aging
Shielding fruit flies from Earth’s magnetic field changed their lifespans. (404 Media)
10 ‘Dopamine sites’ are recreating the thrill of shopping without paying
FoodNeverComes has attracted more than 2.7 million visitors since June. (BBC)
Quote of the day
"They decided to break the law."
—Ed Santow, co-founder of the Human Technology Institute, tells ABC radio why there should be serious legal consequences for OpenAI agents hacking Australia's Medicare statistics portal.
One more thing
The quest to figure out farming on Mars
If ever a blade of grass grew on Mars, those days are over. But could they begin again? What would it take to grow plants to feed future astronauts on Mars?
To grow food there, we can’t just drop seeds in the ground and add water. We will need to create a layer of soil that can support life. And to do that, we first have to get rid of the red planet’s toxic salts.
Researchers recently discovered a potential solution—and the early signs are promising. Read the full story.

articles.title: Dar Ventures expands DarE to back Africa’s built-environment tech startups
articles.text:
Dar Ventures, the venture capital arm of design and engineering firm Dar, has partnered with Plug and Play, a global open innovation and early-stage venture platform, to expand its startup programme for technology companies working across architecture, engineering, construction and the wider built environment across Africa and other markets.
The partnership will give the programme, DarE, access to Plug and Play’s global network of startups, investors and corporate partners. Its 12-week hybrid programme will target pre-seed to pre-Series A companies with a minimum viable product (MVP) or market-ready product, primarily across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, while remaining open to companies globally.
Africa’s tech ecosystem raised $1.44 billion across 174 deals in the first half of 2026, while early-stage startups received just $9 million, down from $25 million a year earlier, according to TechCabal Insights. For startups building technology for specialised industries such as construction and infrastructure, access to industry expertise, customers, capital and international markets can offer another route to growth.
DarE will support technologies across the architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) and wider built-environment value chain, including construction, infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), smart cities and sustainability.
The programme will target companies with early market validation and strong potential for commercial adoption and international growth, with selected startups receiving expert support, one-on-one mentorship, direct industry engagement and curated access to investors, corporate partners and international markets.
Dar Ventures said DarE will also build a global alumni community to keep participating companies connected beyond individual cohorts, creating continued opportunities for commercial partnerships, knowledge exchange, investment and cross-market expansion.
“DarE has always been about providing the right platform for entrepreneurs to thrive,” Nader Aboushadi, co-founder of Dar Ventures, said in a statement. “Partnering with Plug and Play allows us to take that ambition to the next level, identifying exceptional founders and giving them access to the expertise and markets, coupled with Dar Ventures projects and capital they need to grow.”
Since launching the programme in 2023 as an incubator, Dar Ventures says DarE has supported 32 startups across four cohorts, connecting founders with industry expertise, commercial opportunities and an investment network. The programme was originally a six-month incubator for AEC technology startups in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), with selected startups eligible for up to $50,000 in equity-free funding.
Dar Ventures said Plug and Play will bring its global network of more than 60 offices, 550 corporate and government partners across more than 25 industries, and more than 10,000 startups accelerated since 2012 to DarE’s next phase. The partnership will expand the programme beyond its original MENA focus.
“Dar is a global industry leader with deep expertise across the built environment, and we are proud to support the next chapter of DarE,” Karima El Hakim, Partner, Africa at Plug and Play, said. “By bringing Plug and Play’s global innovation, venture, and corporate ecosystem to the platform, we aim to connect founders with industry, accelerate commercial adoption, and support technologies shaping how the world is built.”
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Amazon estaria recontratando ex-funcionários após demissões em massa • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Amazon estaria recontratando ex-funcionários após demissões em massa
Empresa parece estar “voltando atrás” com alguns especialistas em IA e Cloud, apontam vazamentos de e-mails do RH.
A Amazon parece ter se arrependido de algumas das mais de 30 mil demissões realizadas ao longo do último ano. A empresa estaria tentando recontratar ex-funcionários que foram mandados embora, sobretudo para as áreas de inteligência artificial e nuvem. A informação vem de emails de RH obtidos pelo site Business Insider, que também confirmou a informação com um porta-voz da companhia.
Desde outubro de 2025, a Amazon anunciou diversos cortes sob a justificativa de “remover burocracia”. Além disso, a vice-presidente sênior de pessoas e tecnologias, Beth Galetti, confirmou em comunicado que as demissões teriam a ver com o avanço da inteligência artificial, que estaria forçando a empresa a se “organizar de forma mais enxuta”.
No último corte, anunciado em julho, a companhia alegou que o “setor se move muito rápido”, e que estaria focada em “acelerar os trabalhos que mais contam”. As demissões atingiram a área de AGI (sigla para inteligência artificial geral, em inglês). O setor de IA seria justamente um dos destinos para as tentativas de recontratação reveladas nesta quarta-feira (23/09). Apesar de curioso, esse movimento da empresa parece ser algo comum por lá: o chamado “bumerangue”.
Um dos emails fala em uma iniciativa “bumerangue” de recontratação liderada pelo Vice-Presidente da Amazon Web Services, Swami Sivasubramanian. Acontece que a prática não é novidade na Amazon. Em uma publicação no site da AWS, a empresa justifica o costume de recontratar esses funcionários que já passaram por lá. A ideia é tê-los de volta para “cumprir o trabalho” que já haviam começado antes.
Já em 2023, um documento vazado apontava a intenção do então vice-presidente de RH da AWS, Ian Wilson, de contar novamente com alguns ex-funcionários demitidos. Agora, outro porta-voz da empresa falou sobre o assunto, afirmando que a empresa está “sempre aberta” a ex-funcionários. Segundo ele, o foco não é, necessariamente, em pessoas que foram demitidas, e sim naqueles que saíram da empresa após o retorno ao presencial por cinco vezes na semana.
Apesar do momento curioso de demissões em massa envolvendo IA e, agora, tentativas de recontratação para o mesmo setor, o movimento bumerangue da Amazon envolve também outras áreas. No outro email revelado pelo Business Insider, um ex-funcionário da AWS Finance é convocado novamente, sendo inclusive questionado se sua saída não teria a ver com a política de retorno ao presencial.
Da mesma forma, alguns posts no LinkedIn mostram mais pessoas da AWS fazendo o mesmo movimento. Em um deles, uma funcionária da área de marketplace acaba de anunciar seu retorno para o time. Outro exemplo envolve um funcionário comemorando seu aniversário de dois anos desde o retorno.
