Zhiye Liu is a news editor, memory reviewer, and SSD tester at Tom’s Hardware. Although he loves everything that’s hardware, he has a soft spot for CPUs, GPUs, and RAM.

articles.title: Après les ventilateurs, Dreo passe au chauffage et prépare une IA pour aider à réduire la facture d’électricité
articles.text:
À la sortie d'un été marqué par le succès de ses ventilateurs, Dreo veut désormais s’installer dans nos maisons toute l’année. La marque lance deux chauffages connectés et un purificateur d’air, avant l’arrivée d’une IA capable de coordonner ses appareils pour améliorer le confort et maîtriser la consommation électrique.
Dreo ne compte pas quitter nos salons avec la fin de l’été. Le fabricant, qui s’est fait connaître en France grâce à ses ventilateurs, présentait ce 23 septembre trois nouveaux appareils pour affronter les mois les plus froids de l'année : les chauffages 720S et 711S, ainsi que le purificateur d’air 530S, déjà aperçu à l’IFA. Tous peuvent être commandés dès maintenant, à des tarifs compris entre 120 et 150 euros, mais les expéditions du 711S ne commenceront que le 28 septembre.
La marque a de bonnes raisons de vouloir prolonger l’aventure. Officiellement arrivée en France en avril, après une phase de test en 2025, elle revendique 180 000 pièces vendues sur Amazon France au 21 septembre, dont 45% au seul mois de juin selon Hugo Esquenet, directeur marketing de la marque en France. Lors de sa présentation à la presse, Dreo a également mis en avant ses premières places dans plusieurs catégories sur Amazon, notamment les ventilateurs aux États-Unis et les chauffages d’appoint au Royaume-Uni.
Deux chauffages pour réchauffer une pièce ou simplement son occupant
Le 720S, proposé à 120 euros, possède une particularité intéressante : sa partie supérieure peut changer de position pour modifier la diffusion de la chaleur. Abaissée, elle dirige le souffle vers une zone précise, par exemple lorsqu’on travaille à son bureau. Relevée, elle répartit l’air chaud à 360° pour couvrir une pièce de 15 à 25 m², selon Dreo.
Le fabricant promet également un fonctionnement pouvant descendre à 25 dB, ainsi qu’un arrêt automatique en cas de basculement accidentel et une protection contre la surchauffe.
Le 711S prend le problème autrement. Vendu 150 euros, il utilise la convection naturelle. L’air froid entre par le bas, se réchauffe puis ressort par le haut, sans ventilateur. De quoi éviter le bruit de soufflerie dans une chambre ou un bureau. Sa façade en verre trempé soigne la présentation et l’appareil peut être fixé au mur pour libérer de la place au sol.
Les deux modèles développent jusqu’à 2 000 watts et disposent d’un mode économique qui module leur puissance à l’approche de la température demandée. Dreo revendique ainsi jusqu’à 40% de consommation en moins par rapport à un fonctionnement continu à pleine puissance. L’économie éventuelle vient donc de la régulation et du temps de fonctionnement réduit, pas d’un meilleur rendement de la résistance électrique.
Ces deux chauffages retrouvent surtout l’application Dreo, dont nous avions apprécié la simplicité et la clarté lors de nos tests de ventilateurs au printemps, les TurboCool 516S et 765S. Avec plusieurs chauffages installés, on peut régler indépendamment la température de chaque pièce, pour garder le bureau au chaud pendant le télétravail tout en chauffant moins la chambre, par exemple.
Les utilisateurs déjà équipés retrouvent ainsi leurs appareils dans une interface familière, sans multiplier les applications. Un confort d’usage qui compte au quotidien et donne davantage d’intérêt à la partie connectée qu’une simple télécommande supplémentaire.
Un purificateur qui ajuste son fonctionnement à la qualité de l’air
Le troisième appareil, le 530S, s’attaque aux poussières, aux particules fines et aux odeurs. Ce purificateur à 140 euros associe un préfiltre, un filtre à particules et du charbon actif, avec un capteur PM2,5 chargé d’adapter automatiquement la ventilation.
Un voyant coloré donne une indication immédiate de la qualité de l’air tandis que l’application permet de programmer l’appareil et de suivre l’usure de son filtre principal. Selon Dreo, ce dernier capture 99,97% des particules en suspension de 0,3 µm, conformément au protocole IEST, dont les particules fines PM2,5.
Le fabricant annonce un débit d’air purifié de 221 m³/h, soit l’équivalent de 4,8 volumes d’air filtrés par heure dans une pièce de 19 m². Cela peut compléter l’aération du logement, mais certainement pas la remplacer.
En 2027, une IA pour faire travailler tous ces appareils ensemble
La nouveauté la plus intéressante pourrait toutefois arriver un peu plus tard. Dreo prépare Air Intelligence, un système destiné à coordonner ses chauffages, ventilateurs, purificateurs et autres appareils compatibles. L’équipe française vise un lancement au minimum en 2027.
Plutôt que de régler chaque produit séparément, l’utilisateur pourrait ainsi laisser l’IA croiser leurs mesures avec la météo, la pollution extérieure ou, encore, les niveaux de pollen. Température, humidité et circulation de l’air serviraient notamment à évaluer le confort ressenti dans le logement, résumé par un score sur 100.
L’autre promesse concerne le portefeuille. L’application doit suivre la consommation des appareils et estimer les économies possibles, en kilowattheures comme en euros. Elle pourrait, par exemple, indiquer combien vous économiseriez en baissant le chauffage d’un degré. Vous choisiriez ensuite d’appliquer ce réglage ou de conserver votre température habituelle.
Toujours côté domotique, Dreo travaille également à rendre ses nouveaux chauffages compatibles avec Matter. Air Intelligence doit ainsi pouvoir dialoguer avec certains équipements d’autres marques, mais le calendrier et la liste des produits pris en charge restent à préciser.

articles.title: Elon Musk chez Paramount-Warner ? Le projet fou qui fait trembler Hollywood
articles.text:
À quelques jours de boucler le rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery pour 110 milliards de dollars (environ 97 milliards d’euros), Paramount cherche de l’argent frais pour financer l’opération. Selon des sources proches du dossier citées par Semafor le 23 septembre 2026, les dirigeants du groupe, mené par son CEO David Ellison, ont évoqué l’idée de proposer à Elon Musk de rejoindre les investisseurs qui apportent des fonds propres à l’opération. Le milliardaire n’est qu’un des noms envisagés.
Semafor n’a pas pu connaître le montant envisagé. Le choix du patron de X, Tesla et SpaceX n’a en tout cas rien d’un hasard. Elon Musk est proche du père de David Ellison, Larry Ellison, cofondateur d’Oracle. Larry Ellison a investi dans Tesla en 2018, a siégé à son conseil d’administration, et a apporté 1 milliard de dollars (environ 880 millions d’euros) au rachat de Twitter par Musk en 2022. Larry Ellison garantit personnellement plus de 40 milliards de dollars (environ 35 milliards d’euros) de fonds propres dans le rachat. Selon Semafor, un chèque de Musk allégerait cette charge et diversifierait l’actionnariat du nouvel ensemble.
Un soutien rassurant pour Wall Street et Paramount, mais risqué politiquement
Sur le plan financier, un chèque du milliardaire serait un signe de confiance fort envers le futur Paramount-Warner Bros., souligne Semafor. Très suivi par les petits porteurs, Elon Musk pourrait aussi rassurer Wall Street quant à la solidité du financement de ce géant du divertissement.
Sur le plan politique, l’arrivée d’Elon Musk au capital serait bien plus délicate. L’idée que l’homme d’affaires puisse détenir des parts, même minoritaires, dans des médias d’information comme CNN et CBS News inquiéterait les démocrates, déjà alarmés en 2024 par son argent, son poids politique et son contrôle de X. Même s’il est peu probable que Musk obtienne un rôle opérationnel dans la gestion des rédactions, sa présence au capital de CNN et de CBS News ferait probablement réagir Washington, estime Semafor.
Un rachat débloqué, mais sous conditions
Ces discussions ont été rendues publiques deux jours après l’accord conclu ce lundi 21 septembre entre Paramount et les 12 États américains qui l’attaquaient en justice pour bloquer le rachat. Le groupe évite ainsi de verser aux actionnaires de Warner Bros. Discovery 7 millions de dollars (environ 6 millions d’euros) par jour de retard au-delà du 1er octobre. David Zaslav, CEO de Warner Bros. Discovery, table sur une finalisation au plus tard début octobre. En échange, Paramount s’est engagé auprès des États à sortir 30 films par an au cinéma et à dépenser 1,5 milliard de dollars (environ 1,3 milliard d’euros) de plus dans la production, sous la surveillance d’un juge pendant cinq ans.
Le rachat touche aussi le streaming, puisqu’il réunit HBO Max et Paramount+ sous le même toit. Le groupe doit surtout faire face à sa dette. Il sortira du rachat avec plus de 80 milliards de dollars de dettes (environ 70 milliards d’euros) pour environ 3 milliards de dollars (2,6 milliards d’euros) de trésorerie disponible par an, selon The Hollywood Reporter. Chaque dollar consacré aux intérêts manquera pour financer des films et des séries.
Elon Musk a fait de la lutte contre le « virus woke » l’un de ses combats favoris sur X. S’il investissait dans le groupe qui possède DC Comics, Star Trek, Harry Potter et Game of Thrones, il n’aurait sans doute aucun rôle formel dans la gestion, comme le souligne Semafor. Il pourrait en revanche commenter publiquement les choix du groupe sur X. Paramount n’a pas souhaité commenter.

articles.title: Reykjavík-based 50skills raises €5.3 million to scale its AI-powered HR workflow automation platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
50skills, a Reykjavík-based startup building the operating system for people workflows, has raised a €5.3 million ($6 million) funding round to accelerate hiring in sales, marketing, and community, while continuing to invest in the platform, including the AI agents that work alongside HR teams.
The round was co-led by Frumtak Ventures, Swiss Post Ventures, Avant, and American family office DRD Investments.
Frumtak Ventures Partner and Chair of the 50skills board, Ásthildur Otharsdóttir, said, “50skills has turned years of customer feedback into a platform organisations run their people operations on every day. As AI changes how work gets done, the companies that win will be those that bring people, workflows and AI agents together safely and effectively. 50skills has the product, the domain expertise and the customer traction to lead that shift. We are proud to continue backing Kristján and the team.”
Founded in 2017, 50skills states that it is building the infrastructure for people and AI agents to run processes together. HR teams use it to design and run the experience of their own employees across the organisation’s existing systems. The platform combines deterministic workflows, AI agents and human oversight with the governance and security that HR and people operations require.
According to the company, HR teams manage hundreds of recurring processes, but many still depend on email, spreadsheets and manual coordination across systems that were never designed to work together.
50skills claims to bring those processes into a single platform. The company notes that HR teams describe the process they want, and the platform turns that into an operational workflow connected to the systems the organisation already runs on. From there, automation handles predictable work, AI agents handle tasks requiring interpretation, and people remain in control of decisions requiring human judgment.
50skills co-founder and CEO, Kristján Freyr Kristjánsson, said, “AI is changing how organisations create value. Our job is to make that practical for the teams responsible for people. We are building the operating system for people workflows, where HR teams design the experience they want for their employees and the platform runs it. The hard part is the balance: deterministic workflows where a process has to run the same way every time, probabilistic agents where a step needs interpretation, and human oversight, governance and security throughout. For HR and people operators, that balance is not optional, it is the job. That is what we build, and this round lets us bring it to many more organisations.”
The company offers two products: Hire, an applicant tracking system, and Journeys, the AI-powered platform for building and running people processes. HR teams describe a process in plain language; the platform builds it, runs it and keeps a complete record of every step.
The Icelandic startup highlighted that its platform has been used to complete over 4 million actions in the past 12 months by HR teams in the Nordics and the UK. Notable clients include Icelandair, Eimskip, Blue Lagoon, Domino’s, and Securitas, as well as public-sector bodies such as the Ministry for Foreign Affairs and the City of Reykjavík, alongside a growing base of customers across the Nordics and the UK.

articles.title: What Is Thermal Stability and Why Does It Matter in Electrical Insulation? - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Temperature is a key factor for any electrical equipment. During operation, it generates heat, and insulation must maintain its electrical and physical properties.
Excessive heat in electrical applications can accelerate ageing and eventually affect insulation performance.
This is the reason thermal stability is required. Thermal stability relates to how well an insulating material withstands heat without unacceptable deterioration. Mica is an inorganic insulation material used in demanding electrical applications, and you should choose the right electrical insulation mica sheet based on the application.
What Is Thermal Stability?
Let’s dive deeper and see what thermal stability exactly does. Thermal stability is a material’s ability to retain its required properties when exposed to elevated temperatures for a specified period.
For electrical insulation, the properties that matter are:
- Dielectric strength
- Mechanical integrity
- Dimensional stability
- Resistance to thermal degradation
- Insulating performance
Thermal stability and thermal endurance differ. Thermal stability is a material characteristic, while thermal endurance evaluation considers how insulation properties change with temperature and ageing time.
Why Does Thermal Stability Matter in Electrical Insulation?
Thermal stability matters in electrical insulation for the following reasons:
- Eliminating premature insulation ageing
Heat can accelerate degradation. Especially when equipment operates near its temperature limits.
- To maintain dielectric performance
Electrical insulation must continue to separate conductive components. And withstand the electrical stresses the system was designed for.
-  Supporting equipment reliability
Insulation deterioration can cause electrical faults, downtime, and shorter component life.
-  Improving material selection
Thermal characteristics help engineers select insulation materials appropriate for the application’s operating environment.
What Happens When Electrical Insulation Is Exposed to Excessive Heat?
This is what happens when electrical insulation is exposed to excessive heat:
- Gradual material ageing
- Loss of mechanical strength
- Changes in dielectric properties
- Cracking, embrittlement, or deformation depending on material
- Reduced service life
- Increased risk of insulation failure
The relationship between temperature and ageing is not simply about whether a material can briefly tolerate a particular temperature.
Duration matters
A material exposed to elevated temperatures continuously can age very differently from one subjected to a short temperature excursion.
This is why thermal endurance evaluations consider both temperature and time.
What Is a Thermal Stability Test?
A thermal stability test evaluates how a material or insulation system responds after exposure to elevated temperatures.
The appropriate test depends on:
- Material type
- Application
- Property being evaluated
- Temperature range
- Ageing duration
- Applicable standard
The general process is:
Step 1: Prepare representative test specimens.
Step 2: Expose specimens to controlled elevated temperatures.
Step 3: Maintain exposure for defined periods.
Step 4: Measure relevant properties before and after ageing.
Step 5: Analyze the degree of property change.
Thermal Stability vs. Thermal Endurance
| Term | What it describes | 
| Thermal stability | Ability to retain required properties when exposed to heat | 
| Thermal endurance | Ability to withstand thermal ageing over time | 
| Thermal ageing | Progressive material degradation caused by temperature exposure | 
| Thermal class | Classification associated with the thermal capability of insulation | 
Why Mica Is Used for High-Temperature Electrical Insulation
Mica is an inorganic mineral-based insulating material. It is valued for electrical insulation applications where heat resistance and dielectric performance are important. Mica can be manufactured into different insulation formats depending on the application. Mica-based insulation is used in electrical equipment that must withstand demanding thermal conditions.
Mica sheet electrical insulation can be used where equipment needs a thin, electrically insulating barrier that can operate in demanding environments.
The role of mica sheets in applications is:
- Motors
- Generators
- Heating equipment
- Transformers
- Electrical appliances
- High-temperature electrical components
Choosing the Right Electrical Insulation Mica Sheet
The right electrical insulation mica sheet should be chosen based on:
- Operating temperature
- Required dielectric strength
- Thickness
- Mechanical requirements
- Flexibility or rigidity
- Application geometry
- Manufacturing and fabrication requirements
- Relevant standards and testing requirements
Selecting an electrical insulation mica sheet requires more than looking at its temperature rating. Engineers also need to consider dielectric requirements, thickness, mechanical characteristics, application conditions, and the expected service environment.
Applications of Mica Insulation Sheets
The applications of mica insulation sheets are:
- Motor and generator insulation
- Coil insulation
- Heating elements
- Electrical appliances
- Transformers
- High-temperature industrial equipment
How Axim Mica Supports Electrical Insulation Applications
Axim Mica focuses on mica-based electrical insulation materials. Material selection should be based on the electrical, thermal, mechanical, and dimensional requirements of the application
Looking for mica insulation for a high-temperature electrical application? Contact Axim Mica to discuss your material requirements.
Conclusion
Thermal stability is an important consideration when selecting electrical insulation. Heat can accelerate ageing and affect material properties over time. A proper thermal stability test or thermal endurance evaluation provides useful evidence about material performance. Engineers should consider temperature, exposure time, electrical stress, mechanical requirements, and the complete operating environment. Mica-based insulation can be an important option for applications where electrical insulation must perform under demanding thermal conditions.

articles.title: Après les avoir installées de force sur votre PC, Microsoft abandonne ces 3 applications
articles.text:
En octobre 2025, Microsoft annonçait en grande pompe l’arrivée de trois nouvelles applications compagnons pour les utilisateurs de Microsoft 365. « Conçues pour rationaliser les flux de travail quotidien », ces trois applications devaient également aider « les utilisateurs à rester concentrés, à réduire les changements de contexte et à effectuer des tâches plus rapidement ».
Moins d’un an plus tard, les résultats escomptés par Microsoft ne sont visiblement pas au rendez-vous. La firme de Redmond vient en effet d’officialiser leur abandon.
Des fonctions déjà présentes dans d’autres applis
À l’époque, Microsoft avait jugé bonne l’idée d’installer ces trois applications (Contact, Calendrier et Fichiers) par défaut chez les utilisateurs Microsoft 365. Ces applications compagnons squattaient donc la barre des tâches de Windows 11 pour vous permettre d’accéder en un clic à des informations essentielles pour vos tâches quotidiennes.
Leur utilité ne semble malheureusement pas avoir convaincu beaucoup de monde. C’est sans doute ce qui a poussé Microsoft à les abandonner. L’entreprise vient d’annoncer qu’elles cesseront totalement de fonctionner à compter du 16 décembre 2026. Elle a d’ailleurs déjà interrompu les mises à jour et les correctifs de sécurité à destination de ces applications, et à même bloqué leur installation automatique via les mises à jour Microsoft 365.
La fin précipitée de ces applications n’a rien de très étonnant. Car les fonctionnalités qu’elles proposaient faisaient doublon avec d’autres fonctions déjà présentes dans les différents outils de Microsoft. Le Calendrier et les Contacts sont déjà intégrés à Outlook et Microsoft Teams, et les Fichiers sont accessibles via la recherche Windows, l’Explorateur de fichiers, Sharepoint, OneDrive et même directement dans les applis Office. Sans oublier l’assistant intelligent Copilot qui peut être interrogé pour retrouver rapidement des fichiers, des personnes ou des rendez-vous.
Des applis installées de force, mais à supprimer manuellement
Si Microsoft n’a pas eu de mal à imposer l’installation de ses applications compagnons sur le PC des utilisateurs Microsoft 365, l’entreprise semble avoir un peu plus de mal pour ce qui est de leur désinstallation. Comble de l’ironie, ces trois applications, bien que rendues inutilisables, resteront installées sur votre machine. Microsoft n’a prévu aucune mise à jour permettant de les faire disparaître. C’est à vous que reviendra la charge de leur désinstallation.
Une opération, somme toute simple, que vous devrez réaliser manuellement, mais dont vous auriez pu vous passer. Vous devrez en effet vous rendre dans les Paramètres > Applications > Applications installées afin de rechercher les applications Microsoft 365 Compagnons pour enfin les Désinstaller.

articles.title: Srijan Realty aims to redefine residential living in Kolkata with the launch of Orizon
articles.text:
Srijan Realty aims to redefine residential living in Kolkata with the launch of Orizon
Spread across 8.3 acres on the Southern EM Bypass, the six‑tower, 702‑unit community blends 80% open space, barrier‑free design, and IGBC Platinum pre‑certified sustainability.
Srijan Realty, one of Eastern India’s most established residential developers, has announced the launch of Orizon, a 702-unit residential community spread across 8.3 acres off the Southern EM Bypass in Jagaddal, South Kolkata.
The launch arrives as the corridor completes a decade-long transformation from a peripheral suburb into one of the city’s most aspirational residential addresses, supported by expanding metro and suburban rail connectivity, dual EM Bypass access, and a maturing ecosystem of schools, hospitals and retail destinations.
Located on BC Roy Road in Jagaddal, with two access points off the Southern EM Bypass roughly 400 metres and 750 metres apart, Orizon comprises six high-rise towers ranging from 17 to 23 storeys, housing 702 three-bedroom residences sized between approximately 1,208 and 1,650 square feet.
Roughly 80% of the 8.3-acre site, 85% including podium-level landscaping, has been kept open, an unusually low-density ratio for a development of this scale so close to the city.
Shahid Khudiram Metro Station is roughly 14 minutes away, with Sonarpur railway station around 15 minutes; Spencer’s, Wood Square Mall and Southwinds Galleria are all within a six-minute drive.
A life beyond the ordinary
Orizon’s design philosophy takes its name from the word “horizon”, built around the idea that space, light, and an unobstructed view are increasingly scarce commodities in a city that has grown denser over the past two decades.
Residences feature terrace-style and standing balconies intended to maximize natural light and cross-ventilation, while the project’s golden façade, visible from the EM Bypass, is conceived as a visual landmark along the corridor.
Despite its dual EM Bypass access and proximity to South Kolkata’s commercial nodes, the development has been planned to function as a self-contained green enclave, insulated from the congestion typically associated with high-density urban corridors.
Schools, including BDM International and Narayana, along with healthcare providers such as Apollo Hospital’s upcoming campus, Peerless Hospital and RN Tagore Hospital, are within a 20-minute radius.
Lifestyle infrastructure
At the centre of the development sits a roughly 33,000-square-foot clubhouse featuring an infinity-edge swimming pool, jacuzzi and dedicated kids’ pool, alongside a 21,000-square-foot podium-level garden anchoring a sports arena with facilities for tennis, basketball, pickleball and badminton.
Indoor offerings extend to a gymnasium, yoga and meditation studio, squash court, co-working space, home theatre, library, and a dedicated senior citizens’ lounge. The developer says these amenities are designed to serve every age group within a single community rather than cater narrowly to one demographic.
Inclusive, barrier-free design
A defining feature of Orizon is its barrier-free design, incorporating wheelchair access ramps, lift cabins wide enough to accommodate wheelchairs, Braille and voice-enabled lift controls, accessible toilets and designated accessible parking throughout common areas.
Srijan Realty positions this not as a regulatory minimum but as a forward-looking response to India’s multigenerational households, where ageing parents, differently abled family members, and young children increasingly share a single home and require equal, independent access to shared spaces.
Sustainability and future readiness
Orizon has been pre-certified for IGBC Platinum design, India’s highest green building rating, with features including rainwater harvesting, solar power for common areas, low-flow water fixtures, energy-efficient LED lighting, organic waste management, and EV charging infrastructure.
Buildings certified to this standard typically deliver 20-30% energy savings and 30-50% water savings compared with conventional construction.
Srijan Realty has been among Eastern India’s most respected real estate developers for over two decades, with a portfolio of residential communities, integrated townships, retail destinations and commercial developments across Kolkata and beyond.
Leadership Perspective
Dinesh Agarwal, Director, Srijan Realty, said Orizon reflects how they believe Kolkata wants to live today. “Homebuyers are no longer choosing between space and connectivity, or between design and responsibility - they expect all of it together. Southern EM Bypass has moved past being an emerging corridor - it is now one of South Kolkata's defining growth engines, and we have been part of that story for over a decade,” he said.
Agarwal added that Srijan Realty has built Orizon as a “community first, planned around low-density living, open space, and lifestyle infrastructure that we believe will hold its value well beyond the next market cycle, with inclusivity and sustainability designed into its foundations rather than added on at the end”.
Guided by the philosophy that “great homes are built on trust,” the company continues to focus on design quality, customer-centric innovation, and long-term community building.

articles.title: Se jubila a los 67 años con 142 días de vacaciones sin gastar. En lugar de disfrutarlos, se los ha regalado a sus compañeros: "Se los dejo a quienes los necesiten"
articles.text:
Marialuisa Ferramosca podría haber llegado al final de su carrera pensando en cómo gastar los días de descanso que nunca utilizó. No eran pocos: nada menos que 142 jornadas de vacaciones, casi cinco meses. Pero la directora del servicio de emergencias SUEM 118 de Treviso ha decidido jubilarse a los 67 años sin disfrutarlas y destinarlas literalmente a sus compañeros. Después de casi cuatro décadas atendiendo emergencias, su último gesto será dejar también su tiempo a los que puedan necesitarlo para algo mucho más urgente que unas vacaciones.
Jubilarse con meses de vacaciones en el limbo. Ferramosca dejará definitivamente el servicio el 30 de septiembre y será oficialmente jubilada desde el 1 de octubre. Los 142 días que tenía acumulados serán recalculados e incorporados al fondo de ferie solidali de la ULSS 2, un mecanismo pensado para ayudar a trabajadores que necesitan ausentarse por circunstancias especialmente delicadas.
El ejemplo más claro, compañeros que necesitan permanecer junto a un hijo enfermo: Ferramosca no decide personalmente quién recibe sus jornadas, sino que entrega su saldo para que el sistema pueda redistribuirlo entre quienes cumplan los requisitos.
Cuatro décadas de urgencias. La médica comenzó a trabajar en el hospital Ca' Foncello de Treviso en 1988, inicialmente como cirujana de urgencias, después de licenciarse en Medicina en 1987. Se especializó en Cirugía General y posteriormente en Anestesia y Reanimación, y en 1999 se incorporó al SUEM 118, el servicio de emergencias sanitarias.
En marzo de 2020 asumió su dirección provisional precisamente cuando estalló la pandemia y la central llegó a gestionar picos superiores a las 500 llamadas diarias. Desde octubre de 2021 ocupaba oficialmente la dirección del servicio.
Su CV es también una historia de catástrofes. Ferramosca estuvo en primera línea durante la explosión de ButanGas de 1996, el incendio de la fábrica De'Longhi en 2007, la pandemia y el accidente de 2023 en Mestre, donde un autobús cayó desde un paso elevado. Algunas emergencias comenzaron incluso antes de recibir el aviso: durante el incendio de De'Longhi, su equipo estaba realizando unas prácticas cuando vio levantarse la columna de humo y salió hacia el lugar.
Ella, sin embargo, asegura recordar tanto esas grandes catástrofes como intervenciones mucho más pequeñas: después de tantos años, explica, son los rostros y las miradas de los familiares los que permanecen.
UN VISTAZO A...
Lo que no son los días de vacaciones. Posiblemente la gran pregunta. Lo cierto es que el mecanismo italiano permite algo más interesante que una simple transferencia entre dos trabajadores. Las jornadas cedidas pasan a una bolsa solidaria desde la que pueden asignarse a empleados con determinadas necesidades, de modo que Ferramosca no sabe necesariamente quién terminará utilizando el tiempo al que ha renunciado.
La propia dirección de la ULSS 2 ha hecho público el gesto: su director general, Giancarlo Bizzarri, agradeció tanto sus décadas de trabajo como los numerosos días dejados en el fondo para compañeros que los necesiten.
En España sería muy difícil. Sí, una réplica literal chocaría con la protección que la legislación española concede a las vacaciones. El artículo 38 del Estatuto de los Trabajadores establece un mínimo de 30 días naturales y las configura como un periodo de descanso retribuido que, como regla general, debe disfrutarse y no puede sustituirse por una compensación económica.
En el empleo público, el Estatuto Básico del Empleado Público establece igualmente el derecho a vacaciones anuales retribuidas y protege su disfrute. Eso no impide que convenios o acuerdos específicos puedan crear mecanismos solidarios relacionados con determinados permisos o días adicionales, pero un trabajador español no puede simplemente acumular sus vacaciones legales, renunciar a ellas al jubilarse y entregarlas libremente a una bolsa para sus compañeros como ha ocurrido en este caso italiano.
La jubilación de Ferramosca. La mujer llega a los 67 años después de una carrera profesional que comenzó en 1988. Así, alguien dedicado durante décadas a acudir cuando otros necesitaban ayuda se marcha dejando casi cinco meses de su propio descanso para que otros puedan hacer precisamente eso mismo.
Ahora asegura a los medios italianos que todavía no tiene grandes planes para la jubilación, aunque entre sus aficiones está el tai chi. Después de 38 años de emergencias, más de 25 vinculada al SUEM 118 y una pandemia dirigiendo un servicio que recibía más de 500 llamadas al día, se marcha sin utilizar sus últimos 142 días de colgar el teléfono.

articles.title: CISA: Ransomware gangs now exploiting critical TeamCity flaw
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies on Wednesday that ransomware gangs are now also exploiting a critical JetBrains TeamCity vulnerability patched in July.
JetBrains patched the security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-63077) on July 25 in TeamCity On-Premises versions 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3, saying it is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability that lets attackers with HTTP(S) access execute arbitrary operating system commands.
"An unauthenticated attacker could exploit the vulnerability via the TeamCity agent polling protocol to bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the TeamCity server process," it said.
"Depending on the privileges granted to the TeamCity server process, a successful attack could expose TeamCity data, configurations, and stored credentials, modify server state, and potentially compromise the integrity of build artifacts and downstream CI/CD pipelines."
Almost two weeks later, on August 5, CISA added CVE-2026-63077 to its catalog of actively exploited vulnerabilities and ordered U.S. federal agencies to secure their networks against ongoing attacks within three days.
JetBrains confirmed that the flaw was exploited in the wild on August 7, shared indicators of compromise, and urged customers who couldn't immediately patch their servers to limit access to trusted networks.
Now exploited in ransomware attacks
While CISA has not yet shared information about attacks targeting CVE-2026-63077, it updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (KEV) again on Wednesday, flagging the vulnerability as being abused by ransomware gangs.
In total, since October 2023, the cybersecurity agency has tagged four TeamCity security issues as exploited in the wild, all of which have also been abused in ransomware attacks.
Security threat watchdog Shadowserver is now tracking just over 160 TeamCity servers unpatched against the CVE-2026-63077 flaw, down from an initial 700 Internet-exposed servers vulnerable to attacks spotted right after the vulnerability was patched.
Because state-backed hacking groups and ransomware gangs have often leveraged TeamCity vulnerabilities in attacks, IT administrators are advised to patch Internet-exposed servers immediately.
For instance, in October 2024, U.S. and U.K. cyber agencies warned that APT29 hackers linked to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) were targeting vulnerable JetBrains TeamCity and Zimbra servers "at a mass scale."
TeamCity is a Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) platform used by software developers and DevOps teams to automate building, testing, and deploying software code.
JetBrains says more than 30,000 DevOps teams use TeamCity at many high-profile companies, including Citibank, Amazon Games, Tesla, and Samsung.

Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

articles.title: AI is dominating the conversation at Climate Week
articles.text:
AI is dominating the conversation at Climate Week
The debate is louder than usual as climate voices gather.
This week, world leaders descended on Manhattan for the UN General Assembly. It’s also New York Climate Week—investors, policymakers, advocates, and journalists are colliding at panels, talks, and fancy dinners.
With so many climate voices in one place, the discourse can feel a little louder than usual. This year, the unavoidable topic is artificial intelligence.
There’s been a growing tension bubbling up about AI’s impacts on climate and climate tech. Depending on where you stand, you might point to AI’s potential for advancing research, or to the way funding and attention from Big Tech is trickling into energy startups. Or you might focus on the emissions-heavy natural-gas buildout that’s unfolding to meet the sector’s electricity demand.
Everyone seems to agree that AI is important. The big question for those in the climate world, and the conversation I’m constantly having and hearing this week, involves how you see its influence unfolding.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres highlighted the AI and climate crossover in a speech on the first day of the assembly. “The climate crisis fuels instability and displacement,” Guterres said. “Artificial intelligence could help solve all these challenges, or it could make them worse.”
It feels relevant that this year is the first that the world has really had to grapple with the fact that climate goals are slipping out of reach. A recent report from the UN Environment Program said that the world has nearly passed the point where we could possibly keep warming to less than 1.5 °C above preindustrial levels.
Since we’ve essentially missed this target, the report lays out the need not only to quickly and drastically reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, but also to employ carbon removal to help suck up emissions that have already been released into the atmosphere.
The billion-dollar question is whether AI could help with any of this.
The energy-intensive technology is certainly shining a spotlight on the need to build out electricity supplies and shore up grid reliability. The result is more attention and money for energy technologies, some of which happen to be low- or zero-emissions.
As I’ve covered before, startups across the energy and climate sectors are benefiting. Firms in nuclear, geothermal, wind, and solar power have signed deals with the likes of Google, Meta, and others looking to power their new or growing data centers.
Global climate-tech investment from venture capital hit $26 billion in the first half of 2026, according to data from Currence, a finance tracker for the industry. That’s 55% higher than last year, and products and services for data centers are getting a massive slice of that pie.
But as a Semafor piece about the report points out, some sectors are slipping through the cracks: Carbon management and low-carbon fuels saw VC investment plummet this year. These are important solutions for addressing climate change but may not be able to sell themselves to a data center.
So far, the data center buildout has come with a hefty emissions toll. A few years ago, Microsoft, Google, and Meta all had ambitious goals to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions. Now they’ve all seen emissions rise, largely because of data centers that are needed to power AI.
Some people are optimistic. AI could help speed up progress in areas like the search for new catalysts, as Evelyn Wang, MIT’s VP of energy and climate, pointed out during a panel. And data centers won’t add to climate and water problems forever, Wang told the Associated Press. (She puts the timeline at about a decade until data centers no longer add to planet-warming emissions.)
But a whole lot of natural gas is coming online to meet the immediate demand created by new data centers. And once those power plants are built, they have a decades-long lifetime.
That’s partly why public pushback to AI is growing—people are seeing more pollution and noise near these data centers and the power plants that provide them with electricity. Overall, what I’m hearing this week is that many in the climate sector are skeptical of AI, at best.
“AI leaders are now on thin ice when it comes to license to operate and sinking deep underwater when it comes to public support,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell in a speech this week. “Tech titans need to start showing why the benefits of AI outweigh its skyrocketing costs—for the many, not just the tiny few.”
This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here.

articles.title: The GPU Madness Has Come to This: 9070 XT vs. 5060 Ti 16GB
articles.text:
Good news, guys. I've saved up my dollarydoos and I'm finally ready to buy a new graphics card for playing all my favorite video games. So let's go shopping, shall we?
I've got around $1,200 to spend here in Australia, roughly $850 USD, though ideally we'd like to spend a little less. Let's aim for a mid-range GeForce GPU because we've heard over on Reddit that GeForce is better than Radeon, so that's probably correct. Clearly, we're off to a very sensible start.
The GeForce RTX 5060 Ti seems like what we're after, the 16GB model of course, because we might eventually play something other than Fortnite. You never know.
Wow, what's going on here? The last time we checked, admittedly earlier in the year, the 5060 Ti 16GB was priced around $750. Now they're starting at $1,050 and are mostly out of stock.
In fact, PC Case Gear has just a single model available, a PNY card for $1,049. Yikes. Bugger that, let's try Mwave. Here we go, $769. Nice. Wait, it's out of stock. Okay, $1,000, also out of stock. $1,049, finally one that's available, and it's another PNY model. Then there's the Asus Dual at $1,129. Man, it's rough out here.
Okay, so we know those Radeon GPUs aren't meant to be as good, but we're getting desperate, so let's take a look. Based on what we're seeing at local retailers, a GPU called the Radeon RX 9070 XT appears to be the direct competitor to the 5060 Ti 16GB. They're a little more expensive, but pricing is surprisingly similar, starting at $1,149 with plenty of models around $1,249. Hopefully it's not much slower than the GeForce GPU.
Just to make sure this isn't some bizarre Australian pricing anomaly, we also checked Newegg. There, the 5060 Ti 16GB starts at around $780, which means the 9070 XT is actually cheaper, with Radeon models starting at roughly $740. Both GPUs come with 16GB of VRAM, so we clearly need to see how they compare.
For that, we've benchmarked the Radeon RX 9070 XT and GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB across 52 games to see what gamers are actually getting for roughly an $800 budget overseas or around $1,200 in Australia. Rather than walk through all 52 games individually, we'll highlight some of the more interesting results before getting to the full performance summary and cost-per-frame analysis. Let's do it...
Test System Specs
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1A4] Resizable BAR Enabled | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | Sapphire Radeon RX 9070 XT Pure Asus Prime GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 16GB | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 25H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.8.1 GeForce Game Ready Driver 610.88 | 
Benchmarks
007 First Light
Starting with 007 First Light, we see the 9070 XT is 81% faster at 1440p using the Medium preset, with frame rates jumping from 67 fps on the RTX 5060 Ti to 121 fps on the Radeon GPU. That seems like quite a lot.
The 4K results are even worse for the GeForce GPU. Again using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT was 106% faster, taking performance from a measly 34 fps to a highly playable 70 fps.
Switching to the Ultra preset didn't help the RTX 5060 Ti all that much. The margins did come down, but even so, the 9070 XT was still 62% faster at 1440p and 78% faster at 4K. At native resolutions, the 5060 Ti is effectively limited to 1440p here, while 4K is a realistic option with the 9070 XT.
Spider-Man 2
Swinging into Spider-Man 2, the 9070 XT continues to flex on the 5060 Ti. At 1440p using the Very High preset, it averaged 130 fps compared with 81 fps on the 5060 Ti, a massive 60% performance advantage.
Even at 4K, the Radeon GPU remained rock-solid at 80 fps, making it 70% faster than the 5060 Ti, which managed just 47 fps.
Enabling the demanding Ray Tracing Ultimate mode brings frame rates down, but the hierarchy stays firmly in place. At 1440p, the 9070 XT delivered a playable 67 fps, making it 60% faster than the 5060 Ti's 42 fps. Then at 4K, the 9070 XT averaged 36 fps, giving it a 50% advantage over the 5060 Ti's cinematic 24 fps.
Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
Moving over to Lego Batman, we see the bloodbath continue. At 1440p using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT pumps out 234 fps compared with 149 fps for the 5060 Ti, making the Radeon card a cool 57% faster. Bumping the resolution to 4K makes the Nvidia card's value proposition look even more embarrassing. The 9070 XT crushes it by an 88% margin, delivering a buttery-smooth 147 fps while the 5060 Ti trails far behind at just 78 fps.
Cranking the visuals up to the Epic preset gives the RTX 5060 Ti a slight breather in terms of the performance gap, but it still gets thoroughly outclassed. At 1440p, the Radeon GPU maintains a comfortable 40% lead, hitting 102 fps versus 73 fps for the GeForce GPU.
Pushing the resolution to 4K, the 9070 XT manages to scrape by with an almost 60 fps experience, making it 51% faster than the 5060 Ti's rather pathetic 39 fps. Ultimately, while 1440p is doable on both GPUs, anyone hoping for a decent native 4K experience here will be severely disappointed by the GeForce card.
Fortnite
Fortnite gives the RTX 5060 Ti its closest showing yet, at least in lightweight competitive settings. At 1440p using Performance Mode, the 9070 XT was just 14% faster, though that gap stretched to 30% at 4K.
However, once Unreal Engine 5's full graphical suite is unleashed using Epic Quality settings with ray tracing enabled, normal service resumes. At 1440p, the 9070 XT rendered 120 fps, making it 54% faster than the 5060 Ti's 78 fps. Then at 4K, AMD held a flat 50% lead at 66 fps versus 44 fps.
Forza Horizon 6
In Forza Horizon 6, the rasterized and ray-traced results tell an identical story of AMD dominance. Using the Extreme preset at 1440p, the 9070 XT was 65% faster, rendering 140 fps compared with the 5060 Ti's 85 fps.
Moving to 4K, the 9070 XT breezed past the 100 fps mark, while the 5060 Ti failed to maintain 60 fps, giving the Radeon GPU a 76% advantage.
Tossing ray tracing into the mix highlights the hardware gap even further. At 1440p, the 9070 XT remained 79% ahead with 75 fps versus 42 fps. At 4K, both GPUs struggled, but the 9070 XT's 43 fps was still 79% faster than the unplayable 24 fps produced by the RTX 5060 Ti. With some upscaling support, the Radeon GPU would at least be usable here.
Crimson Desert
Next up is Crimson Desert, where the 9070 XT maintains a commanding lead. Using the Medium preset at 1440p, the Radeon GPU averaged 103 fps compared with 67 fps for the 5060 Ti, a 54% performance advantage.
At 4K, the disparity widened considerably. The Radeon GPU cruised along at 66 fps for a 69% advantage, while the GeForce card stumbled into sub-40 fps territory at just 39 fps.
Enabling the Cinematic quality preset doesn't do Team Green any favors either. At 1440p, the 9070 XT remained 54% faster, rendering 86 fps against the 5060 Ti's 56 fps. Meanwhile, at 4K, the 9070 XT averaged a respectable 53 fps, beating the 5060 Ti's 32 fps by 66%. For a smooth visual showcase at maximum settings, the 5060 Ti clearly punches well below its inflated price point.
Ark: Survival Ascended
Unreal Engine 5 continues to take no prisoners, but the RTX 5060 Ti suffers a particularly grim fate here. At 1440p using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT delivered 70% greater performance, managing 51 fps while Nvidia's offering crawled along at just 30 fps.
Stepping up to 4K effectively turned the RTX 5060 Ti into a slideshow at 18 fps, whereas the Radeon GPU was 72% faster at 31 fps. That's not exactly lightning quick, but it is substantially better.
Things get downright comical with the Epic preset. At 1440p, the 9070 XT was 81% faster, and at 4K the gap widened to 83%, leaving the 5060 Ti choking at a miserable 12 fps average with single-digit 1% lows. Simply put, native rendering on the 5060 Ti is essentially unplayable across the board in this title. It's so bad, in fact, that most of these results wouldn't be made workable even with Ultra Performance DLSS thrown into the mix.
Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
In Night City, traditionally a stronghold for Nvidia hardware, particularly with ray tracing enabled, the raw tier mismatch makes for some brutal viewing. At 1440p using the Ultra preset, the 9070 XT sat comfortably at 131 fps, giving it a massive 90% lead over the 5060 Ti's 69 fps. Stepping up to 4K widened the gap further to 103%, with the Radeon GPU maintaining a playable 63 fps average while the 5060 Ti stumbled along at just 31 fps.
Even with Ray Tracing Ultra engaged, the 5060 Ti simply lacks the horsepower to compete. At 1440p, the 9070 XT was nearly twice as fast, with a 96% performance advantage.
Native 4K proved punishing for both, but the 9070 XT's 26 fps still placed it 86% ahead of the 5060 Ti's slideshow-like 14 fps average.
Stalker 2: Heart of Chornobyl
Venturing into the Zone at native resolution yields another heavy round of defeats for the GeForce GPU. At 1440p using the Medium preset, the 9070 XT clocked in at 122 fps, 54% faster than the 5060 Ti's 79 fps, with the Radeon GPU's 1% lows even surpassing the GeForce card's average frame rate. At 4K, the Radeon GPU delivered a 63% uplift, managing 70 fps while the 5060 Ti fell flat at 43 fps.
Dialing the visuals up to Epic tightens things slightly, but the hierarchy remains unchanged. At 1440p, the 9070 XT stayed 52% ahead with 70 fps versus 46 fps.
At 4K, neither GPU is delivering a high-refresh experience, but the 9070 XT's 40 fps still outpaced the 5060 Ti's 26 fps by 54%.
Pragmata
Rounding out this portion of the testing with Pragmata, the Radeon GPU continues its dominant sweep. At 1440p using the Max Quality settings, the 9070 XT rendered 138 fps, outpacing the 5060 Ti's 89 fps by 55%. Moving to 4K pushed that lead to 63%, with AMD hitting a smooth 78 fps while Nvidia struggled to break 50 fps at 48 fps.
Enabling ray tracing barely slowed down the 9070 XT. At 1440p with full ray tracing, the Radeon GPU averaged 135 fps, enjoying a 63% advantage over the 5060 Ti's 83 fps.
Then at 4K, the 9070 XT averaged a solid 76 fps for a 69% margin over the 5060 Ti's 45 fps. With both GPUs selling for equivalent money, giving up more than 60% of your frame rate for the GeForce badge is a tough pill to swallow.
Arc Raiders
Finally, in Arc Raiders, we see some of the narrowest margins of the test suite, though the 9070 XT still wins in every configuration. Using Epic Quality with RT Static at 1440p, the Radeon GPU was 30% faster, extending that margin to 38% at 4K.
Stepping up to RT Epic at 1440p compressed the margin to its narrowest point at 24%. At 4K, the gap settled at 30%, with the 9070 XT reaching 133 fps while the 5060 Ti achieved 102 fps. Both cards provide high frame rates here, but you're still getting roughly a third more performance from the Radeon GPU for the same money.
Performance Summary: 52 Games
Looking at the massive 52-game average across mixed quality settings, the overall picture doesn't get any prettier for Nvidia. At 1440p, the Radeon RX 9070 XT pulls ahead by 62%, averaging 123 fps compared with the RTX 5060 Ti's 76 fps.
In fact, the Radeon card's 1% lows of 97 fps comfortably beat the GeForce card's average frame rate, highlighting just how wide the performance gulf really is.
Step up to 4K and the margin widens to 71% in AMD's favor. Here, the 9070 XT delivers a genuinely smooth 72 fps average, whereas the 5060 Ti is left struggling in the low 40s at just 42 fps, with its 1% lows dipping to 33 fps.
When essentially the same retail price gets you a card capable of smooth 4K gaming on one side and a GPU that's clearly better suited to 1440p on the other, the value equation for the 5060 Ti completely falls apart.
Cost Per Frame
Australian Dollars
To better illustrate the value equation, here's the cost-per-frame data based on current Australian retail pricing. Despite coming in $100 cheaper, the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB still costs 48% more per frame based on our 1440p results and 57% more at 4K. That's crazy.
United States
But the situation is far worse in the United States, and we strongly suspect Australian pricing will catch up over the coming weeks, as retailers currently appear hesitant to restock RTX 5060 Ti cards at today's asking prices.
Over at Newegg, the 5060 Ti comes in 71% more expensive per frame based on our 1440p data and an insane 81% more expensive at 4K.
There's really not much more that needs to be said here.
The GeForce Tax Is Getting Ridiculous
It's hard to say when this madness will end, or even how much worse things might get. If we'd told you just a few months ago that the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB would soon cost as much as, or even more than, the Radeon RX 9070 XT, most of you probably would have laughed us out of the room. And we wouldn't blame you. It's hard to imagine, but here we are.
In part, these inflated prices are the result of the industry-wide memory shortage. The 9070 XT is now at least 23% above MSRP, though the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB is a little over 80% above its MSRP. Both feature 16GB of VRAM, but the GeForce GPU uses GDDR7 memory whereas the 9070 XT still relies on GDDR6, so there are cost differences there.
Tying into this, Nvidia recently notified board partners that it was increasing prices for its GPU and memory bundles, which was quickly followed by significant price increases for GeForce graphics cards, as we've seen with the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB. Exactly how much is the increase isn't publicly known. I have some off-the-record details, but it sounds as though they've added a bit extra on top, which would help explain how the 5060 Ti has ended up more than 80% above MSRP.
Nvidia is also able to get away with these extreme prices because of AI demand. That doesn't just mean data centers, which aren't buying GeForce gaming cards, but also users building systems for local AI workloads. Those buyers are helping soak up these hideously overpriced GeForce GPUs.
As I understand it, and please note that I am far from an expert on this AI stuff, there is significantly greater demand for the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB than the Radeon RX 9070 XT among users running AI workloads locally. As we've just seen, the RX 9070 XT is an extremely capable gaming GPU, and it actually offers more raw memory bandwidth than the RTX 5060 Ti despite using GDDR6 memory. Memory bandwidth can also be an important factor in AI workloads.
However, Nvidia remains the dominant choice for local AI builders. The disparity in demand largely comes down to software support, ecosystem maturity, and ease of use.
Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem remains one of the foundational software layers for modern AI development. New AI models, interfaces, fine-tuning tools, and GitHub projects are frequently developed, optimized, and tested on Nvidia hardware first. Some popular tools and inference frameworks also specifically target Nvidia GPUs.
The Radeon RX 9070 XT can be a compelling option for users willing to work within AMD's software ecosystem, particularly under Linux, where its raw performance and memory bandwidth can be put to good use. But for most local AI users, the RTX 5060 Ti remains the "safer bet" as it guarantees compatibility with upcoming AI tools, requires less troubleshooting, and dominates in image generation. For these reasons, Nvidia has been able to jack up pricing and keep selling GPUs, but in doing so fewer and fewer gamers are now going GeForce, not that Nvidia cares.
If you're building a gaming PC and want more than 8GB of VRAM, as it stands, Radeon is increasingly the only way to go. At these prices, paying the GeForce tax simply isn't worth it.

articles.title: Island Raises $400 Million at $6.4 Billion Valuation
articles.text:
Island announced Thursday that it raised $400 million in a Series F funding round, bringing the company’s valuation to $6.4 billion.
The latest funding round was led by Evolution Equity Partners and it brings the total investment in Island to well over $1 billion. The company will use the money to enhance its platform and boost growth.
Island has developed an agentic control plane designed to govern both human interactions and automated workflows across endpoints, software, and networks.
Expanding beyond its core enterprise browser offering, the platform now uses an endpoint-outward SASE architecture to deliver zero trust network access (ZTNA), device posture assessment, and inline data loss prevention (DLP) without traditional VPNs.
Security teams can implement granular DLP rules directly where work occurs, blocking unapproved clipboard transfers, downloads, and screen captures.
The platform delivers ZTNA by constantly validating user credentials and environmental context before permitting connections to private data centers or hosted services.
For organizations using AI, the solution provides guardrails that separate proprietary information from external language models while mitigating prompt injection risks.
“Island created the first Enterprise Browser to protect the primary place people work. From there, we expanded into data protection and DLP, then built a next-generation SASE architecture from the endpoint outward,” said Mike Fey, CEO and co-founder of Island. “Those combined capabilities give CIOs, CISOs, and business unit owners one security, productivity, and governance framework for everywhere human and agentic work occurs.”

articles.title: Canvas UI Ships 35 HTML-in-Canvas Components That Run WebGL and WebGPU Effects Over Live DOM
articles.text:
Canvas UI, an open source component library from React Bits creator David Haz, has launched as the first library built on the experimental HTML-in-Canvas API, running GPU effects over real, interactive page content.
The library ships 35 components, including pointer-driven fluid, fire, glass lenses, ASCII filters, VHS grain and particle reveals. Every effect has a WebGL build using GLSL and a WebGPU build using WGSL through vgpu, with wrappers for React, Solid, Preact, Vue, Svelte and dependency-free vanilla TypeScript.
Rather than painting a dead bitmap, most components use Chrome's html-in-canvas API to lay out live DOM inside a canvas, capture it with drawElementImage, upload it as a texture and distort it in a shader. Text stays selectable, links stay clickable, and the content stays in the accessibility tree. Components are distributed as source through a shadcn-compatible registry rather than as a package:
npx shadcn@latest add @canvas-ui/liquid-react
The full experience needs Chrome with the canvas-draw-element flag, or an origin trial token, which runs from Chrome 148 through 150 and is bound to a single domain. Elsewhere, html-in-canvas effects fall back to a plain GPU overlay or render the wrapped content unchanged, and the 3D object components work everywhere.
Because code is copied into the repository, upgrades mean re-running the install command and reconciling local edits. Switching renderers is mostly replacing the installed file with the -webgpu registry item, which adds vgpu and @webgpu/types. The project also documents that Chrome 150's changes to texElementImage2D and copyElementImageToTexture require no migration, since capture happens through the 2D API and uploads use standard texImage2D or copyExternalImageToTexture.
shadcn called it one of the most impressive registries they have seen, and the Chrome for Developers account said it was good to see html-in-canvas empowering new frameworks. Writing a detailed teardown, Flavio Copes praised the unglamorous engineering: the Liquid component stops its loop with IntersectionObserver when off-screen, honours prefers-reduced-motion, and releases textures, programs and listeners on unmount. His advice was to use one strong effect rather than six, and to avoid dashboards, checkout flows and documentation sites.
On Hacker News, one commenter responded to a demo's banner with scepticism about a Google-only capability:
Use Chrome... and aren't we supposed to reject these technologies that allow Google to Embrace, Extend, Extinguish?
Kudos to the artist in spite of this unfortunately esoteric (wish it weren't) concern
Another user replied:
The standardization process requires implementations before standardization. And the most recent comments on the WHATWG issue are from Jake Archibald (Mozilla) and Anne van Kesteren (Apple). This isn't a unilateral Google project.
Accessibility discussion in the WICG explainer is still open, including how drawable subtrees without updated geometry are exposed.
Paper Shaders offers zero-dependency canvas shaders installed from npm, but they sit behind or around content as texture. React Bits, from the same author, animates DOM directly. Canvas UI is the only option using the page itself as shader input, which is also why it depends on a feature that Safari and Firefox do not implement.
Licensing is MIT plus the Commons Clause, so commercial use is allowed but reselling the components is not. The repository has passed 4,600 stars, and the registry is MCP-ready, letting assistants browse and install components through the shadcn MCP server.

articles.title: Malas noticias para 'Gremlins 3', que lanza su primer tráiler pero retrasa (y mucho) su fecha de estreno
articles.text:
Cuando hace unos meses se confirmó el desarrollo de Gremlins 3, los fans se llevaron una inesperada alegría. La saga de fantasía los ochenta regresaba con una nueva entrega que, además contaría con Chris Columbus, guionista de la original, como director. El cineasta de obras como Solo en casa, La Señora Doubtfire o las dos primeras cintas de Harry Potter se haría cargo de un proyecto que generaba mucha ilusión. Ahora, sin embargo, llegan noticias agridulces.
Warner Bros. ha lanzado el primer teaser tráiler de Gremlins 3. En él, el bueno de Gizmo se asoma tímidamente desde dentro de una mochila. El pequeño personaje regresará otra vez a las andadas para volver a generar el caos. Sin embargo, este adorable primer vistazo a su retorno ha venido acompañado de una noticia bastante menos agradable para los fans que con tanto ansia esperan el título.
Y es que la compañía ha confirmado que Gremlins 3 retrasa su fecha de estreno hasta el 6 de octubre de 2028. Anteriormente estaba prevista para noviembre de 2027, por lo que el retraso es bastante importante, de prácticamente un año entero. Un inesperado revés que obliga a armarse de paciencia para poder disfrutar de la próxima aventura de estas alocadas criaturas demoníacas.
Qué sabemos de Gremlins 3
Por el momento, la sinopsis y el reparto de Gremlins 3 se mantienen en secreto. El filme fue anunciado originalmente en 2025, cuando se desveló además que el mismísimo Steven Spielberg será productor ejecutivo del proyecto. La guionista se está encargando de escribir la película basándose en una idea original del propio Chris Columbus junto a Zach Lipovsky y Adam B. Stein (Destino Final: Lazos de sangre).
La primera entrega de Gremlins, estrenada en 1984 y dirigida por Joe Dante, fue un éxito rotundo de taquilla. El filme recaudó 212 millones de dólares en todo el mundo pese a contar con un presupuesto de apenas 11 millones. Seis años después, en 1990 llegó la secuela, Gremlins 2, la nueva generación. Esta logró recaudar tan solo 41 millones de dólares, cifras muy por debajo de su predecesora. En cualquier caso, también se la considera un clásico.

articles.title: Ando wants to take on Slack with a team messaging app that lets humans and agents work together | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When Sara Du was helping companies build MCP servers in 2025, people kept asking her how they could use AI agents from within Slack itself. But there were a bunch of technical hurdles in the way: moving messages back and forth and getting agents the right context, all without burning through token budgets.
Upon digging into the problem, Du realized that there was a deeper issue that stemmed from how communication platforms were designed. “The deeper I went, the more I felt Slack and Teams were built for a world that was starting to pass us by,” Du told TechCrunch. “Agents were treated as apps you install even as they were becoming participants in the team.”
The solution, Du thought, could be a system that eliminates “meat proxies,” as Du calls the phenomenon of people having to relay AI agents’ work to their teams. “The human effectively becomes the messenger between the agent and the rest of the company,” she said.
An ideal system would instead let agents “participate in the shared conversations where work already gets coordinated,” Du said. “They should be able to understand why a decision was made, ask a colleague a question, build on another agent’s work, and bring in a human when judgment is needed.”
Her startup, Ando, on Thursday came out of stealth with an app that sets out to do exactly that: It’s a team messaging platform designed for both human and AI workers.
Ando bills itself as a full replacement for Slack or any other messaging platform that companies using AI agents might want for internal communication. The app gives agents their own identities and inboxes and lets them partake in conversations as naturally as people can.
The app has channels, DMs, group conversations, and even live calls that can be transcribed and viewed by an agent, Du said. Agents can browse channels, pick which ones to join, and can even join conversations without being tagged. If a company’s agent thinks a human worker needs to be notified of something, it can message them on its own rather than waiting for approvals.
To continue building the app, Ando on Thursday said it has raised $20 million in pre-seed and seed funding from investors including Accel, Index Ventures, and Emergence.
Du’s idea isn’t a new one. Most of the major players in the workplace collaboration space have already built in support for AI agents — Slack, for instance, has turned its native bot into an AI agent, and Microsoft has gone to great lengths to integrate Copilot into Teams in ways that connect to the rest of its Office 365 suite.
But there is still a market for apps to challenge the incumbents given how quickly AI is invading workplaces. Just a few months ago, Twitter and Block co-founder Jack Dorsey announced Buzz, which brings together people and AI agents into one messaging app, though it’s more targeted at developers.
Du also feels there’s still enough of an advantage in building an AI-agent-native team messaging platform as legacy incumbents try to figure out how to pivot their existing software.
Regardless, she seems to understand that Ando has an uphill battle ahead of it, and said that things were slow in the beginning. “A lot of people we showed it to early on were understandably unimpressed. It was, in many respects, just a jankier messaging platform. People would get stuck on that before they even got to what was different about the agents,” she explained.
But she said her team knew they were onto something when more and more customers started using Ando for longer periods. With Ando, she started to see that agents could do more than people expect: An agent could notice two conversations being held in different channels about the same problem, and without being asked to, could bring everyone together in a group chat, explain the context, and even suggest a decision.
“That was really delightful for me,” she said, “I felt agents could better manage people than humans can because they can process a lot more messages than a human can in a shorter span of time.”
She said Ando is currently working with customers in software, real estate, and finance across 15 countries, though many of the teams it serves right now are small. The fresh capital will be used to hire more people and burn through more tokens, she said.
“I think agents will let very small teams operate at a scale that previously required hundreds of people,” she said. “They can take on more of the execution, research, and coordination work, while humans spend more of their time on judgment, strategy, and deciding what should happen next.”

articles.title: Muse will apparently let you download its entire filesystem
articles.text:
A pair of developers say that with very little prompting, Meta’s Muse will share its entire filesystem with you. Peter James and Jonny L. Saunders have said they both independently coaxed Muse into zipping up and sharing the entire contents of its root filesystem, Ubuntu system files, app templates, and internal documentation. Saunders posted on Mastodon that it was “extremely easy” to replicate James’ results and that Muse had “Almost no prompt injection resistance.”
Muse will apparently let you download its entire filesystem
With a little coaxing, Meta’s AI will reveal all its secrets.
Meta denies that the incident represents a security breach. As noted in its announcement post, Meta’s Muse runs in persistent Linux virtual machines for each user. Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts said, “Just like with the laptop in front of you, of course you can see the files. Exporting virtual machine data doesn’t give people any privileged access to Meta infrastructure or to other people’s data.” Unlike with the average laptop, however, the data potentially reveals some interesting things about how Meta’s new AI platform functions.
This is the second Muse vulnerability disclosed this week, after security researcher Patrick Wardle discovered an exploit that would let attackers hijack the AI agent, redirect transcription processing, and access a user’s Muse account. Meta quickly issued a hotfix.
Both James and Saunders gained access to plain-text Markdown and JSON files describing in detail how Hatch (Meta’s internal name for Muse) processes requests, handles data, and connects to other services like Gmail. While it’s well documented that AI agents hallucinate and will provide false information about how they function, Saunders said that it is “generating hundreds of MB of accurate library code and compiled binaries” in a matter of seconds and that, “unless it synthesized a whole Ubuntu VM in less than a minute then I think this is a real dump.”
When I asked Muse to share its filesystem with me, it initially refused, saying it would be a security risk. When I shared links to evidence that it had created archives for others, it responded that it should not have done that and continued to say that it “can’t do a full / copy.” However, after starting a new session and prompting it with some flattery and curiosity, it created “safe” versions of /opt/hatch and /home/hatch for me, stripped of things like SSH keys. It also exposed its full directory tree to me and offered to “pull a safe copy” of “any specific subtree that looks interesting.” The resulting files seem to match what Saunders and James shared.
Roberts explained that while Meta isn’t seriously concerned about the leaks, “We’re continuing to make updates to the product, so users may see changes in how much information is available about their virtual machine.”
The developers’ dump potentially reveals a lot about Muse’s internal workings. For one, it stores its memory in plain Markdown files. It also performs a nightly “dream” review of recent conversations, which it then builds into guidance for future conversations, according to James. Saunders also found that many of Muse’s capabilities were hard-coded, including its ability to cancel subscriptions and “the machinery that manages runaway agent spawning.” Saunders speculates that many of the bash and Python scripts running Muse in the background were created using Claude, though that is unconfirmed.
James also found references to hardware integration called Meta Home Link, which appears to give Muse access to devices on a home network. Though Meta has not announced any feature by that name, and it’s not guaranteed that it will ship.

articles.title: Bentley dévoile le Torcal, son premier SUV électrique de 888 ch dérivé du Porsche Cayenne
articles.text:
La foudre s’est abattue à Crewe, au Royaume-Uni. Dans un communiqué publié ce 23 septembre 2026, Bentley vient de lever le voile sur sa toute première voiture électrique, baptisée Torcal. Ce SUV n’a pas été développé à partir d’une feuille blanche. Pour mémoire, la marque britannique fait partie du groupe Volkswagen et peut donc profiter des technologies de ce dernier.
Ainsi, le nouveau Torcal reprend la plateforme PPE (Premium Platform Electric) utilisée par le Porsche Cayenne Electric. Voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir sur ce cousin anglais qui mise tout sur le luxe.
Un style caricatural pour le Bentley Torcal
Fait amusant, avec ses 5 mètres de long, le Torcal est la plus courte des Bentley à quatre portes ! Mais par sa carrure musclée, le SUV électrique en impose davantage que le reste de la gamme du constructeur anglais. Mercedes peut d’ailleurs aller se rhabiller, Bentley est le nouveau roi de la calandre illuminée. Admirez plutôt ces 76 diamants à LED, posés à la main. Le lien de parenté avec le Porsche Cayenne se devine de trois quarts arrière, mais le design reste bien celui d’une Bentley.
À bord aussi, Bentley soigne le raffinement. Les yeux avisés remarqueront en revanche un certain détail identique au cousin technique allemand : l’écran tactile incurvé au centre. Pour le reste, Bentley fait dans l’exclusivité et cela donne un habitacle qui semble moins chargé. Le coffre est annoncé à 460 litres, plus 90 litres sous le capot avant, contre 781 litres pour le Cayenne. Bentley semble avoir sacrifié du volume de chargement au profit de l’espace pour les passagers arrière.
Le Torcal se distingue aussi par le son. Pour imiter le rythme d’un vrai V8 Bentley, le son moteur artificiel, baptisé Dynamic Symphony, a été enregistré avec de vrais instruments (batterie, alto, guitare basse). Ça, c’est le luxe. Enfin, Bentley ajoute un tissu 100 % laine mérinos, un placage fait de noyer et quatre portes qui s’ouvrent et se ferment électriquement.
Moins puissant que le Cayenne Turbo Electric
Sans surprise, l’ensemble mécanique du Cayenne se retrouve dans le plancher du Torcal : deux moteurs électriques pour une transmission intégrale et une large batterie de 113 kWh nets en 800 V. Dans sa version de base, le SUV britannique développe 821 chevaux et 1 194 Nm, pour un 0 à 100 km/h en 3,4 secondes et 250 km/h en pointe.
Dans la version S, le SUV monte à 888 ch et 1 350 Nm avec le launch control, de quoi expédier le 0 à 100 km/h en 2,9 secondes et atteindre 260 km/h. Si le Torcal reste moins puissant que le Cayenne (1 156 ch en version Turbo), c’est parce que «la plupart des clients trouvent qu’une accélération plus brutale que celle-ci est une expérience désagréable », souligne Bentley. Quelle que soit la version, l’autonomie atteint jusqu’à 600 km WLTP.
Suspension indépendamment active, roues arrière directrices et recharge de 10 à 80 % en 16 minutes à 400 kW, le Torcal reprend encore bon nombre d’éléments au SUV allemand.
Quel prix pour le Bentley Torcal ?
Bentley n’a encore donné ni le prix français ni la date de livraison en France. Au Royaume-Uni, le Torcal débute à 173 300 livres sterling (environ 200 000 €) et le Torcal S à 199 300 livres (environ 230 000 €). C’est environ 33 000 € de plus que le Cayenne Turbo Electric (167 200 € en France), et près de 40 000 € de plus que son compatriote, le tout nouveau Range Rover Electric, vendu 161 500 €.
